EDCS-00380662.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus ucto Hilarius Secutor et Resinia Syntrophen liberti patrono optimo faciendum curaverunt\n
EDCS-00380662.translation: To the Divine Shades. Vuctus Hilarius, the Secutor, and Resinia Syntrophen, freedmen, had this made for their excellent patron.
EDCS-00380662.summary: This is a funerary inscription by freedmen for their patron, likely dating to the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-00380667.summary: This is a short dedication or maker's inscription, possibly for a construction or a funerary monument.

EDCS-00380670.summary: This is a brief inscription, possibly a funerary epitaph or a good-luck wish, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-00380679.text_edition: \n Deo Apollini Gimius Rufinus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-00380679.translation: Rufinus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the god Apollo Gimius.
EDCS-00380679.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Apollo Gimius by Rufinus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-00380683.translation: To the Goddess Dirona. Adiutor and Iunianus willingly and deservedly fulfilled [their vow].
EDCS-00380683.summary: This is a votive inscription to the goddess Dirona by Adiutor and Iunianus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-00380685.summary: This inscription likely records the names of two individuals, possibly as builders or dedicants, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-03000637.summary: This inscription records a monetary transaction or value, likely related to goods or services, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-03000643.text_edition: \n arbitratu Flori filii in id opus XIIII HS\n
EDCS-03000643.translation: By the direction of Florus, his son, for this work 14 HS.
EDCS-03000643.summary: This inscription records the cost or allocation of funds (14 sesterces) for a specific work under the direction of Florus' son, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-03000645.translation: Publius Attius Servatus [dedicated this] to the Parcae [...
EDCS-03000645.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription potentially dedicating something to the Fates (Parcae) by Publius Attius Servatus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-03000646.text_edition: \n Callosiae Clamosae coniugi carissimae quae vixit annis XXVIIII et menses V dies numero XVIIII cui Flavius A vir perfectissimus praepositus vinorum coniux eius faciundum curavit\n
EDCS-03000646.translation: To Callosiae Clamosae, dearest wife, who lived 29 years, 5 months, and 19 days, Flavius A, a most accomplished man, prefect of the wines, her husband, had this made.
EDCS-03000646.summary: This is a funerary monument (epitaph) for Callosiae Clamosae, dedicated by her husband, Flavius A, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-03000648.translation: To Catu/linus, a man of highest rank.
EDCS-03000648.summary: This inscription is a dedication or honorific mention of Catu/linus, a person of senatorial or high equestrian rank, possibly from the imperial period.

EDCS-03000649.summary: This is likely a tombstone or memorial for Carpus, identified by his military rank as a standard-bearer ('signifer'), probably from the Roman army.

EDCS-03700618.summary: This inscription appears to relate to a legacy or inheritance concerning a person named Noni, possibly on a legal document or boundary marker.

EDCS-03700621.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription potentially naming individuals, possibly Lucius Julius Soi[---] and Julia Sacr[---], the context of which is lost.

EDCS-04900710.translation: To the god Mars Camulus, Verecundus, son of Fructus, gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-04900710.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the god Mars Camulus by Verecundus, son of Fructus, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-04900711.translation: Pyrame, farewell. Eutyche, farewell. Ierax, farewell. Olympe, farewell.
EDCS-04900711.summary: This inscription consists of multiple farewells to individuals named Pyrame, Eutyche, Ierax, and Olympe, possibly on a tomb or a personal item.

EDCS-04900715.text_edition: \n Deo Herculi ex voto Ialus D\n
EDCS-04900715.translation: To the god Hercules, according to a vow, Ialus D[...].
EDCS-04900715.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the god Hercules by Ialus D[---], fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-04900718.translation: Caratula, priestess of the Muses(?), Communis, to Hercules, 6000.
EDCS-04900718.summary: This inscription mentions Caratula, possibly a priestess, and Communis dedicating something (perhaps a sum of money, indicated by 6000) to Hercules.

EDCS-05000630.text_edition: \n Deo Marti Volmioni Lucius Acceptius Minusus ex voto T L \n
EDCS-05000630.translation: To the god Mars Volmonius, Lucius Acceptius Minusus fulfilled his vow, T L.
EDCS-05000630.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the god Mars Volmonius by Lucius Acceptius Minusus, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-05200506.summary: This is a very brief inscription, possibly an ownership mark or abbreviation, with no further context provided.

EDCS-05200508.translation: In honor of the divine house, Iulianus set this up to the Mother of the Gods.
EDCS-05200508.summary: This dedication to the Mother of the Gods was set up by Iulianus, likely during the imperial period given the reference to the 'divine house'.

EDCS-05200509.translation: Mercatorius Tertius willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-05200509.summary: This votive inscription records Mercatorius Tertius fulfilling a vow, likely dedicated to a deity, with the date inferable from the context of Roman votive practices.

EDCS-06100419.translation: Collyrium diapsoricum of Gaius Numisius Peregrinus. Collyrium euodes of Gaius Numisius Peregrinus.
EDCS-06100419.summary: This inscription lists two types of cosmetic preparations, 'diapsoricum' and 'euodes', made by Gaius Numisius Peregrinus, likely a merchant or producer, from the Roman period.

EDCS-06100420.translation: Of Titus Iulius Mercator, diasmyrn(es) after an attack.
EDCS-06100420.summary: This inscription refers to a product, 'diasmyrn(es)', belonging to Titus Iulius Mercator, possibly a medicine or cosmetic, with a context suggesting its use after an incident.

EDCS-06100421.translation: Of Titus Exquesus. Of Titus Exquesus. Crocodes of Titus Exquesus. Cro[---] / [---] / [---]
EDCS-06100421.summary: This fragmented inscription appears to list cosmetic or medicinal products ('Crocodes') associated with Titus Exquesus, likely a vendor or manufacturer from the Roman period.

EDCS-06100427.translation: To Iulia Pothi, daughter of Iulla.
EDCS-06100427.summary: This is a dedication to Iulia Pothi, daughter of Iulla, likely a funerary or honorific inscription.

EDCS-06100429.summary: This inscription identifies Optatus as the slave of Polla, likely a funerary or ownership marker.

EDCS-06100430.translation: Here lies Marianus, who lived about 38 years, whom his wife Dalmatia commends into the bosom of the saints.
EDCS-06100430.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Marianus at approximately 38 years of age and his wife Dalmatia's grief and hope for his afterlife, suggesting a Christian context.

EDCS-06100431.translation: To the god Cerunnicus Soltrius, Pruscus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-06100431.summary: This votive inscription records Pruscus fulfilling a vow to the god Cerunnicus Soltrius, likely from the Roman period with local deities.

EDCS-06100433.translation: From Marcus, son of Marcus, the Censor: dialibanum, lenimentum penicillum, stacton chelido-nium, melinum opobalsamatum.
EDCS-06100433.summary: This inscription lists items, likely perfumes or medicinal compounds, attributed to Marcus, son of Marcus, the Censor.

EDCS-06100438.text_edition: \n Leno Marti L L Marcus Mercatorius Creto votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-06100438.translation: Marcus Mercatorius of Crete, slave of Marcus, has paid his vow to Mars willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-06100438.summary: This inscription records a votive offering made to Mars by Marcus Mercatorius, a freedman, who fulfilled a vow.

EDCS-06100442.text_edition: \n Ptine pro Lysipemine <f=E>ilio votum solvit libens merito \n
EDCS-06100442.translation: Ptine has paid her vow to Lysipemine willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-06100442.summary: This inscription records a votive offering made by Ptine to Lysipemine.

EDCS-07600315.translation: To the departed spirits: Masclinus Victorinus.
EDCS-07600315.summary: This is a tombstone inscription dedicated to the memory of Masclinus Victorinus.

EDCS-07600316.translation: To the departed spirits: Caupius Virilis and his wife Silvi(a).
EDCS-07600316.summary: This is a tombstone inscription dedicated to Caupius Virilis and his wife Silvi(a).

EDCS-08300465.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Marti et Ancamnae Caius Serotinius Iustus ex voto posuit\n
EDCS-08300465.translation: In honor of the divine house, Caius Serotinius Iustus dedicated this to Mars and Ancamna, in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-08300465.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the gods Mars and Ancamna, made by Caius Serotinius Iustus in honor of the imperial family.

EDCS-08300466.text_edition: \n Novellum piper pondo VIII nummum sestertium XX\n
EDCS-08300466.translation: Novellum, 8 pounds of pepper, for 20 sesterces.
EDCS-08300466.summary: This inscription appears to be a record of a sale or transaction for pepper.

EDCS-08400390.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely part of a funerary or dedicatory text, mentioning Gallus and Pri.

EDCS-08400391.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Luci Valeri Secundi patris et Valeri Vitalis filii et Valeri Secundi filii et Valeriae Luciferae filiae Dis Manibus Luci Valeri Callisti\n
EDCS-08400391.translation: To the departed spirits: of Lucius Valerius Secundus, the father, and Valerius Vitalis, the son, and Lucius Valerius Secundus, the son, and Valeria Lucifera, the daughter. To the departed spirits: of Lucius Valerius Callistus.
EDCS-08400391.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating multiple members of the Valerius family.

EDCS-08500478.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Belatullus Cossi Marullina Bellos Belatulli\n
EDCS-08500478.translation: To the departed spirits: Belatullus, son of Cossus Marullinus, and Bellos, son of Belatullus.
EDCS-08500478.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Belatullus and Bellos, indicating a family relationship.

EDCS-08500479.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Augusto Taciti filio Gauvae Sexti coniugibus\n
EDCS-08500479.translation: To the spirits of the departed, to Augustus, son of Tacitus, and to his wives Gauva and Sextus.
EDCS-08500479.summary: This funerary inscription honors Augustus, son of Tacitus, and his wives Gauva and Sextus.

EDCS-08500482.text_edition: \n Silvano sacrum et Nymphis loci Arete Druis antistita somnio monita dedit\n
EDCS-08500482.translation: Arete, priestess of the place, dedicated this to Silvanus and the Nymphs of the place, having been warned by a dream.
EDCS-08500482.summary: This dedication to Silvanus and the Nymphs was made by Arete, a priestess, who was guided by a dream.

EDCS-08500483.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Genialio Iullino Iulliniuss sic Exuperator sic\n
EDCS-08500483.translation: To the spirits of the departed, to Genialis, son of Iullinus; Iullinius says so; Exuperator says so.
EDCS-08500483.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Genialis, son of Iullinus, with attestations from Iullinius and Exuperator.

EDCS-08500486.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Reginus, son of Cintugnatos.
EDCS-08500486.summary: A funerary inscription honoring Reginus, son of Cintugnatos.

EDCS-08500494.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deo Cretoni et Genio pagi AC Publius Capitonius ad excolendam memoriam Capitoni patroni proscaenium\n
EDCS-08500494.translation: In honor of the divine house, Publius Capitonius, for the cultivation of the memory of his patron Capito, dedicated the stage-front to the god Creton and the Genius of the district.
EDCS-08500494.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a proscenium (stage-front) by Publius Capitonius to the god Creton and the Genius of the district, honoring the imperial family and his patron Capito.

EDCS-08600538.text_edition: \n Deo Herculi Magiso votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-08600538.translation: Freely and deservedly paid the vow to the god Magisan Hercules.
EDCS-08600538.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow to the god Magisan Hercules.

EDCS-08600798.translation: To Verecundus, son of Rufus, a citizen of the Viromandui. Iulia Admericca and Nericcius Fronto, his heirs, erected this.
EDCS-08600798.summary: This funerary inscription was erected by the heirs Iulia Admericca and Nericcius Fronto for Verecundus, son of Rufus, a Viromanduan citizen.

EDCS-08600799.translation: To Gnaeus Pollienus... his... [perhaps a relative or friend]...
EDCS-08600799.summary: This is a fragmented inscription, likely funerary or dedicatory, honoring Gnaeus Pollienus.

EDCS-08900489.translation: To the god Hercules. Verus [son of ?]inius, in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-08900489.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to the god Hercules made by Verus, son of ?inius.

EDCS-09001534.translation: To the gods, the shades. Gelos made this for his most beloved daughter, Satria, who lived 18 years, 10 months, and 4 days. Consida NVVLTAB.
EDCS-09001534.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Satria, set up by her father Gelos, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09001535.translation: Here rests in peace, of holy and good memory, Aviulfus, who lived 20 years, 4 months, and 6 days.
EDCS-09001535.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aviulfus, stating his lifespan and place of rest, likely from the Late Roman or Early Christian period.

EDCS-09001537.translation: Vegetinus's diamond for toughness. Vegetinus. Vegetinus. Noni's hedgehog for its disease.
EDCS-09001537.summary: This inscription appears to be a collection of curious phrases or possible remedies, potentially related to medical or amuletic contexts, with several mentions of 'Vegetinus'.

EDCS-09200373.translation: [Serving in all] civil offices and honors, along with the priesthood, [Tiberius Avitus Genialis, son of Sulpicius Avitus].
EDCS-09200373.summary: This is a fragmented inscription honoring Tiberius Avitus Genialis for his public service and priestly duties, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09200375.summary: This inscription consists of two personal names, possibly indicating ownership or dedication, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09200376.summary: This is a personal name, Sextus Caupius Secundus, likely an owner or dedicator, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09200377.summary: This inscription indicates a location associated with the Teucorians, likely a settlement or territory marker from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09200380.summary: This inscription marks a place associated with Marcus Vi(), possibly indicating ownership or a boundary, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09200381.summary: This inscription consists of a personal name, Gaius Totius, likely an owner or dedicator, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09200383.summary: This inscription contains multiple personal names and indicates a place associated with Tachi(ti?), likely related to land ownership or settlement from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09200384.translation: Vitalis, of the voting tribe Quirina, from the Sasso region?
EDCS-09200384.summary: This inscription likely records personal names, possibly related to tribal affiliation and origin, for an unknown purpose.

EDCS-09200385.translation: Tertius, son of As[...]; Gaius Tertius.
EDCS-09200385.summary: This inscription appears to list personal names, possibly indicating a father and son or two individuals named Tertius.

EDCS-09300410.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus et memoriae Prisci Marciani Prisci Marciani liberti Priscita Calliope coniunx viva paravit\n
EDCS-09300410.translation: To the divine shades and the memory of Priscus Marcianus. Priscita Calliope, his wife, while alive, prepared this.
EDCS-09300410.summary: This is a funerary dedication set up by a wife for her deceased husband, Priscus Marcianus.

EDCS-09300411.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus et memoriae Cintusminae Magioni filiae Caius Reginius December sibi et coniugi defunctae vivus posuit\n
EDCS-09300411.translation: To the divine shades and the memory of Cintusmina, daughter of Magio. Gaius Reginius December, while alive, placed this for himself and his deceased wife.
EDCS-09300411.summary: This is a funerary dedication set up by a husband for himself and his deceased wife, honoring his wife Cintusmina.

EDCS-09300412.summary: This damaged inscription mentions Censorinus and indicates that someone placed this monument, likely funerary.

EDCS-09300413.summary: This inscription records the name Mulsinus Silvinus and a payment of 10 asses, possibly related to a purchase or service.

EDCS-09300415.translation: To the divine shades of Caranta, daughter of Conteddi.
EDCS-09300415.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Caranta, daughter of Conteddi.

EDCS-09300416.summary: This fragmentary inscription mentions a wife, likely within a funerary context.

EDCS-09300421.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription that appears to contain personal names, possibly related to a funerary monument.

EDCS-09300422.translation: To Hercules. Maternus fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-09300422.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the god Hercules by Maternus.

EDCS-09300423.translation: To the god Hercules, Silvester, son of Saturninus, paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-09300423.summary: This is a votive dedication to the god Hercules, made by Silvester.

EDCS-09300424.translation: Taluppa [paid] his vow for the health of Tatu[---], son of [---].
EDCS-09300424.summary: This inscription records a votive offering made by Taluppa for the health of his son, Tatu[---].

EDCS-09300426.translation: [---], son of Banus, paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-09300426.summary: This is a votive inscription made by an unnamed individual, son of Banus.

EDCS-09300427.text_edition: \n Minervae Lucius Calvisius Dignatus Aviti? fil(ius) votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-09300427.translation: To Minerva, Lucius Calvisius Dignatus, son of Avitus(?), paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-09300427.summary: This is a votive dedication to Minerva by Lucius Calvisius Dignatus.

EDCS-09300428.translation: To the departed spirits: Sumaronia Tasgilla, wife, and Veranius Verinus and Verania [---], and Aestivus Verianus, a veteran, [erected this].
EDCS-09300428.summary: This is a funerary monument set up for Aestivus Verianus and other deceased individuals by his wife and son.

EDCS-09300429.translation: To Lautinius Mandatus, deceased, and to Poppilia, his wife, [he] set [this up] while alive.
EDCS-09300429.summary: This inscription records a tombstone set up by a living person for Lautinius Mandatus and his deceased wife Poppilia.

EDCS-09300430.translation: To the departed spirits: Actianus Curmillianus, son of Curmillus, himself for himself and for Gloria, daughter of Catissus, his deceased wife, set [this] up while alive.
EDCS-09300430.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Actianus Curmillianus for himself and his deceased wife Gloria.

EDCS-09300431.translation: To [---]iola, daughter of Silvicus, Sacurius [---]s, his wife, and Sacer, his son, erected [this] while alive.
EDCS-09300431.summary: This inscription records a tombstone erected by Sacurius and his son Sacer for Sacurius' wife and daughter.

EDCS-09300432.translation: [... for] Marcus Maturicius Maternus and Marcianus(?) [...], and Mariana Mari[---] with the deceased.
EDCS-09300432.summary: This inscription appears to be part of a funerary monument commemorating Marcus Maturicius Maternus and other deceased individuals.

EDCS-09300433.translation: [... and] for Carilla, daughter of Decman, his wife, Marcus, [her] son, [arranged for this to be placed].
EDCS-09300433.summary: This inscription records that Marcus, son of Carilla, arranged for a monument to be placed for his mother.

EDCS-09300434.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Gaius Agisillius Caratus.
EDCS-09300434.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication to the underworld gods for Gaius Agisillius Caratus.

EDCS-09300436.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Publio Silvio Gento et Venustiae Marti coniugi Silvius Genti filius posuit\n
EDCS-09300436.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Silvius Genti, son of Genti, set up this monument for Publius Silvius Gentus and his wife Venustia Martia.
EDCS-09300436.summary: This funerary inscription records the erection of a monument by Silvius Genti for his parents, Publius Silvius Gentus and Venustia Martia.

EDCS-09300437.translation: To Caratullius Cintussus, son of Cintussus, a merchant in the oyster trade; his heir took care to place this.
EDCS-09300437.summary: This funerary inscription records the placement of a monument by the heir of Caratullius Cintussus, a merchant.

EDCS-09300438.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Marcus Matorius Maius and his wife Augusta.
EDCS-09300438.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication to the underworld gods for Marcus Matorius Maius and his wife Augusta.

EDCS-09400560.text_edition: \n Deae Nehalaenniae sic Exomnius Isaurici filius aram posuit ex iussu\n
EDCS-09400560.translation: To the goddess Nehalaennia, thus Exomnius, son of Isauricus, set up an altar by command.
EDCS-09400560.summary: This votive inscription records Exomnius, son of Isauricus, setting up an altar to the goddess Nehalaennia by command.

EDCS-09400561.text_edition: \n Deae Nehalenniae Titus Tertinius Virilis pro se et suis votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-09400561.translation: To the goddess Nehalaennia, Titus Tertinius Virilis fulfilled his vow for himself and his family, gladly and deservedly.
EDCS-09400561.summary: This votive inscription records Titus Tertinius Virilis fulfilling a vow to the goddess Nehalaennia for his family.

EDCS-09400562.text_edition: \n Deae Nehalaenniae sic Neuto Lucani filius votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-09400562.translation: To the goddess Nehalaennia, thus Neuto, son of Lucanus, fulfilled his vow, gladly and deservedly.
EDCS-09400562.summary: This votive inscription records Neuto, son of Lucanus, fulfilling a vow to the goddess Nehalaennia.

EDCS-09400563.text_edition: \n Deae Nehalenniae Titus Tagadunius Adiutor votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-09400563.translation: To the goddess Nehalaennia, Titus Tagadunius Adiutor fulfilled his vow, gladly and deservedly.
EDCS-09400563.summary: This votive inscription records Titus Tagadunius Adiutor fulfilling a vow to the goddess Nehalaennia.

EDCS-09400564.text_edition: \n Deae Nehalaenniae sic aram quam Quintus Phoebius Hilarus decurio municipii Batavorum ob merces suas bene conservatas voverat posuit libens merito Albino et Maximo consulibus\n
EDCS-09400564.translation: To the goddess Nehalaennia, thus he set up the altar which Quintus Phoebius Hilarus, decurion of the municipality of the Batavians, had vowed for his own successful ventures, gladly and deservedly, under the consulship of Albinus and Maximus.
EDCS-09400564.summary: This votive inscription records Quintus Phoebius Hilarus, a decurion, setting up an altar to the goddess Nehalaennia for successful ventures during the consulship of Albinus and Maximus.

EDCS-09400565.text_edition: \n Deae Nehalaenniae sic pro mercibus conservandis Caius Crescentius Florus ex iussu monumentum posuit? \n
EDCS-09400565.translation: To the goddess Nehalaennia, thus Gaius Crescentius Florus, by command, set up this monument for the preservation of his merchandise?
EDCS-09400565.summary: This votive inscription records Gaius Crescentius Florus setting up a monument to the goddess Nehalaennia, possibly by command, for the preservation of his merchandise.

EDCS-09400566.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deae Nehalenniae Caius Maximinius Rusticus et Titus Iulius Tacitus votum solverunt libentes merito\n
EDCS-09400566.translation: In honor of the divine house, to the goddess Nehalennia, Gaius Maximinius Rusticus and Titus Iulius Tacitus gladly fulfilled their vow as was deserved.
EDCS-09400566.summary: This inscription records two individuals, Caius Maximinius Rusticus and Titus Iulius Tacitus, fulfilling a vow to the goddess Nehalennia in honor of the imperial family.

EDCS-09400567.text_edition: \n Deae Nehalenniae Caius Senius Secundus pro se et suis votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-09400567.translation: To the goddess Nehalennia, Gaius Senius Secundus for himself and his family gladly fulfilled his vow as was deserved.
EDCS-09400567.summary: This inscription records Gaius Senius Secundus fulfilling a vow to the goddess Nehalennia for himself and his family.

EDCS-09400568.text_edition: \n Deae Nehallenniae Commodus Ufentis filius votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-09400568.translation: To the goddess Nehalennia, Commodus, son of Ufentis, gladly fulfilled his vow as was deserved.
EDCS-09400568.summary: This inscription records Commodus, son of Ufentis, fulfilling a vow to the goddess Nehalennia.

EDCS-09400569.text_edition: \n Deae Nehalenniae Placidus Viduci filius cives sic Veliocassinius negotiator nnicianus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-09400569.translation: To the goddess Nehalennia, Placidus, son of Viducius, a citizen and merchant from Veliocassinius, gladly fulfilled his vow as was deserved.
EDCS-09400569.summary: This inscription records Placidus, son of Viducius, a merchant, fulfilling a vow to the goddess Nehalennia.

EDCS-09400570.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deae Nehalenniae Caius Iulius Aprilis veteranus ex beneficiario consularis pro se et suis votum solvit libens merito Maximo et Aeliano consulibus\n
EDCS-09400570.translation: In honor of the divine house, to the goddess Nehalennia, Gaius Iulius Aprilis, a veteran formerly a deputy of the consular governor, for himself and his family gladly fulfilled his vow as was deserved, when Maximo and Aelianus were consuls.
EDCS-09400570.summary: This inscription records a veteran, Gaius Iulius Aprilis, fulfilling a vow to the goddess Nehalennia during the consulship of Maximo and Aelianus, honoring the imperial family.

EDCS-09400571.text_edition: \n Immunii Primus et Ibliomarus Treveri votum solverunt libentes merito\n
EDCS-09400571.translation: Immunius and Ibliomarus of the Treveri gladly fulfilled their vow as was deserved.
EDCS-09400571.summary: This inscription records two individuals, Immunius and Ibliomarus, both from the Treveri tribe, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-09400572.translation: To the goddess Nehalennia, Marcus Iustinius [made an offering].
EDCS-09400572.summary: This incomplete inscription records Marcus Iustinius making an offering to the goddess Nehalennia.

EDCS-09400573.text_edition: \n Deae Nehalenniae pro navibus Mercatorius Amabilis votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-09400573.translation: To the goddess Nehalennia, for the ships, Mercatorius Amabilis gladly fulfilled his vow as was deserved.
EDCS-09400573.summary: This inscription records Mercatorius Amabilis fulfilling a vow to the goddess Nehalennia, specifically for the protection of ships.

EDCS-10600003.inscription_type: tituli honorarii, tituli operum, tituli sacri
EDCS-10600003.translation: Emperor Caesar Flavius Constantinus, the greatest Augustus, eternal, son of the divine Augustus Pius, forever to be celebrated throughout the world for his victories, bestowed upon his city of the Remi, as a sign of his customary generosity, the baths, begun and completed at the expense of his treasury.
EDCS-10600003.summary: This inscription records Emperor Constantine the Great dedicating baths he funded to the civitas of the Remi, likely in the early 4th century CE.

EDCS-10600004.translation: Felix militiae took up his devoted vows, Jovinus advanced to the height of his virtues, and twice appointed master of cavalry and infantry for his merits, extended his eternal name through the ages. But this great praise was surpassed by his serious piety, and he dedicated his remarkable triumphs to religion, so that he might overcome with his deeds the honor that fame had given him and hope for eternal life through his actions. Conscious of the holy life-giving fount, the measurer joyfully adorns a lasting dwelling for his mortal limbs, providing for the salvation of his body and the restoration of his limbs to life. Almighty Christ, the venerable and awesome judge, the faithful hope of the devout suppliants, the noble one, rewards his servants not for their deeds but because faith and piety outweigh justice.
EDCS-10600004.summary: This complex funerary poem celebrates a deceased individual named Jovinus, praising his military achievements and piety, and ultimately attributing his salvation to Christ, likely dating to the 4th century CE.

EDCS-10600128.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Placida.
EDCS-10600128.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Placida.

EDCS-10600129.translation: To the spirits of the departed and to the memory of Primitivus, son of Vitalis, his most excellent husband Caius Curtius Macribalata dedicated and gifted this to his deserving wife.
EDCS-10600129.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated by a husband to his deceased wife, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10600130.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Saturnina, mother, placed [this] for Primulus.
EDCS-10600130.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a mother for her deceased son, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10600131.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Of Primus.
EDCS-10600131.summary: A fragmentary funerary epitaph that likely records the name of the deceased, Primus.

EDCS-10600132.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Primus.
EDCS-10600132.summary: A funerary epitaph that records the name of the deceased, Primus.

EDCS-10600133.translation: To the spirits of the departed and to the memory of Proclus, son of Camius, and of Procla, his daughter.
EDCS-10600133.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated to Proclus and his daughter Procla, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10600134.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Pupilla.
EDCS-10600134.summary: A funerary epitaph that records the name of the deceased, Pupilla.

EDCS-10600135.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Regalis.
EDCS-10600135.summary: A funerary epitaph that records the name of the deceased, Regalis.

EDCS-10600137.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Rio[---]ae.
EDCS-10600137.summary: A fragmentary funerary epitaph mentioning a female name, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10600138.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Sacrill(a).
EDCS-10600138.summary: A funerary epitaph mentioning the name Sacrilla, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10600140.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Salutar(i)s, the son.
EDCS-10600140.summary: A fragmentary funerary epitaph commemorating a son named Salutaris, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10600141.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Sammius Peculiaris.
EDCS-10600141.summary: A funerary dedication for Sammius Peculiaris.

EDCS-10600142.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Satta.

EDCS-10600143.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Saturnina.

EDCS-10600145.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Saturnina, daughter of Albinus.
EDCS-10600145.summary: A funerary dedication for Saturnina, daughter of Albinus.

EDCS-10600146.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Saturninus.

EDCS-10600147.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Saturninus and Dotilla.
EDCS-10600147.summary: A funerary dedication for Saturninus and Dotilla.

EDCS-10600148.translation: To the spirits of the departed and to the memory. Saturninus, son of Sattonius.
EDCS-10600148.summary: A funerary dedication for Saturninus, son of Sattonius.

EDCS-10600149.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Secunda.

EDCS-10600150.summary: A tombstone recording the name Secunda twice, possibly for emphasis or indicating a dual burial.

EDCS-10600151.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Secundus Burdo.
EDCS-10600151.summary: A funerary dedication for Secundus Burdo.

EDCS-10600152.translation: To the spirits of the departed and to the memory of Secundus and Veneria, his daughter, who lived [3] years. Her father(?) [3]X[.
EDCS-10600152.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Secundus and his daughter Veneria, likely from the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-10600153.translation: To the spirits of the departed and to the memory of Senator. His dearest wife Vitalina erected this monument for him; he lived 72 years.
EDCS-10600153.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Vitalina to her husband Senator, who lived 72 years, likely from the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-10600154.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Senniola Bellicca.
EDCS-10600154.summary: This is a simple funerary dedication to Senniola Bellicca, likely from the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-10600155.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Sepp(a) and Ne[---]. Victor[---]?
EDCS-10600155.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription possibly for Seppa and another person named Ne[---], with Victor[---] perhaps being the dedicator, likely from the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-10600156.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Serotinus. His mother Gavva.
EDCS-10600156.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Gavva to her son Serotinus, likely from the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-10600157.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Silvanus.
EDCS-10600157.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Silvanus, likely from the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-10600158.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Sinccus, son of Iucundus(?).
EDCS-10600158.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sinccus, identified as the son of Iucundus, likely from the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-10600160.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Suc[---].
EDCS-10600160.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription beginning with 'Suc[---]', likely from the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-10600161.summary: This is a dedication or commission by Sueoninus, likely for a funerary monument, possibly from the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-10600162.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription possibly naming individuals related to Sulpicius Restutus and Crescentis, likely from the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-10600164.summary: This inscription, likely from a tombstone, records that Tarsica prepared this monument for a relative while she was alive.

EDCS-10600166.translation: To the Divine Manes. For Verecundus (?).
EDCS-10600166.summary: This is a dedication to the Divine Manes, likely for a person named Verecundus, possibly a tombstone inscription.

EDCS-10600167.translation: To the Divine Manes. Iaecca, mother, prepared (this) while alive for her children [3]rio and Victorina.
EDCS-10600167.summary: This funerary inscription records that Iaecca, a mother, prepared this monument while alive for her children.

EDCS-10600169.summary: This brief inscription is a dedication to the Divine Manes for Victorina, likely a tombstone.

EDCS-10600170.translation: To the Divine Manes. For Felicionius (?) and his wife, and for their daughters Victorina and Tertia.
EDCS-10600170.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to the Divine Manes and commemorates Felicionius (?), his wife, and their daughters Victorina and Tertia.

EDCS-10600176.summary: This inscription records a memorial set up for someone named Amica, likely a tombstone or memorial marker.

EDCS-10600184.summary: This inscription fragment records a memorial for Lucrio (?), possibly from a tombstone.

EDCS-10600186.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Divine Manes, likely for a person named Valerius, possibly a tombstone.

EDCS-10600206.summary: This inscription is too fragmentary to determine its purpose or content.

EDCS-10600209.translation: To the god Jupiter Mapas, Sollius, his son, fulfilled his vow deservedly.
EDCS-10600209.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Jupiter Mapas by Sollius, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-10600210.summary: This is a tombstone marking the burial place of a woman named Florena, from an unspecified date.

EDCS-10600211.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying Censorinus as a citizen of Remi, likely from a tombstone or public monument.

EDCS-10600212.translation: May Ursicina live in God, having died at the age of 25. I will sleep in peace and rest.
EDCS-10600212.summary: This is a tombstone for Ursicina, who died at 25, likely from the early Christian period, expressing hope for peace in the afterlife.

EDCS-10600214.translation: Lucius Magius Secundus dedicated the stage area as a gift from his own resources to the divine Augustus, the god Apollo, and the district of Vennecti.
EDCS-10600214.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a stage area by Lucius Magius Secundus to Apollo and the Augustan divinity, for the district of Vennecti, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10600216.translation: To the god Mercurius, Attaedius son of Lituccus fulfills his vow, willingly and deservedly, having undertaken it.
EDCS-10600216.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the god Mercurius by Attaedius, son of Lituccus, who fulfilled a vow, likely dating from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10600217.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Reginus, son and heir, made this from his own resources for Senecionis, son of Messicus, and his relatives.
EDCS-10600217.summary: This is a tombstone inscription where Reginus erected a monument for his father Senecionis and other family members, from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10600218.translation: His wife had this made for Divixtilla, an excellent woman, daughter of Macrinus, perhaps a legate.
EDCS-10600218.summary: This funerary inscription states that the wife of Divixtilla, daughter of Macrinus (possibly a legate), had the monument made for her, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10600220.translation: Matrona made this for Decimus Giamillius Tagius and Vaccia, wife of Tagius, and her children.
EDCS-10600220.summary: This inscription records that Matrona commissioned a monument for her husband Decimus Giamillius Tagius, her wife Vaccia, and their children, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10600221.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Furius Antoninus, a circitor of the Dalmatian regiment, lived 28 years, 15 days, 3 hours. His college erected a memorial to him at a cost of 5,030 denarii.
EDCS-10600221.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Furius Antoninus, a soldier in the Dalmatian regiment, detailing his lifespan and the cost of his memorial erected by his colleagues, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10600222.translation: Platanus, a cavalryman in the Dalmatian unit, lived 11 years. He paid for the expense from his own resources, 338 denarii.
EDCS-10600222.summary: This tombstone records the life of Platanus, a cavalryman in the Dalmatian unit, who lived 11 years and paid for his burial expenses, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10600223.translation: To the goddess Diana. Licinius, son of [---], willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow by dedicating [a statue?].
EDCS-10600223.summary: A funerary or votive inscription dedicated to Diana, likely by a person named Licinius who fulfilled a vow.

EDCS-10600225.translation: To Isis, Myrionyma, and Serapis. Expectatus, steward of Augustus, son of Hermes, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10600225.summary: A votive inscription dedicated to Isis, Myrionyma, and Serapis by Expectatus, a steward of Augustus.

EDCS-10600227.translation: He lies here, [---]us, son of Seccius, an Arvernian, a cavalryman of the Vocontian ala, aged 25, after 7 years of service.
EDCS-10600227.summary: A tombstone for a Roman cavalry soldier of the Vocontian ala, who died after 7 years of service.

EDCS-10600233.summary: A fragmentary inscription indicating that Gabilius restored something.

EDCS-10600239.summary: A tombstone recording the name and age at death of Baudiricus.

EDCS-10600241.summary: A very brief and possibly informal inscription mentioning Ibetius and Andecarus, possibly in a context of drinking or a shared meal.

EDCS-10600243.translation: [---]ius Tiberinus and [---] Ulpius Paullinus, curators of the same, took care that the monument be erected.
EDCS-10600243.summary: An inscription recording the erection of a monument by two curators, identified as Tiberinus and Ulpius Paullinus.

EDCS-10600244.translation: Vibius Atticus, the father, placed [this] in memory of Atticus.
EDCS-10600244.summary: A funerary monument set up by Vibius Atticus in memory of his son, also named Atticus.

EDCS-10600245.translation: To the departed spirits. Lucius Censorinus.
EDCS-10600245.summary: A short funerary inscription dedicating the monument to the shades of the departed on behalf of Lucius Censorinus.

EDCS-10600246.summary: A very fragmentary inscription with initials and a name, likely of a votive or funerary nature.

EDCS-10600253.translation: Leuboricus rests here in peace, having lived for 8 years.
EDCS-10600253.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a child named Leuboricus, likely from the late Roman or post-Roman period.

EDCS-10600254.translation: In Christ rests Radogisilus the faithful.
EDCS-10600254.summary: This is an early Christian funerary inscription for a faithful individual named Radogisilus.

EDCS-10600255.translation: For the health and victory of the Emperor, Setubogius, son of Esuggius, dedicated two tribunalia to Apollo and Veriogodumnus from his own funds.
EDCS-10600255.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Apollo and Veriogodumnus for the emperor's well-being by Setubogius, son of Esuggius, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10600256.translation: Saturninus, son of Seccus, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Gesacus Augustus.
EDCS-10600256.summary: This is a votive inscription where Saturninus, son of Seccus, fulfilled a vow to Gesacus Augustus, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10600257.translation: Lucius Romanius Priscus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the god Mercury.
EDCS-10600257.summary: This is a votive inscription where Lucius Romanius Priscus fulfilled a vow to the god Mercury, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10600258.summary: This is a dedication or memorial inscription for Titus Messius, associated with Samarobriva, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10600260.translation: To the spirits of the departed and for the memory of Ianuarius, standard-bearer of the numerically named Ursensian cohort, a citizen of the Sequani, who lived 29 years(?); Severianus his brother erected this memorial.
EDCS-10600260.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Ianuarius, a standard-bearer from the Ursensian cohort, erected by his brother Severianus, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10600261.translation: Valerius Durio, circitor of the numerically named cataphractarii, lived 30 years.
EDCS-10600261.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Valerius Durio, a circitor of the cataphractarii, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10600262.translation: To the spirits of the departed and for the memory of Valerius Iustus, equestrian, who lived 31 years; the cohort of provincials established this.
EDCS-10600262.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Valerius Iustus, an equestrian, sponsored by the cohort of provincials, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10600263.translation: To the spirits of the departed and for the memory of Valerius Zurdigix, decurion of...
EDCS-10600263.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Valerius Zurdigix, a decurion, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10600266.translation: In the consulship of... concerning the goods of Caius Iulius... it was agreed that they should give... on the 7th day before the Kalends of September. Concerning the monument of Caius Iulius... they granted.
EDCS-10600266.summary: This inscription concerns a grant related to the monument of Caius Iulius, likely made in the consular year indicated, granting use of his property or funds to VIIVII.

EDCS-10600268.translation: To the departed gods and to the memory of Flamin(ius) Acurio, who lived 60 years.
EDCS-10600268.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Flamin(ius) Acurio, recording his name and age at death, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10600269.translation: To the departed gods and to the memory of Maccius Lucilius Publius Rufus, Firmus Ateste placed [this] for a friend who deserved well of him, aged 8 years.
EDCS-10600269.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Firmus Ateste for his friend Maccius Lucilius Publius Rufus, recording the deceased's name, the dedicator, and his age at death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10600270.translation: To the departed gods and to the memory of Modesta, daughter of Modestus, who lived 18 years and 32 days.
EDCS-10600270.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Modesta, daughter of Modestus, recording her name, parentage, and age at death, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10600271.translation: Marcus Popillius Sodalis, son of Medeticca, daughter of Senicatus.
EDCS-10600271.summary: This inscription records the names and parentage of Marcus Popillius Sodalis and Medeticca Senicati, possibly a dedication or family record.

EDCS-10600272.translation: Vittata, daughter of Victorinus, lived 9 years.
EDCS-10600272.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Vittata, daughter of Victorinus, recording her name, parentage, and age at death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10600275.translation: In the name of Christ, Adalhildis rests here in peace, lived 26 years. She died on the 15th day of April.
EDCS-10600275.summary: This is an early Christian funerary epitaph for Adalhildis, recording her name, age at death, and date of death, likely from the post-Roman period.

EDCS-10600276.translation: Ansebertus rests here in peace, lived 30 years. He died.
EDCS-10600276.summary: This is an early Christian funerary epitaph for Ansebertus, recording his name, age at death, and date of death, likely from the post-Roman period.

EDCS-10600277.translation: Aus trechildis rests here in peace, lived 31 years. She died in the manner of February, the 3rd day.
EDCS-10600277.summary: This is an early Christian funerary epitaph for Austrechildis, recording her name, age at death, and date of death, likely from the post-Roman period.

EDCS-10600278.translation: Bellosa will carry [her child?] for three years.
EDCS-10600278.summary: This inscription, possibly a curse or a prophecy, mentions Bellosa and the duration of three years, the context of which is unclear.

EDCS-10600279.translation: Belsoaldus rests here in peace. He lived [3] years. Maritius made [this] on the third day; pray for us.
EDCS-10600279.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Belsoaldus, likely from the early medieval period, with a statement of his lifespan and a maker's name.

EDCS-10600280.translation: Duviadius lived in God, faithful, for 14 years, 8 months, 1 day. He made the inscription.
EDCS-10600280.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Duviadius, likely from the early medieval period, stating his age at death and that he created the inscription.

EDCS-10600281.translation: Egrebaldus rests here in peace. He lived 41 years. He died. No(vember) 15th. He made [this].
EDCS-10600281.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Egrebaldus, likely from the early medieval period, stating his age at death and the date of his passing.

EDCS-10600282.summary: This is a funerary or dedication inscription for Floreda, identified as a 'sanctimonialis' (holy woman or nun).

EDCS-10600283.translation: Hildulf, aged 3 years, rests here in peace. Pray for us.
EDCS-10600283.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Hildulf, a child aged 3, likely from the early medieval period.

EDCS-10600284.translation: Leudelinus rests here in peace. He lived 50 years. He died. Genarius made [this] on the 15th day. // Valdolina rests here in peace. She lived 30 years. She died. Julius made [this] on the 23rd day.
EDCS-10600284.summary: This inscription records the deaths of two individuals, Leudelinus (aged 50) and Valdolina (aged 30), likely from the early medieval period.

EDCS-10600285.summary: This is a dedication inscription, possibly funerary, for Nonnite, dedicated by a spouse.

EDCS-10600286.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Patroina, stating her age at death.

EDCS-10600287.translation: Riginus, who went before in peace.
EDCS-10600287.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Riginus, indicating he has died and is 'in peace'.

EDCS-10600288.translation: Thoribius rests here in peace. // Faustinianus rests here in peace. He lived 50 (?) years. May peace be with you.
EDCS-10600288.summary: This inscription records two individuals, Thoribius and Faustinianus, resting 'in peace', with an approximate lifespan given for Faustinianus.

EDCS-10600289.translation: To Mars, lord, may you live. Nasola(?) and his wife Livil(la?) made this.
EDCS-10600289.summary: This is a dedication to the god Mars, likely by a man named Nasola and his wife.

EDCS-10600290.summary: This is a tomb inscription recording the death and burial of Ursicinus.

EDCS-10600297.translation: From the augury of the god Rio, the possessors of this district in their own land took care [of this monument], [dedicated to] Aucalo, son of Aucon, and [to] Camulus, son of [---].
EDCS-10600297.summary: This is a dedication to deities and possibly local spirits, concerning land ownership and its upkeep, likely from a rural context.

EDCS-10600299.translation: For Lecta, belonging to Pinarius Sabinus, Caesar's freedman.
EDCS-10600299.summary: This inscription records a dedication or ownership by Lecta, linked to Pinarius Sabinus, a freedman of Caesar.

EDCS-10600300.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, possibly a name or title.

EDCS-10600303.summary: This inscription names Claudius Vestalis, also known as Lautus, potentially related to a place or a legal status.

EDCS-10600307.translation: [---] gave and dedicated as a gift of Silvanus Sonn[---].
EDCS-10600307.summary: This is a dedication to Silvanus, likely made by someone whose name begins with Sonn[---].

EDCS-10600308.translation: To the departed spirits. His heirs took care to erect this monument for Quintus Arrenius Verecundus, trierarch of the British fleet.
EDCS-10600308.summary: This is a tombstone erected by the heirs of Quintus Arrenius Verecundus, who served as a trierarch in the Roman fleet in Britain.

EDCS-10600309.translation: Beladius, son of Talanus, a Pannonian, aged 45, with 31 years of service, lies here.
EDCS-10600309.summary: This is a tombstone for Beladius, a Pannonian soldier who served 31 years and died at the age of 45.

EDCS-10600310.translation: Tiberius Claudius Seleucus, freedman of Augustus, trierarch, made this monument for Claudia Prima, his freedwoman.
EDCS-10600310.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Tiberius Claudius Seleucus, a freedman of Emperor Augustus and a trierarch, for his freedwoman Claudia Prima.

EDCS-10600313.translation: To the departed spirits, for his young children, Domitianus, trierarch.
EDCS-10600313.summary: A tombstone dedicated to Domitianus's young children by Domitianus himself, who held the rank of trierarch.

EDCS-10600314.translation: To the departed spirits, for Graecia Tertia, daughter of Publius, who lived 3 years, 1 month, and 16 days. Publius Graecius Tertinus, her father, trierarch of the British fleet, saw to its erection.
EDCS-10600314.summary: A tombstone for a young girl named Graecia Tertia, erected by her father, a trierarch in the British fleet.

EDCS-10600315.summary: A tombstone for Lossius Proclinus, identified as a beneficiary, with a possible clarification by Lottius Secundus.

EDCS-10600316.translation: Corio Eavus made this workshop, 103 feet.
EDCS-10600316.summary: An inscription recording the construction of a workshop by Corio Eavus, specifying its length in feet.

EDCS-10600318.translation: To the departed spirits, for Exsupera, aged 30 years, her mother provided.
EDCS-10600318.summary: A tombstone for Exsupera, who died at age 30, erected by her mother.

EDCS-10600320.translation: To the departed spirits, for Iulia Vitalica, Lucius Longius Felix, her husband.
EDCS-10600320.summary: A tombstone for Iulia Vitalica, erected by her husband, Lucius Longius Felix.

EDCS-10600321.summary: A simple tombstone marking the burial place of Viator.

EDCS-10600322.translation: Perhaps by Volusius Saturninus, lies here.
EDCS-10600322.summary: A tombstone indicating that Volusius Saturninus is buried here, possibly indicating the dedicator.

EDCS-10600323.translation: To the departed spirits, for Publia Vongidia Saturnina, who lived 20 years. Valerius Natalis made this for his most devoted and deserving wife.
EDCS-10600323.summary: A tombstone for Publia Vongidia Saturnina, who died at 20, erected by her husband Valerius Natalis.

EDCS-10600326.summary: An epitaph for Sennius, likely a child, expressing affection for the deceased.

EDCS-10600328.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Marco Antonio Gordiano Pio Felici Augusto pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate III consuli II patri patriae civitas Morinorum\n
EDCS-10600328.translation: To the Emperor, Caesar Marcus Antonius Gordianus Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 3rd time, consul for the 2nd time, father of the country, the people of the Morini [dedicate this].
EDCS-10600328.summary: This inscription is a dedication by the civitas Morinorum to Emperor Gordian III, likely dating to his third tribunate and second consulship (AD 241-242).

EDCS-10600329.translation: Sacred to Sulevis. Lucius Cassius Nigrinianus [dedicated this] for himself [and others?].
EDCS-10600329.summary: This is a dedication to the deity Sulevis by Lucius Cassius Nigrinianus, with the latter part of the inscription indicating it was for himself and possibly others.

EDCS-10600330.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. From a brother.
EDCS-10600330.summary: This is a funerary inscription (Dis Manibus) from a brother to the deceased Sualiccia.

EDCS-10600331.translation: Sacred to Augustus and the god Jupiter. Vitalis, son of Priscus, from the village of Dolichus, took care of [this].
EDCS-10600331.summary: This inscription records the care taken by Vitalis, son of Priscus, for a sacred monument possibly dedicated to Augustus and Jupiter, belonging to the vicus Dolich(ens)is.

EDCS-10600334.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus monimentum instituit sibi vivus Ulpius Iustus Ar\n
EDCS-10600334.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Ulpius Iustus established this monument for himself while alive.
EDCS-10600334.summary: This is a funerary inscription where Ulpius Iustus established his own monument (a "living memorial") for himself.

EDCS-10600336.summary: This is a dedication to the god Apollo by Tiberius Minucius.

EDCS-10600337.translation: To the Nervini. Gaius Julius Tertius willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10600337.summary: This inscription records Gaius Julius Tertius fulfilling a vow made to the Nervini.

EDCS-10600338.translation: Sacred because of the arrival of Tiberius Caesar, son of Augustus, grandson of the deified [Caesar]. Gnaeus Licinius Navos, son of Gaius, of the Voltinia tribe.
EDCS-10600338.summary: This inscription is a sacred dedication by Gnaeus Licinius Navos related to the arrival of Tiberius Caesar.

EDCS-10600340.translation: To Tiberius Iulius Tiberinus, duovir, of the Nervii. Quintus Titius Vilicus, lictor.
EDCS-10600340.summary: This inscription honors Tiberius Iulius Tiberinus, a duovir of the Nervii, and is associated with Quintus Titius Vilicus, a lictor.

EDCS-10600341.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Quintus Pompeius Crispus and Tarquinia Secunda. Pompeius Victor [made this] for [his] parents. // To the spirits of the underworld. Marcus Pompeius Victor, quaestor of Roman citizens of the civitas Nerviorum, made this for himself and his wife Ocratia Secunda while alive.
EDCS-10600341.summary: This inscription contains two funerary dedications: the first by Pompeius Victor for his parents, and the second by Marcus Pompeius Victor, a quaestor among the Nervii, for himself and his wife.

EDCS-10600344.translation: To the Divine Shades: Gaius Julius Ulpianus made this for Julia Felicula.
EDCS-10600344.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Gaius Julius Ulpianus for Julia Felicula.

EDCS-10600345.summary: A funerary epitaph recording a maker identified only as Modicus.

EDCS-10600346.translation: Utilis and Optata, wife of Quintus Sutor Brocchus, are buried here.
EDCS-10600346.summary: A funerary epitaph for Utilis and Optata, wife of Quintus Sutor Brocchus.

EDCS-10600348.translation: [---] Camillia Aiausa, daughter of Camillus Victor, [fulfilled her] vow.
EDCS-10600348.summary: A funerary inscription fragment recording Camillia Aiausa, daughter of Camillus Victor, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-10600349.translation: To the Divine Shades: For Latinianus.
EDCS-10600349.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated to Latinianus.

EDCS-10600350.translation: To the Divine Shades: For Probus, son of Tiberius.
EDCS-10600350.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated to Probus, son of Tiberius.

EDCS-10600353.translation: To the Cantrustei Mothers: Gaius Appianius Paternus willingly and deservedly [fulfilled his vow] for himself and his family.
EDCS-10600353.summary: An inscription dedicated to the Mothers by Gaius Appianius Paternus for himself and his family.

EDCS-10600354.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Imbrius Verattius votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10600354.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Imbrius Verattius willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10600354.summary: A votive inscription to Jupiter Best and Greatest by Imbrius Verattius.

EDCS-10600383.translation: For Ammacae, also called Gamaleda, daughter of Verecundus.
EDCS-10600383.summary: A funerary dedication to Ammacae (or Gamaleda), daughter of Verecundus.

EDCS-10600385.translation: Here rests Amabeles, in Christ, who lived [3] years, 6 months, 12 days.
EDCS-10600385.summary: A Christian funerary epitaph for Amabeles, recording her lifespan.

EDCS-10600400.text_edition: \n Deo Entarabo et Genio |(curiae) Ollodagi porticum quam Velugnius Ingenuus promiserat post obitum eius Sollavius Victor filius adoptivos fecit\n
EDCS-10600400.translation: To the god Entarabus and the Genius of the curia, Sollavius Victor, his adopted son, built the portico which Velugnius Ingenuus had promised after his death.
EDCS-10600400.summary: This inscription records the completion of a portico in honor of local deities, funded by an adopted son after the death of the original promisor.

EDCS-10600403.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deo Apollini Granno Phoebo Lucius Ingenuvius Primanus ex voto posuit\n
EDCS-10600403.translation: In honor of the divine house, Lucius Ingenuvius Primanus dedicated this altar to the god Apollo Grannus Phoebus in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-10600403.summary: This inscription records a private dedication to Apollo, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE, in honor of the imperial family.

EDCS-10600404.text_edition: \n Deo Asclepio Titus Iulius Titi filius Fabia Saturninus procurator Augustorum dono dedit\n
EDCS-10600404.translation: Titus Iulius Saturninus, son of Titus, of the Fabia tribe, procurator of the emperors, gave this gift to the god Asclepius.
EDCS-10600404.summary: This inscription records a gift made by an imperial procurator to the god Asclepius, likely from the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-10600405.text_edition: \n Deae Bellonae aram Iusta ex imperio posuit libens merito\n
EDCS-10600405.translation: Iusta erected this altar to the goddess Bellona, willingly and deservedly, by order.
EDCS-10600405.summary: This inscription records a private vow fulfilled by a woman named Iusta to the goddess Bellona.

EDCS-10600406.text_edition: \n Dibus et deabus Iulia Reticiana pro se et suis donum dedit\n
EDCS-10600406.translation: Iulia Reticiana gave this gift to the gods and goddesses for herself and her family.
EDCS-10600406.summary: This inscription records a general dedication to all gods and goddesses by a woman for her household.

EDCS-10600409.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Genio arenariorum consistentium colonia Augusta Treverorum Axsillius Avitus sive Sacruna donum dedit\n
EDCS-10600409.translation: In honor of the divine house, Axsillius Avitus, also known as Sacruna, dedicated this gift to the Genius of the quarry workers residing in the colony Augusta Treverorum.
EDCS-10600409.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the Genius of quarry workers in Augusta Treverorum, made in honor of the imperial house.

EDCS-10600411.text_edition: \n Deae Hecatae Caius Candidius Piscator visu monitus\n
EDCS-10600411.translation: Gaius Candidius Piscator, prompted by a vision, [dedicated this to] the goddess Hecate.
EDCS-10600411.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the goddess Hecate by a man named Caius Candidius Piscator, inspired by a vision.

EDCS-10600412.text_edition: \n Deae Icovellaunae Marcus Primius Alpicius votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10600412.translation: Marcus Primius Alpicius willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the goddess Icovellauna.
EDCS-10600412.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow to the goddess Icovellauna by Marcus Primius Alpicius.

EDCS-10600413.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Iovi Optimo Maximo Aurelius Masgilus et Lucius Aelius Victor beneficiarii legionis VIII Augustae votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10600413.translation: In honor of the divine house, Aurelius Masgilus and Lucius Aelius Victor, beneficiaries of the Legio VIII Augusta, willingly and deservedly fulfilled their vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus.
EDCS-10600413.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by two soldiers of the Legio VIII Augusta, in honor of the imperial family.

EDCS-10600414.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Caius uniaus Iaus et Titus Albius Ianuarius de suo dederunt\n
EDCS-10600414.translation: Caius uniaus Iaus and Titus Albius Ianuarius gave this from their own resources to Jupiter Optimus Maximus.
EDCS-10600414.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus made by two individuals from their personal funds.

EDCS-10600415.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Iovi Optimo Maximo arcum cum ostiis Melius Finitimus ex voto suscepto libens merito\n
EDCS-10600415.translation: In honor of the divine house, Melius Finitimus gave a triumphal arch with gates to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, in accordance with a vow freely undertaken and deserved.
EDCS-10600415.summary: This is a dedication of a triumphal arch and gates to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, honoring the imperial family.

EDCS-10600417.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et vico Voclannionum Urissulius Campanus donum dedit\n
EDCS-10600417.translation: Urissulius Campanus gave this gift to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and the neighborhood of the Voclannioni.
EDCS-10600417.summary: This inscription records a gift to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and a local neighborhood association.

EDCS-10600418.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Iovi Optimo Maximo et vico Voclannionum culinam vetustate conla<p=B>sam infra scripti de suo restituerunt ius Caupo Iulius Statianus ius Saturninus Sattonius sionius Axillius imitius Sattonius ollius Secco Pardius incius Ursinus Pardius Afer us Quartius inus \n
EDCS-10600418.translation: In honor of the divine house, the undersigned restored the kitchen below, worn out by age, to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and the neighborhood of the Voclannioni; from their own funds: the innkeeper Iulius Statianus, the innkeeper Saturninus Sattonius, Sionius Axillius, Imitius Sattonius, Ollius Secco Pardius, Incius Ursinus Pardius Afer, Us Quartius.
EDCS-10600418.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a kitchen by named individuals, honoring the imperial family, Jupiter Optimus Maximus, and a local neighborhood association.

EDCS-10600420.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Numini Augusti et Genio viciniae Marcus Mannius Marinus et Cossia Nerta et sui donum dederunt\n
EDCS-10600420.translation: Marcus Mannius Marinus and Cossia Nerta and their family gave this gift to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, the numen of Augustus, and the genius of the neighborhood.
EDCS-10600420.summary: This is a dedication of a gift to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, the emperor's divine presence, and the local neighborhood spirit.

EDCS-10600421.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deo Marti Intarabo Vitalius Victorinus et Novellinius Mallus fanum et simulacrum a fundamentis ex voto restituerunt\n
EDCS-10600421.translation: In honor of the divine house, Vitalius Victorinus and Novellinius Mallus restored a shrine and its statue from the foundations, in accordance with a vow, to the god Mars Intarabo.
EDCS-10600421.summary: This inscription records the vow-based restoration of a shrine and statue to the god Mars Intarabo, honoring the imperial family.

EDCS-10600422.text_edition: \n Leno Marti Sulpicius I Segnior Oeceano quam lux aeterna vocabat luctificus Titan numquam magis aethera\n
EDCS-10600422.translation: Leno, from Sulpicius I Segnior, to Mars, to Oceanus, whom eternal light called the bringer of grief; Titan never more the sky...
EDCS-10600422.summary: This is a fragmented inscription, possibly a dedicatory verse, mentioning Mars, Oceanus, and Titan.

EDCS-10600423.text_edition: \n Marti Victori Augusto Caius Alpinius Alpini libertus Avi\n
EDCS-10600423.translation: Caius Alpinius, freedman of Alpinius, to Mars Victor Augustus.
EDCS-10600423.summary: This is a dedication to Mars Victor Augustus by Caius Alpinius, a freedman.

EDCS-10600424.text_edition: \n Indus Mediomatricus Mercurio votum libens merito solvit\n
EDCS-10600424.translation: Indus of the Mediomatrici freely and deservedly paid his vow to Mercury.
EDCS-10600424.summary: This inscription records Indus of the Mediomatrici fulfilling a vow to Mercury.

EDCS-10600426.text_edition: \n Deo Mercurio Respectia Victoria solvit votum libens\n
EDCS-10600426.translation: Respectia Victoria freely paid her vow to the god Mercury.
EDCS-10600426.summary: This inscription records Respectia Victoria fulfilling a vow to the god Mercury.

EDCS-10600430.text_edition: \n Deae <S=D>ironae Lucius Lucanius Censorinus sigillum donum dedit \n
EDCS-10600430.translation: Lucius Lucanius Censorinus gave this small statue as a gift to the goddess Sirona.
EDCS-10600430.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a small statue to the goddess Sirona by Lucius Lucanius Censorinus.

EDCS-10600432.translation: To the goddess Sulevia, Dimmia fulfilled [a vow].
EDCS-10600432.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the goddess Sulevia by Dimmia.

EDCS-10600435.text_edition: \n Moderata pro salute sua et fratr[is ------\n
EDCS-10600435.translation: Moderata for the health of herself and her brother [...]
EDCS-10600435.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription recording a vow made by Moderata for the health of herself and her brother.

EDCS-10600436.text_edition: \n Secundius pro Procla filia votum solverunt libentes laeti merito\n
EDCS-10600436.translation: Secundius and [others?] fulfilled their vow for Procla, daughter, gladly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-10600436.summary: This inscription records Secundius and others fulfilling a vow for Procla, a daughter.

EDCS-10600440.text_edition: \n Indulgentissimo domino nostro Flavio Valerio Constantio nobilissimo C Caesari Valerius Concordius vir perfectissimus dux devotus Numini maiiestatique eorum\n
EDCS-10600440.translation: Valerius Concordius, most perfect *dux* and devoted to the divine power and majesty of our most indulgent lord Flavius Valerius Constantius, the most noble Caesar, has [made this dedication].
EDCS-10600440.summary: This is a dedication made by Valerius Concordius, a *dux*, to the emperor Constantius, likely in the 4th century CE.

EDCS-10600442.translation: Here lies Aelius Constantius, consular man, count and master of both branches of the military service, and patrician, and second ordinary consul.
EDCS-10600442.summary: This is a tombstone for Aelius Constantius, who held high military and administrative offices, including ordinary consul, likely in the late Roman Empire.

EDCS-10600444.translation: To Marcus Ga[vius] / son of Marcus / Max[imus], prefect [of the praetorium].
EDCS-10600444.summary: This is a tombstone for Marcus Gavius Maximus, who held the prestigious position of Praetorian Prefect.

EDCS-10600447.translation: Marcus Piavionius Victorinus, tribune of the praetorians, restored [this].
EDCS-10600447.summary: This inscription records that Marcus Piavionius Victorinus, a tribune of the praetorian guard, restored something.

EDCS-10600448.translation: Here rests in peace Babbo, who lived 7 years, 7 months, and [3 days]. Gerontius, tribune, placed this monument for his son.
EDCS-10600448.summary: This is a tombstone for Babbo, a child, placed by his father Gerontius, a tribune.

EDCS-10600450.translation: Hariulf, bodyguard of the imperial household, son of Hanhavald of royal lineage of the Burgundians, who lived 20 years, 9 months, and 9 days. Reutilo, his maternal uncle, made this.
EDCS-10600450.summary: This is a tombstone for Hariulf, a bodyguard of Burgundian royal descent, erected by his uncle Reutilo.

EDCS-10600451.translation: Here rest the remains of Hloderic, who took the title of count in the vicariate, was esteemed in his rank and first in his class, for whom his noble wife ordered a monument to be made out of love; who lived in this world more or less [30] years; whose burial was in this world on the 7th day before the Kalends of August.
EDCS-10600451.summary: This is a tombstone for Hloderic, a count, erected by his wife, dating to the late Roman or early medieval period.

EDCS-10600452.text_edition: \n Flavio <C=G>ornelio Rufino ex cohort<e=IS> prima Hamiorum milliar<ia=TE> in Syria genito in Asia Trallis defuncto Augusta Treverica annorum LV C<l=I>audia Afrania Valentina coniugi carissimo viva fecit \n
EDCS-10600452.translation: To Flavius Cornelius Rufinus, born in Syria, a man of the first cohort of Hamian archers, who died in Augusta Treverica, aged 55; his dearest wife, Claudiana Afrania Valentina, erected this monument to him while she was alive.
EDCS-10600452.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Flavius Cornelius Rufinus, a soldier who died in Augusta Treverica, erected by his wife.

EDCS-10600453.summary: This is a very short inscription, likely a tombstone or dedication, for Vitalis, a standard-bearer.

EDCS-10600454.translation: Rianus Amba, aged 30, [with X years] of service.
EDCS-10600454.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age and service length of Rianus Amba.

EDCS-10600455.translation: Here lies Vialis, who lived 75 years and served among the senior Jovian soldiers for 11 years; his dearest wife placed this inscription.
EDCS-10600455.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life span and military service of Vialis, erected by his wife.

EDCS-10600456.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Marco Aurelio Materno Augusti liberto defuncto coniugi rarissimo et incomparabili pientissimo suis Alexandria Prudentia coniux fecit\n
EDCS-10600456.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Alexandria Prudentia, his wife, erected this monument to Marcus Aurelius Maternus, freedman of the emperor, her most rare, incomparable, and devoted husband.
EDCS-10600456.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Aurelius Maternus, a freedman of the emperor, erected by his devoted wife.

EDCS-10600457.text_edition: \n Qui dolet interitum mentem soletur amore tollere mors vitam potuit post fata superstes fama viget periit corpus sed nomen in ore est vivit laudatur legitur celebratur amatur nuncius Augusti velox pede cursor cui Latiae gentis nomen patriaeque Sabinus o crudele nefas tulit hic sine crimine mortem damnatus periit deceptus fraude latronum nihil scelus egisti fama est quae nescit obire posuit Turius\n
EDCS-10600457.translation: He who grieves at death should soothe his mind and banish sorrow; death could not take his life, but he survives beyond the grave, his fame flourishes. The body perished, but the name is on the lips; he lives, is praised, is read, is celebrated, is loved. A swift messenger of the Emperor, a runner with winged foot, whose name was Sabinus, of Latin stock and of the homeland. O cruel impiety! He met his death here without crime, condemned and deceived by the treachery of brigands. Fame testifies that he did no wrong and did not pass away. Turius placed this.
EDCS-10600457.summary: This is a funerary inscription praising the victim of a judicial error and brigandage, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10600458.translation: Here rests in peace Ingenua, a faithful Christian. Ursacius, her most devoted dominical courier, placed this inscription for his most sweet mother, who lived 28 years and died on the eighth day before the Kalends of February, in Christ.
EDCS-10600458.summary: This is a Christian funerary epitaph for Ingenua, erected by her son Ursacius.

EDCS-10600459.text_edition: \n Iacet hiic Maura coniux Bonifati a veste sacra <q=O>uae <p=R>rececessit in <p=R>ace et fuit secum annos XX \n
EDCS-10600459.translation: Here lies Maura, wife of Bonifatius, from the sacred vestments, who passed away in peace and was with him for 20 years.
EDCS-10600459.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Maura, wife of Bonifatius, noting her marriage duration.

EDCS-10600461.text_edition: \n Iustio Muciano decurioni civitatis Treverorum duumviro aerarii publici et Rustio Muciano filio defunctis Aprilia Ursula coniunx viva sibi et Aprilia Paterna filia titulum faciendum curaverunt\n
EDCS-10600461.translation: Aprilia Ursula, wife of the deceased, while alive, and Aprilia Paterna, daughter, arranged for this monument to be made to Iustius Mucianus, decurion of the city of the Treveri and duumvir of the public treasury, and to Rustius Mucianus, son.
EDCS-10600461.summary: This is a funerary monument commissioned by a wife and daughter for two male relatives, Iustius and Rustius Mucianus, who held civic and financial offices in Augusta Treverorum.

EDCS-10600462.text_edition: \n Ob memoriam custodiendam adque propagandam magistrorum et parentum suorum Iustiani Iuliani Aprilis Pompeiani Theodori Martialis Arcadi Nycteri Concordius et Hemerius haruspices publici civitatis Treverorum fecerunt\n
EDCS-10600462.translation: For the sake of remembrance and perpetuation of their masters and parents, Iustianus, Iulianus, Aprilis, Pompeianus, Theodorus, Martialis, Arcadius, Nycterus, Concordius, and Hemerius, public haruspices of the city of the Treveri, made this.
EDCS-10600462.summary: This is a dedication made by public haruspices of Augusta Treverorum to commemorate their masters and parents.

EDCS-10600463.text_edition: \n IIIIIIvir Augustalis Iunianus Modestus libertus et heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-10600463.translation: Iunianus Modestus, a member of the college of the Six, as freedman and heir, saw to its construction.
EDCS-10600463.summary: This inscription records the construction of a monument by Iunianus Modestus, a member of a priestly college.

EDCS-10600464.translation: Tasgillus, a Treveran, saw to its construction.
EDCS-10600464.summary: This inscription records the construction of a monument by Tasgillus, an individual from the Treveran tribe.

EDCS-10600465.translation: Here lies in peace Apronius, a leading man, who lived more or less 40 years; his wife Aventina with her sons placed the monument; he rests on the 6th day before the Kalends of November.
EDCS-10600465.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Apronius, who lived about 40 years, and was commemorated by his wife and sons on October 27th.

EDCS-10600469.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Eugeniae filiae defunctae Iulius Victor cuparius et saccarius et Acceptinae coniugi et Florentio filio vivis vivus fecit\n
EDCS-10600469.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Julius Victor, a cup-maker and sack-maker, erected this for Eugenia, his deceased daughter, and for his wife Acceptina and his son Florentius, while he himself was alive.
EDCS-10600469.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Julius Victor, a craftsman, for his deceased daughter, wife, and son.

EDCS-10600471.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Aemilius Epictetus sive Hedonius grammaticus Graecus Primaniae Ianuariae coniugi sanctissimae defunctae et sibi vivus fecit\n
EDCS-10600471.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Aemilius Epictetus, also known as Hedonius, a Greek teacher of grammar, erected this while alive for Primania Ianuaria, his most devoted wife, deceased, and for himself.
EDCS-10600471.summary: This funerary inscription records a monument dedicated by Aemilius Epictetus, a Greek grammarian, to his wife and himself.

EDCS-10600473.translation: Silvanus the merchant rests here in peace.
EDCS-10600473.summary: This is a brief funerary inscription for Silvanus, identified as a merchant.

EDCS-10600474.text_edition: \n Alba et Lucio Albanio vestiari Lucius Albanius libertus ipse \n
EDCS-10600474.translation: Lucius Albanus, himself a freedman, [dedicated this to] Alba and Lucius Albanus.
EDCS-10600474.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Lucius Albanus, a freedman, to Alba and Lucius Albanus.

EDCS-10600475.text_edition: \n Iulia Pieris obstetrix hic iacet nulli gravis\n
EDCS-10600475.translation: Iulia Pieris, the midwife, lies here, burdensome to no one.
EDCS-10600475.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates Iulia Pieris, a midwife, noted for being unobtrusive.

EDCS-10600476.translation: The names listed appear to be a series of individuals, possibly associated with a group or a shared project.
EDCS-10600476.summary: This inscription is a list of numerous names, likely representing members of a collegium or individuals involved in a communal building project.

EDCS-10600484.text_edition: \n Quod desiderasti monumentum hoc Lucio Acceptio Artino filio mater pientissimae solicitae fecit vale\n
EDCS-10600484.translation: For the monument which you desired, your most devoted and solicitous mother made it for Lucius Acceptius Artinus, your son. Farewell.
EDCS-10600484.summary: This inscription records a mother's dedication of a monument to her son, Lucius Acceptius Artinus.

EDCS-10600485.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Aeliae Quadratillae filiae innocentissimae\n
EDCS-10600485.translation: To the departed spirits of Aelia, a most innocent daughter.
EDCS-10600485.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication to Aelia, honoring her innocence.

EDCS-10600486.translation: To the departed spirits of Afra, daughter of Americanus.
EDCS-10600486.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication to Afra, daughter of Americanus.

EDCS-10600487.summary: This fragmented inscription appears to record names, possibly of a dedicator and recipient in a funerary context.
