EDCS-10600489.summary: This fragmented inscription seems to contain names, possibly related to a funerary dedication.

EDCS-10600490.translation: [---]ino [---] / deceased / Attavilla Ursa for her husband and / Acceptius, optio, for his brother and himself, made while alive.
EDCS-10600490.summary: This funerary inscription records a monument made by Acceptius for himself and his deceased brother, and by Attavilla Ursa for her deceased husband.

EDCS-10600491.translation: [---] for Gaius At[---] / deceased / [---] for [---] / for [---]S, [made] [---]
EDCS-10600491.summary: This fragmentary inscription appears to be a funerary dedication, mentioning a deceased person and a maker.

EDCS-10600492.text_edition: \n Aurelius sibi et Aureliae Successae coniugi vivae sibi et suis vivus fecit eo quod mihi defuncto nemo facturus erat qu\n
EDCS-10600492.translation: Aurelius, while alive, made this for himself and for Aurelia Successa, his wife, while she was alive, and for his family, because when I was deceased, no one would have made it for me.
EDCS-10600492.summary: This funerary inscription is a self-dedication made by Aurelius for himself, his wife Aurelia Successa, and his family, intended to ensure a monument after his death.

EDCS-10600493.text_edition: \n defunctae Calionius Festus sibi et suis vivus fecit\n
EDCS-10600493.translation: Calonius Festus, while alive, made this for himself and his family, for the deceased.
EDCS-10600493.summary: This funerary inscription records a self-dedication made by Calonius Festus for himself and his family.

EDCS-10600494.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Camulissius Aprilis et Crispina Iusta parentes Aprilio Iustino filio defuncto et sibi vivis fecerunt\n
EDCS-10600494.translation: To the departed spirits. Camulissius Aprilis and Crispina Iusta, parents, made this for Aprilis Iustinus, their deceased son, and for themselves, while alive.
EDCS-10600494.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by parents, Camulissius Aprilis and Crispina Iusta, for their deceased son Aprilis Iustinus and for themselves.

EDCS-10600495.translation: [---] arranged for it to be made / Catullinus and
EDCS-10600495.summary: This fragmentary inscription indicates that Catullinus and another person arranged for something to be made, likely a monument.

EDCS-10600496.text_edition: \n coniugi defuncto Cricconia Donilla co<n=I>iux eius sibi et posterisque suis viva faciendum curavit \n
EDCS-10600496.translation: After her husband had died, Cricconia Donilla, his wife, arranged for this to be made for herself and her descendants while she was alive.
EDCS-10600496.summary: This is a funerary epitaph arranged by Cricconia Donilla for herself and her descendants, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-10600497.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Domiti Tryphonis Domitius Graptus filius et Tutia Maxsimi<l=I>la nurus faciendum curaverunt \n
EDCS-10600497.translation: To the departed spirits of Domitius Tryphonis. Domitius Graptus, his son, and Tutia Maxsimilla, his daughter-in-law, arranged for this to be made.
EDCS-10600497.summary: This funerary epitaph records the arrangement of a monument by the son and daughter-in-law for Domitius Tryphonis, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-10600500.translation: To the departed spirits of Iulia Faustinula [restored name]...
EDCS-10600500.summary: This is a fragmented funerary epitaph dedicated to Iulia Faustinula, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-10600501.text_edition: \n Libero filio Saturnini defuncto Noniani Nonillus et Saturninus sibi et suis vivis fecerunt\n
EDCS-10600501.translation: Nonianus Nonillus and Saturninus made this for their deceased son Liber, and for themselves and their families, while alive.
EDCS-10600501.summary: This funerary epitaph records the construction of a monument by Nonianus Nonillus and Saturninus for their deceased son Liber and for themselves, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-10600503.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely an epitaph or a dedication, for Lucius Magius Pudentus, possibly from the Imperial period.

EDCS-10600505.translation: To the departed spirits. Sabinia Diuturna made this for her deceased husband Mascellionius Marcellinus and for herself, while alive.
EDCS-10600505.summary: This funerary epitaph records that Sabinia Diuturna commissioned a monument for her deceased husband Mascellionius Marcellinus and for herself, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-10600506.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Motucio Luperco liberto bene cognito defuncto Secundinius Motucus \n
EDCS-10600506.translation: To the departed spirits of Motucius Lupercus, a freedman, well-known, who had died. Secundinius Motucus [arranged for this].
EDCS-10600506.summary: This funerary epitaph is for Motucius Lupercus, a well-regarded freedman, and was arranged by Secundinius Motucus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-10600508.translation: [This was dedicated] by Pacata, daughter of Indus.
EDCS-10600508.summary: This inscription records a dedication or memorial by Pacata, daughter of Indus, possibly from the Imperial period.

EDCS-10600510.text_edition: \n na defuncta NTVIIA Procella mater dedicavit\n
EDCS-10600510.summary: This fragmented inscription records a dedication by Ntvivia Procella, a mother, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-10600513.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Quintae EI Desider RINO\n
EDCS-10600513.translation: To the departed spirits of Quita, [name lost] Desider [name lost] Rino [name lost]...
EDCS-10600513.summary: This is a fragmented funerary epitaph listing multiple names, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-10600514.text_edition: \n Sappulono Iurico genero Secundina et sibi viva faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-10600514.translation: Secundina had this made for her son-in-law Sappulono Iurico and for herself while alive.
EDCS-10600514.summary: This is a funerary epitaph, likely from a tombstone or similar monument, recording a dedication made by Secundina for her son-in-law and herself.

EDCS-10600515.text_edition: \n Saturo filio defuncto Perpetuius Servandus sibi et suis vivus f[ecit ------\n
EDCS-10600515.translation: Perpetuius Servandus made this for his deceased son Saturus and for himself and his family while alive.
EDCS-10600515.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication made by Perpetuius Servandus for his deceased son Saturus and for his family, intended for a tomb or monument.

EDCS-10600516.text_edition: \n ------ Secun]dinus Sattaro filio defuncto annorum XXV et Saturnino Sattara nepoti\n
EDCS-10600516.translation: [... Secundinus made this for his deceased son Sattaro, aged 25, and for Saturninus, grandson of Sattara.
EDCS-10600516.summary: This fragmented epitaph records the dedication of a monument by Secundinus for his deceased son and grandson, specifying the age of the son.

EDCS-10600517.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Secundio fecerunt filii et Opimia Abba ita \n
EDCS-10600517.translation: His sons and Opimia Abba made this for the departed Secundio.
EDCS-10600517.summary: This is a funerary inscription where the sons and Opimia Abba dedicated a monument to the deceased Secundio.

EDCS-10600518.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Sextinio Secundino coniugi defuncto et Severiano et Saturo filiis vivis Primulia Saturna et sibi viva fecit\n
EDCS-10600518.translation: Primulia Saturna and herself while alive made this for her deceased husband Sextinius Secundinus, and for her living sons Severianus and Saturus.
EDCS-10600518.summary: This funerary epitaph records a dedication made by Primulia Saturna for her deceased husband and living sons, and for herself.

EDCS-10600519.translation: The parents [made this] for the just Victoria Caliope [deceased...].
EDCS-10600519.summary: This fragmented inscription appears to be a funerary epitaph where parents dedicated a monument to their deceased daughter, Victoria Caliope.

EDCS-10600522.translation: ...most dutiful [daughter], deceased, who lived 17 years, 7 months, 5 days. [3]icia [deceased] heir and [3]R[...
EDCS-10600522.summary: This broken funerary inscription records the age at death of a deceased woman and mentions an heir, likely from a tombstone.

EDCS-10600526.translation: ...iana, daughter [of...?], for herself and her family.
EDCS-10600526.summary: This fragment of an inscription likely pertains to a funerary monument, indicating a dedication by a woman named Iana for herself and her family.

EDCS-10600544.summary: This very brief and damaged inscription contains names, possibly of a person or people associated with a monument or dedication.

EDCS-10600753.summary: This is a short inscription, possibly a curse or a wish for protection related to a person named Martinianus, perhaps associated with a property or monument.

EDCS-10600754.summary: A brief epitaph recording that Eleuthera, identified as a sinner, placed this monument.

EDCS-10600757.translation: Aufidius the presbyter, of age more or less 60, rests here in peace. Augurina his sister and Augurius his son, because of their love, ordered this tombstone to be made.
EDCS-10600757.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Aufidius, a presbyter aged around 60, placed by his sister and son out of affection.

EDCS-10600759.translation: Here lies Basilius the subdeacon, who lived about 50 years. Bonosa his daughter placed this tombstone on the day of his deposition, the day before the Ides of January.
EDCS-10600759.summary: An epitaph for Basilius, a subdeacon who lived approximately 50 years, placed by his daughter Bonosa, with the date of deposition recorded.

EDCS-10600760.translation: The bones of Ursinianus the subdeacon rest beneath this tomb. He deserved to be joined with the company of saints, whom neither raging Tartarus nor cruel punishment will harm. His most sweet wife Ludula placed this tombstone. She departed on the 5th day before the Kalends of December. She lived 33 years.
EDCS-10600760.summary: This epitaph commemorates Ursinianus, a subdeacon, whose remains are buried here; his wife Ludula placed the monument after his death at the age of 33.

EDCS-10600762.translation: Here rests Ursatius the ostiarius, who lived 67 years. Exsuperius his son placed this tombstone.
EDCS-10600762.summary: An epitaph for Ursatius, an ostiarius (doorkeeper) aged 67, placed by his son Exsuperius.

EDCS-10600763.translation: Here rests in peace Abbo, who lived 33 years. His brother made this tombstone out of affection.
EDCS-10600763.summary: This inscription records the burial of Abbo, who lived 33 years, with the monument placed by his brother due to affection.

EDCS-10600764.translation: Here rests in peace Agricius, who lived 8 years and 2 months. Calvola his mother and Februarius his father placed this tombstone.
EDCS-10600764.summary: An epitaph for Agricius, who lived 8 years and 2 months, with the monument placed by his parents, Februarius and Calvola.

EDCS-10600766.translation: Here rests Ac[---]us, who lived 50 years and 30 days. Marinus placed this tombstone for his comrade(?).
EDCS-10600766.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Ac[---]us, aged 50 years and 30 days, with the monument likely placed by his comrade Marinus.

EDCS-10600768.text_edition: \n Hic Amantiae in pace hospita caro iacet\n
EDCS-10600768.translation: Here lies Amantiae, a dear guest in peace.
EDCS-10600768.summary: A simple epitaph stating that Amantiae, a welcome guest, lies here in peace.

EDCS-10600769.translation: Here will rest well in peace Amelius, who lived 34 years and 3 months and 15 days. Rufa placed this tombstone for her dearest son.
EDCS-10600769.summary: An epitaph for Amelius, who lived 34 years, 3 months, and 15 days, with the monument placed by his mother Rufa.

EDCS-10600770.translation: Ampelius rests here in peace, who lived 23 years, 25 days. Siclvdo Sinoi.
EDCS-10600770.summary: This epitaph records the death of Ampelius, who lived 23 years and 25 days.

EDCS-10600772.translation: Apiciola, who lived... set up this monument... in peace.
EDCS-10600772.summary: This epitaph records the death of Apiciola and the erection of her monument.

EDCS-10600773.translation: Here lies in peace the sweetest daughter Arablia, who lived 7 years, [missing months] months and 10 days. Her father Posidonius set up this monument. In peace.
EDCS-10600773.summary: This epitaph records the death of the infant Arablia, daughter of Posidonius, and states her age at death.

EDCS-10600774.translation: Arcadiola will rest here, who lived more or less 34 years. Her [relatives?] Ursulus, Maurus, and Hetlea erected this monument. In peace.
EDCS-10600774.summary: This epitaph records the death of Arcadiola, who lived approximately 34 years, and names the individuals who erected the monument.

EDCS-10600777.translation: Auspicius made [this] for himself, [living] 22 years and 3 months.
EDCS-10600777.summary: This epitaph records the life of Auspicius, who lived 22 years and 3 months.

EDCS-10600778.translation: Here lies in peace Bancio, who lived 2 years, 2 months, and 8 days. His mother Faventia set up this monument.
EDCS-10600778.summary: This epitaph records the death of Bancio, who lived 2 years, 2 months, and 8 days, and identifies his mother as the monument's erector.

EDCS-10600779.translation: Here lies Barbario, who lived 8 months and 24 days. In peace.
EDCS-10600779.summary: This epitaph records the death of Barbario, who lived 8 months and 24 days.

EDCS-10600780.translation: Here lies Bonosus, who lived [missing years] years, 6 months, 13 days. [Name] set up the monument. In peace.
EDCS-10600780.summary: This epitaph records the death of Bonosus, providing his age at death in months and days, and noting the erection of his monument.

EDCS-10600786.summary: This is a fragmented inscription with only partial names or words preserved.

EDCS-10600787.translation: Here lies in peace Dafinis(?), who lived 26 years, [missing days] days.
EDCS-10600787.summary: This epitaph records the death of Dafinis(?), who lived 26 years and some days.

EDCS-10600788.translation: Damasius, the accountant(?), rests here in peace.
EDCS-10600788.summary: This is an epitaph for Damasius, identified as an accountant (?), who rests in peace.

EDCS-10600789.translation: Dardanius, who lived 35 years, will rest here; his brother Apronius placed this tombstone in peace.
EDCS-10600789.summary: This epitaph records the death of Dardanius, who lived 35 years, with his brother Apronius setting up the monument.

EDCS-10600790.translation: Dignissima Fidelis, who lived 1 year, 8 months, and 5 days, rests here in peace; Dignantius and Meropia placed this tombstone for their father.
EDCS-10600790.summary: This epitaph commemorates Dignissima Fidelis, who died at the age of 1 year, 8 months, and 5 days, with Dignantius and Meropia setting up the stone for their father.

EDCS-10600791.translation: Doxates, who lived more or less 25 years, lies buried here in peace.
EDCS-10600791.summary: This epitaph states that Doxates lies buried here in peace, having lived approximately 25 years.

EDCS-10600793.translation: Escupilio, who lived 1 year, 10 months, and 17 days, lies here in peace; his mother and father placed this tombstone.
EDCS-10600793.summary: This epitaph records Escupilio, who lived 1 year, 10 months, and 17 days, with his parents setting up the monument.

EDCS-10600795.text_edition: \n Hic iacet Eusebius qui vixit annum unum et menses sex m<i=E>nus dies V titulum posuit dulcissimo filio suo Vitachristi mater \n
EDCS-10600795.translation: Eusebius, who lived one year and six months and 5 days, lies here; his mother placed this tombstone for her sweetest son Vitachristi.
EDCS-10600795.summary: This epitaph marks the burial of Eusebius, who lived 1 year, 6 months, and 5 days, with his mother setting up the stone for her son Vitachristi.

EDCS-10600796.summary: This is a brief epitaph for Euticianus, described as faithful, in peace.

EDCS-10600797.summary: This is a damaged epitaph for a person named Euticia, with partially legible or uncertain names following.

EDCS-10600798.translation: Exsoperantia, who lived 9 years, 5 months, and 15 days, lies here; Albinus and Terintina, her parents, placed this tombstone in peace.
EDCS-10600798.summary: This epitaph records Exsoperantia, who lived 9 years, 5 months, and 15 days, with her parents Albinus and Terintina setting up the monument.

EDCS-10600799.translation: Ipsychius, who lived in the world 28 years and 4 months, will rest in peace; Archontus placed this tombstone for his dearest wife.
EDCS-10600799.summary: This epitaph states that Ipsychius, who lived 28 years and 4 months, will rest in peace, with her husband Archontus setting up the monument.

EDCS-10600801.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely naming Flavius Vic[---] and RIBV[---], with incomplete text suggesting personal names or titles, possibly from a funerary or honorific monument.

EDCS-10600802.translation: This tomb will cover the girl Elavia, aged twelve. Her brother placed the inscription on the day of burial, the 15th day before the Kalends of [---]
EDCS-10600802.summary: This is a funerary inscription for the girl Elavia, who died at twelve years old, placed by her brother with the date of burial recorded.

EDCS-10600804.translation: In peace. VE[---] lived for one year and [---] months. Florentina placed the inscription, buried on the [---] Kalends of September.
EDCS-10600804.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription recording the life span of an individual and the placement of the monument by Florentina, with a date in September.

EDCS-10600805.text_edition: \n Hic iacet Galla quae vixit annos X dies XXX titulum posuerunt Martyrius et Silvia in pace\n
EDCS-10600805.translation: Here lies Galla who lived 10 years and 30 days. Martyrius and Silvia placed the inscription in peace.
EDCS-10600805.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Galla, aged 10 years and 30 days, with the monument placed by Martyrius and Silvia.

EDCS-10600806.translation: Here rests in peace Gaudentiolus, who lived 7 years, 6 months, and 15 days. Gaudentius and Seriola, father and mother, placed the inscription.
EDCS-10600806.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gaudentiolus, who lived 7 years, 6 months, and 15 days, with the monument placed by his parents.

EDCS-10600809.translation: Here lies Genesius, who lived 45 years and was in the bond of marriage for 17 years. Although departed by an untimely death, he nevertheless left behind all his surviving children and his wife. His most loving and most obedient wife dedicated this inscription, forever bound to him.
EDCS-10600809.summary: This is an epitaph for Genesius, who lived 45 years and was married for 17, with the monument dedicated by his devoted wife.

EDCS-10600810.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription for Genesius, recording his name and beginning to state his lifespan.

EDCS-10600811.translation: Geronius placed the inscription for his dearest wife Sanctula, who lived 25 years, 4 months, and 20 days. Rest in peace.
EDCS-10600811.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sanctula, who lived 25 years, 4 months, and 20 days, with the monument placed by her husband Geronius.

EDCS-10600813.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, possibly a funerary monument, mentioning 'Hagdul-' and the number 51, likely referring to an age or a count.

EDCS-10600814.translation: Here rests in the Lord the girl of God, Hilaritas by name, who in all the days of her life worshipped God and observed all the precepts of the Savior Lord in every action. She lived, moreover, more or less 50 years. Lea, devoted to God, a girl bound by the tie of charity and zeal for religion, placed the inscription.
EDCS-10600814.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a young girl named Hilaritas, who lived about 50 years and was devout, with the monument placed by Lea.

EDCS-10600815.translation: Here rests in peace Honoria, who lived 4 years and 4 months. Her parents placed this monument out of love.
EDCS-10600815.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a girl named Honoria, recording her age at death and that her parents erected the monument.

EDCS-10600816.translation: Here lies Ianuaria, who lived approximately 50 years. Valerius placed this monument for his wife in peace.
EDCS-10600816.summary: A funerary epitaph for Ianuaria, stating her approximate age and that her husband Valerius erected the monument.

EDCS-10600817.translation: Here rests Ilecius in peace, a faithful one.
EDCS-10600817.summary: A funerary epitaph for Ilecius, described as faithful, with a date inferred to be late Roman period.

EDCS-10600818.translation: Here rest in peace three most beloved brothers: Iovinianus, Innocentius and Dedamius, Petrus and Urbana. Their parents placed this monument.
EDCS-10600818.summary: A funerary epitaph for three brothers, Iovinianus, Innocentius, and Dedamius, whose parents erected the monument.

EDCS-10600819.text_edition: \n Hic bene quiesc<i=E>t Iovina quae vixit annos X et menses X dies V Viator coniugi dulcissimae titulum posuit \n
EDCS-10600819.translation: Here rests well Iovina, who lived 10 years, 10 months and 5 days. Viator placed this monument for his most beloved wife.
EDCS-10600819.summary: A funerary epitaph for Iovina, detailing her age and that her husband Viator erected the monument for his beloved wife.

EDCS-10600820.translation: Here lies Isa, who lived faithfully in peace for approximately 30 years. Fortio, his grieving wife, placed this monument.
EDCS-10600820.summary: A funerary epitaph for Isa, stating his approximate age and that his wife Fortio erected the monument out of grief.

EDCS-10600821.translation: Here rests in peace a devout girl named Lea, who lived 22 years and 12 days. Litorius and Sancta placed this monument out of love for her.
EDCS-10600821.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lea, a devout girl, recording her age and that Litorius and Sancta erected the monument out of affection.

EDCS-10600822.translation: Leo rests here in peace, lived one year and 40 days. His parents placed this monument for their most beloved son.
EDCS-10600822.summary: A funerary epitaph for Leo, recording his age and that his parents erected the monument for their beloved son.

EDCS-10600823.translation: Here rests in peace Leo, who lived 4 years, 7 months and 12 days.
EDCS-10600823.summary: A funerary epitaph for Leo, detailing his age at death.

EDCS-10600827.translation: Here lies [3]baudes, who lived 3 years and 13 days. Lopolus, his father, placed this monument for him in peace.
EDCS-10600827.summary: A funerary epitaph for [3]baudes, recording his age and that his father Lopolus erected the monument.

EDCS-10600828.translation: Here lies the most sweet infant Lupantia, faithful in peace, who lived 3 years, 5 months, and 18 days. Treverius, her father, for the love of his daughter, placed this monument.
EDCS-10600828.summary: A funerary epitaph for an infant named Lupantia, placed by her father.

EDCS-10600829.translation: Here lies in peace Lupicinus, who lived more or less 70 years, 2 months, and 10 days. Veneria, his most dear wife, placed this monument.
EDCS-10600829.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lupicinus, placed by his wife.

EDCS-10600831.translation: Here lies Marcus, who lived 26 years. Pusena placed this monument on the day of her death.
EDCS-10600831.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus, placed by Pusena.

EDCS-10600832.translation: Here rests Marinus the faithful, who lived more or less 20 years. His son Nonnita placed this monument in peace.
EDCS-10600832.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marinus, placed by his son.

EDCS-10600833.translation: Here lies in peace Martina, a most sweet girl, who lived 16 years and 1 month. Her parents placed this monument.
EDCS-10600833.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young girl named Martina, placed by her parents.

EDCS-10600834.translation: Here in peace rests Martiola the faithful. Her son Sambatius Ursus placed this monument in peace.
EDCS-10600834.summary: A funerary epitaph for Martiola, placed by her son Sambatius Ursus.

EDCS-10600835.translation: Marus shall rest here in peace, who lived 4 years, 3 months, and 15 days. His most devoted father placed this monument.
EDCS-10600835.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marus, placed by his father.

EDCS-10600838.text_edition: \n Memorio coniugi dulcissimo qui vixit annis XXXVII Festa posuit in pace Virtus imperii hostes vincti ludant Romani\n
EDCS-10600838.translation: In memory of my most sweet husband, who lived 37 years. Festa placed this in peace. Let the Romans rejoice with the conquered enemies bound.
EDCS-10600838.summary: A funerary epitaph for a husband, placed by his wife Festa, with an unusual martial epigram.

EDCS-10600839.summary: A fragment of an inscription, too damaged to yield further information.

EDCS-10600842.translation: Here shall rest Nunechius in peace, who lived more or less 80 years. Florentina, his most dear daughter, placed this monument.
EDCS-10600842.summary: A funerary epitaph for Nunechius, placed by his daughter Florentina.

EDCS-10600843.text_edition: \n et Paula rito in pace XXII VII rito II pro caritate pater maritus posuit\n
EDCS-10600843.translation: Paula and her husband rest in peace, having lived 22 years. Her husband, out of love, placed this monument.
EDCS-10600843.summary: A funerary epitaph for Paula and her husband, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10600844.translation: Here lies Perpetuus, in his God Christ, well-deserving, who lived 25 years. Lecontia, his mother, placed this monument. In peace.
EDCS-10600844.summary: A funerary epitaph for Perpetuus, who lived 25 years, set up by his mother, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10600845.translation: Here rests in peace Piolus, who lived 5 years, 2 months, and 11 days. Nigrinus and Ruriciola, his parents, placed this monument.
EDCS-10600845.summary: A funerary epitaph for Piolus, who lived 5 years, 2 months, and 11 days, set up by his parents, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10600849.translation: Here rests in peace Priectus, who lived 16 years. Vindiomola, his mother, placed this monument.
EDCS-10600849.summary: A funerary epitaph for Priectus, who lived 16 years, set up by his mother, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10600853.translation: Here rests in peace Revocatus, who lived more or less 35 years. Francola, his wife, placed this monument.
EDCS-10600853.summary: A funerary epitaph for Revocatus, who lived approximately 35 years, placed by his wife, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10600855.translation: Rusticula passed away before the fourth day before the Ides of January. She had her burial on the day before the Ides of January, having lived 22 years and into her third year.
EDCS-10600855.summary: A funerary epitaph for Rusticula, recording her death date and age, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10600857.summary: A fragmentary epitaph possibly for a father named Sabin[---].

EDCS-10600858.translation: Here rests in peace Sarracina, who lived more or less 34 years. Her sons placed this monument.
EDCS-10600858.summary: A funerary epitaph for Sarracina, who lived approximately 34 years, set up by her sons, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10600860.translation: Here rests in peace Scotto, who lived 65 years. His sweetest wife placed this monument out of love. Peace be with you, Scotte.
EDCS-10600860.summary: A funerary epitaph for Scotto, who lived 65 years, placed by his wife with a wish for peace, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10600862.text_edition: \n Sedatus et Paulina patres dulcissimae filiae Dunamiolae titulum posuerunt quae vixit annos tres et menses quinque et dies viginti\n
EDCS-10600862.translation: Sedatus and Paulina placed this monument for their most beloved daughter Dunamiola, who lived three years, five months, and twenty days.
EDCS-10600862.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young girl named Dunamiola, set up by her parents Sedatus and Paulina.

EDCS-10600864.translation: Sucio rests here, who lived [unknown age].
EDCS-10600864.summary: A fragmentary funerary epitaph for a person named Sucio, possibly with a missing age and name.

EDCS-10600865.translation: [Unknown name] rests here, who lived 3 years and 2 months. Mocdo[?] and [?]ima placed this monument.
EDCS-10600865.summary: A funerary epitaph for an individual with an incomplete name, set up by Mocdo[?] and [?]ima.

EDCS-10600867.translation: Valentinus rests here, who lived 38 years. Marontius the father, Agricia the wife, and his sons placed this monument.
EDCS-10600867.summary: A funerary epitaph for Valentinus, set up by his father Marontius, wife Agricia, and sons.

EDCS-10600869.translation: Valentinus in peace [unknown details] who lived 50 years. Tala[?] car[?].
EDCS-10600869.summary: A fragmentary funerary epitaph for Valentinus, indicating he lived 50 years.

EDCS-10600871.translation: Valentina rests here faithfully in peace, who lived 29 years and 5 months. Virginius Germanio, her kinsman, and his sons placed this monument out of affection.
EDCS-10600871.summary: A funerary epitaph for Valentina, set up by her kinsman Virginius Germanio and his sons.

EDCS-10600872.translation: ]oris for the sweetest infant resting here, who lived two years, ten months, and thirteen days. Victor and Florentina, most devoted parents, placed this monument with peace.
EDCS-10600872.summary: A funerary epitaph for a sweet infant who lived two years, ten months, and thirteen days, set up by parents Victor and Florentina.

EDCS-10600874.translation: Widargildus rests here in peace, [having lived] 7 years and [unknown details] of Saint Maximinus.
EDCS-10600874.summary: A fragmentary funerary epitaph for Widargildus, indicating he lived 7 years and possibly associated with Saint Maximinus.

EDCS-10600875.translation: Cavo Vigur rests here faithfully in peace, his son placed this monument for his most devoted father out of affection.
EDCS-10600875.summary: A funerary epitaph for Cavo Vigur, set up by his son.

EDCS-10600876.translation: Vitalis, Elearius, Codora, and Cofilus Vitalinius and Codora rest innocently in peace.
EDCS-10600876.summary: A funerary epitaph recording multiple individuals, possibly family members, resting in peace.

EDCS-10600877.translation: Here rests in peace one who lived 8 years and 5 months, whom Vinardus the father and Luperca the mother placed [this] monument for their child.
EDCS-10600877.summary: A funerary epitaph for a child, placed by their parents.

EDCS-10600878.translation: Ursa the mother placed this monument for her beloved. Here rests in peace Simplicia. Here rests Victorina, who lived 50 years.
EDCS-10600878.summary: A funerary epitaph for two women, Simplicia and Victorina, with Victorina's age given and the monument placed by Ursa.

EDCS-10600879.translation: Here lies Ursa, who lived 7 years and 10 months. Urso and Romula, parents, placed this monument for her, born/buried on the Ides of August.
EDCS-10600879.summary: A funerary epitaph for a child named Ursa, placed by her parents, with the date of birth/burial specified.

EDCS-10600881.translation: Ursio, may you live in God.
EDCS-10600881.summary: A short inscription wishing the deceased Ursio eternal life in God.

EDCS-10600882.translation: Here rests in peace Ursulla, who lived 21 years. Artula the dear mother placed this monument.
EDCS-10600882.summary: A funerary epitaph for a woman named Ursulla, placed by her mother.

EDCS-10600895.summary: A fragmentary funerary epitaph with illegible names and missing context.

EDCS-10600922.translation: [---]atius, [---] 24 [---] for the year 1 and 10 months, [---] the 2nd day before the Nones of November, [---] November.
EDCS-10600922.summary: A fragmentary inscription that appears to record a date and possibly a duration of life or service.

EDCS-10600941.text_edition: \n Deo Silvano Sinquati Paternius pro salute Emeriti fili sui votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10600941.translation: To the god Silvanus, Paternius fulfilled his vow for the health of his son Emeritus, willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-10600941.summary: A votive inscription dedicated to the god Silvanus by Paternius for his son's well-being.

EDCS-10600942.text_edition: \n Deo Sinquato Lucius Honoratius Aunus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10600942.translation: To the god Sinquatus, Lucius Honoratius Aunus fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-10600942.summary: A votive inscription dedicated to the god Sinquatus by Lucius Honoratius Aunus.

EDCS-10600943.text_edition: \n Leno Marti Exsobinii Novicius et Expectatus votum solverunt libentes merito\n
EDCS-10600943.translation: To the god Mars Exsobinni, Novicius and Expectatus fulfilled their vows willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-10600943.summary: A votive inscription dedicated to the god Mars Exsobinni by Novicius and Expectatus.

EDCS-10600945.summary: This is a dedication by Poppus, likely to a deity or for a public work.

EDCS-10600946.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription indicating that Cesius Cinianus commissioned the object or structure.

EDCS-10600947.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed, Satto.
EDCS-10600947.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the 'Dis Manibus' (Spirits of the Departed) for Satto.

EDCS-10600952.text_edition: \n Lucio Solimario Thannissae Titussiae Gnatae uxori vivae Atrectino filio Dannumara filia heres fecit\n
EDCS-10600952.translation: Titussia Gnatae, wife of Lucio Solimario Thannissa, and Atrectinus, son, and Dannumara, daughter, being his heirs, made this monument while he was alive.
EDCS-10600952.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by heirs for Lucio Solimario Thannissa, indicating its construction during his lifetime.

EDCS-10600953.text_edition: \n Marti Camulo Lellius votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10600953.translation: Lellius paid his vow to Mars Camulus, willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-10600953.summary: This is a votive inscription recording Lellius fulfilling a promise to the god Mars Camulus.

EDCS-10600956.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Gai Iuli Maximini emeriti legionis VIII beneficiarius procuratoris honesta missione missus ista memoriam procuravit Similinia Paterna coniux coniugi karissimo Maximinus ic quiesquit ave viator vale viator\n
EDCS-10600956.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Gaius Iulius Maximinus, a retired soldier ('emeritus') of the Eighth Legion, a beneficiary of the procurator, who was honorably discharged, Similinia Paterna, his wife, provided this memorial for her most dear husband. Maximinus rests here. Farewell, traveler, fare you well, traveler.
EDCS-10600956.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Iulius Maximinus, provided by his wife, detailing his military service and retirement.

EDCS-10600957.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Andecari Nocturni et Miccioniae Cuigillae Censorinius Andecarus filio et coiiugi fecit\n
EDCS-10600957.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Censorinius Andecarus made this for his son and wife, Nocturnus Andecarus and Micconia Cuigilla.
EDCS-10600957.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Censorinius Andecarus for his son and wife, honoring the deceased.

EDCS-10600958.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed, Atillia Abba.
EDCS-10600958.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Atillia Abba.

EDCS-10600959.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus illius defuncti Attilius Regulus patronus idemque heres vivus fecit Dis Manibus patroni sui faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-10600959.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For that deceased person, Attilius Regulus, patron and also heir, while alive, took care to have this made for his patron.
EDCS-10600959.summary: This funerary inscription records Attilius Regulus, who was both patron and heir, commissioning a monument for his deceased patron.

EDCS-10600960.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Cnaeo Avio Bovo defuncto Sextina Cai filia fecit\n
EDCS-10600960.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Sextina, daughter of Caius, made this for her deceased husband, Cnaeus Avvius Bovo.
EDCS-10600960.summary: This is a funerary epitaph provided by Sextina for her deceased husband, Cnaeus Avvius Bovo.

EDCS-10600961.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Boutius Alctus sibi et Coppo fratri vivus fecit\n
EDCS-10600961.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Boutius Alctus made this for himself and his brother Coppo while still alive.
EDCS-10600961.summary: This funerary epitaph records a self-funded tomb erected by Boutius Alctus for himself and his brother.

EDCS-10600963.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Cattonius Secundinus et Sappula uxor IDIEIRE faciundum \n
EDCS-10600963.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Cattonius Secundinus and his wife Sappula had this made.
EDCS-10600963.summary: This funerary inscription records a monument commissioned by Cattonius Secundinus and his wife Sappula.

EDCS-10600964.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Cidionius Amretoutus sibi vivus fecit\n
EDCS-10600964.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Cidionius Amretoutus made this for himself while still alive.
EDCS-10600964.summary: This funerary epitaph records a self-funded tomb erected by Cidionius Amretoutus.

EDCS-10600965.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Corobillio Pautoni et Pruscia Motto coniugibus Mottus\n
EDCS-10600965.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Corobillio Pautoni and Pruscia Motto, husband and wife, Mottus made this.
EDCS-10600965.summary: This funerary inscription records a monument made by Mottus for his parents, Corobillio Pautoni and Pruscia Motto.

EDCS-10600966.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Danni Sextina Desiderata filia faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-10600966.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Sextina Desiderata, daughter of Danni, saw to the making of this.
EDCS-10600966.summary: This funerary epitaph records a monument commissioned by Sextina Desiderata for her deceased relatives.

EDCS-10600967.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Donillae coniugi Cosuonius Acceptus\n
EDCS-10600967.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For his wife Donillae. Cosuonius Acceptus.
EDCS-10600967.summary: This funerary inscription records a tomb dedicated by Cosuonius Acceptus to his wife Donillae.

EDCS-10600968.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Gimmius Manduissa sibi et Ammossa vivus fecit\n
EDCS-10600968.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Gimmius Manduissa made this for himself and Ammossa while still alive.
EDCS-10600968.summary: This funerary epitaph records a self-funded tomb erected by Gimmius Manduissa for himself and Ammossa.

EDCS-10600969.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Ibliomariae Sacrae defunctae Giamillia Giamilla filia viva fecit\n
EDCS-10600969.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Ibliomaria Sacra, deceased. Giamillia, daughter of Giamilla, made this while alive.
EDCS-10600969.summary: This funerary inscription records a tomb erected by Giamillia for her deceased mother, Ibliomaria Sacra.

EDCS-10600970.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Iunius Iustinus Maternus vivus fecit\n
EDCS-10600970.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Iunius Iustinus Maternus made this while alive.
EDCS-10600970.summary: This funerary epitaph records a self-funded tomb erected by Iunius Iustinus Maternus.

EDCS-10600972.translation: [To the spirits of the departed.] For Lucaniae / Adiatumar(ae) [.]
EDCS-10600972.summary: This fragmentary funerary inscription records a dedication to a female, likely deceased, named Lucaniae Adiatumarae.

EDCS-10600973.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Marcelliniae Afrae coniugi defunctae Gratinius Acceptus et sibi vivos sicfecit\n
EDCS-10600973.translation: To the departed spirits. For Marcellinia Afra, my deceased wife, Gratinius Acceptus made this monument for her and for himself while alive.
EDCS-10600973.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Gratinius Acceptus for his deceased wife Marcellinia Afra and himself.

EDCS-10600974.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Messiae Donatae matri Iustus filius vivus faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-10600974.translation: To the departed spirits. For Messia Donata, my mother, Iustus, my son, had this made while alive.
EDCS-10600974.summary: This funerary epitaph records that Iustus commissioned a monument for his mother, Messia Donata.

EDCS-10600975.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragmentary funerary epitaph with personal names.

EDCS-10600976.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus monumentum Iuni Pessiaci et Iulio Mavillo \n
EDCS-10600976.translation: To the departed spirits. A monument for Iunius Pessiaccus and Iulius Mavillus.
EDCS-10600976.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating a monument to Iunius Pessiaccus and Iulius Mavillus.

EDCS-10600977.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Primanio Aprili et Primanio Saturnino Primanius Saturninus vivus sibi et suis vivis fecit\n
EDCS-10600977.translation: To the departed spirits. Primanius Saturninus made this while alive for himself, for Primanius Aprilis, and for Primanius Saturninus, while they were alive.
EDCS-10600977.summary: This funerary epitaph records Primanius Saturninus commissioning a monument for himself and others while alive.

EDCS-10600978.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Primanio Primtivo defuncto et Mato coniugi fili faciendum curaverunt\n
EDCS-10600978.translation: To the departed spirits. For Primanius Primitivus, deceased, and Mato, his wife, the sons had this made.
EDCS-10600978.summary: This funerary inscription states that sons commissioned a monument for their deceased father Primanius Primitivus and his wife Mato.

EDCS-10600979.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Primulio Pardo defuncto et suis herens faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-10600979.translation: To the departed spirits. For Primulius Pardo, deceased, and his heirs, [name] had this made.
EDCS-10600979.summary: This funerary epitaph records that someone commissioned a monument for Primulius Pardo and his heirs.

EDCS-10600980.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Primi Prissonis et Prusciae Maianae uxori viva Viducus filius fecit et Similiae Satiae (et) Bimottia Nequigo\n
EDCS-10600980.translation: To the departed spirits. Viducus, son, made this alive for Primi Prissonis and for Pruscia Maiana, his wife, and for Similia Satia (and) Bimottia Nequigo.
EDCS-10600980.summary: This funerary epitaph records Viducus commissioning a monument for his parents Primi Prissonis and Pruscia Maiana, and others.

EDCS-10600981.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Prusciae Losuarcae Iolsius Secundinus uxori et sibi vivos sic fecit\n
EDCS-10600981.translation: To the departed spirits. Iolsius Secundinus made this alive for Pruscia Losuarca, his wife, and for himself.
EDCS-10600981.summary: This funerary epitaph records Iolsius Secundinus commissioning a monument for his wife Pruscia Losuarca and himself.

EDCS-10600982.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Prusci Magionis et Tertiniai Cossulae coiiugi sic vivae Acaunissa filius fecit\n
EDCS-10600982.translation: To the departed spirits. Acaunissa, son, made this alive for Priscus Magio and Tertinia Cossula, his wife.
EDCS-10600982.summary: This funerary epitaph states that Acaunissa commissioned a monument for his father Priscus Magio and his mother Tertinia Cossula.

EDCS-10600983.text_edition: \n Secundinus Seccalus Secundinae coniugi et Seccaliae Secundinae filiae et sibi vivos sic fecit Dis Manibus\n
EDCS-10600983.translation: Secundinus Seccalus made this for his wife Secundina and his daughter Seccalia Secundina, and for himself while alive. To the departed spirits.
EDCS-10600983.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Secundinus Seccalus for his wife and daughter, and for himself, dating likely to the Imperial period.

EDCS-10600984.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Severiae Martiae Tonnia Gabra filia sua de suo fecit\n
EDCS-10600984.translation: To the departed spirits. Tonnia Gabra made this for her daughter Severia Martia, from her own resources.
EDCS-10600984.summary: A funerary dedication by Tonnia Gabra for her daughter Severia Martia, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-10600985.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Soiianus fecit Sollemni filio et patri Soiio et Primia Tauso matri\n
EDCS-10600985.translation: To the departed spirits. Soiianus made this for his son Sollemnius, and for his father Soius, and for his mother Primia Tausa.
EDCS-10600985.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by Soiianus for his son, father, and mother, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-10600986.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Sollio Viconis et Similia \n
EDCS-10600986.translation: To the departed spirits. For Sollio, son of Vico, and for Similia.
EDCS-10600986.summary: A funerary dedication to Sollio Viconis and Similia, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-10600987.translation: To the departed spirits. For Telionnus, son of Caulnus.
EDCS-10600987.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Telionnus, son of Caulnus, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-10600988.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Terti Primilla patri fecit\n
EDCS-10600988.translation: To the departed spirits. Primilla made this for her father Tertius.
EDCS-10600988.summary: A funerary inscription by Primilla for her father Tertius, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-10600989.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Tornioneius Imunnis et coniugi Iulinia Popillus \n
EDCS-10600989.translation: To the departed spirits. For Tornioneius Imunnis and for his wife Iulia Popillus.
EDCS-10600989.summary: A funerary dedication for Tornioneius Imunnis and his wife Iulia Popillus, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-10600990.translation: [To the departed spirits.] For Verecundus, son of Verecundus, and for Ver[e]cundia, daughter of Verecundus.
EDCS-10600990.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription likely from the Imperial period, commemorating Verecundus and Verēcundia.

EDCS-10600991.translation: [To the departed spirits.] ...cenia, his wife; Verecundus, son of Sistius; and [...]
EDCS-10600991.summary: A fragmented funerary inscription, possibly from the Imperial period, mentioning a woman and Verecundus.

EDCS-10600993.translation: [To the departed spirits.] AE ETA[---] daughter of them, and CE[---] Materna I F[---]
EDCS-10600993.summary: A very fragmentary inscription, possibly funerary, from the Imperial period, mentioning individuals and their relationship.

EDCS-10600997.translation: Viena erected this for her wife, [---]ius.
EDCS-10600997.summary: This funerary inscription records Viena dedicating a monument to her wife, though much of the text is lost.

EDCS-10601001.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus ndio Senili Optato filio heres sibi vivus fecit\n
EDCS-10601001.translation: To the spirits of the departed. A descendant, Senilia Optata, made this for herself while alive, for her son.
EDCS-10601001.summary: This is a funerary inscription with a dedication to departed spirits, likely indicating a family tomb erected by Senilia Optata for her son.

EDCS-10601004.translation: For Aturiacius Primulus and his wife Magiona.
EDCS-10601004.summary: This inscription appears to be a funerary dedication to Aturiacius Primulus and his wife Magiona.

EDCS-10601005.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Sennius Maior, the deceased, her wife Sa[---]a made this for herself while alive.
EDCS-10601005.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Sennius Maior, erected by his wife who also made provisions for herself.

EDCS-10601012.translation: Corinthia V[---]ata ordered this to be placed for herself by will. Caius Crescentius [---]itus, her son.
EDCS-10601012.summary: This inscription records Corinthia's posthumous arrangement for a monument to be erected for her, as stipulated in her will.

EDCS-10601014.translation: [---]cipius, while alive, took care to have this made for himself and for Claudia Mossa, deceased.
EDCS-10601014.summary: This inscription indicates that [---]cipius arranged for a monument for himself and his deceased wife, Claudia Mossa.

EDCS-10601015.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Immunia Viscareva [---]ieliari, while alive, made this for Paternio and for herself and for his wife Aturena.
EDCS-10601015.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Immunia Viscareva, who while alive, erected the monument for Paternio, herself, and his wife Aturena.

EDCS-10601016.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Junius Secundus, Volia Prima and [---].
EDCS-10601016.summary: This is an incomplete funerary inscription dedicated to Junius Secundus by Volia Prima.

EDCS-10601019.translation: To the gods of the underworld. Tessillinius Carantinus fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-10601019.summary: This inscription records Tessillinius Carantinus fulfilling a votive offering to the underworld gods.

EDCS-10601021.translation: To Mars. Vegnius Adiutor, son of Sollius, fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-10601021.summary: This inscription records Vegnius Adiutor, son of Sollius, fulfilling a votive offering to the god Mars.

EDCS-10601022.translation: Sacred to the god Mercury, in honor of the divine house. Adiutor and 3inusa willingly and deservedly placed [this].
EDCS-10601022.summary: This is a dedication to the god Mercury by Adiutor and 3inusa, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-10601028.text_edition: \n Deae Victoriae Victoria Vitalis votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10601028.translation: Victoria Vitalis willingly and deservedly paid her vow to the goddess Victory.
EDCS-10601028.summary: This is a votive dedication to the goddess Victory by Victoria Vitalis.

EDCS-10601030.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Acceptus and 3enus, sons of 3sinius, [dedicated this] for themselves and [---].
EDCS-10601030.summary: This is a tomb inscription dedicated to Acceptus and 3enus, sons of 3sinius, for themselves and others.

EDCS-10601031.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Amma, daughter and heir of Coco Sintorix, took care to have this made.
EDCS-10601031.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Coco Sintorix, with the monument prepared by his daughter and heir, Amma.

EDCS-10601032.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Germania [dedicated this] for Germania, who has died, [---] living [---].
EDCS-10601032.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Germania, set up by someone also named Germania.

EDCS-10601035.translation: Secundius [dedicated this] for his brother, while alive.
EDCS-10601035.summary: This is a dedication by Secundius for his living brother.

EDCS-10601051.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Servatus and Thalia, parents, [dedicated this] for their deceased son, Sereno.
EDCS-10601051.summary: This is a tomb inscription set up by parents, Servatus and Thalia, for their deceased son, Sereno.

EDCS-10601052.translation: [---]EVIIAMA, Efuti, Ad [---] and co-heirs took care to have [this] made.
EDCS-10601052.summary: This is a funerary inscription where co-heirs, including Efuti and Ad[---], arranged for the monument's construction.

EDCS-10601056.translation: Ditias, slave(?) of Gallus Classicianus, made [this].
EDCS-10601056.summary: This inscription records that Ditias, a slave of Gallus Classicianus, made the monument.

EDCS-10601057.translation: To the spirits of the departed. [---] Scyrus [made this] for [---].
EDCS-10601057.summary: This is a tomb inscription, likely a dedication by Scyrus for one or more individuals.

EDCS-10601060.translation: To the departed spirits. Atto and [---]sti, sons of Miccon, while alive made [this for them].
EDCS-10601060.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to departed spirits, with the dedicants identified as Atto and [---]sti, sons of Miccon.

EDCS-10601063.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, possibly a dedication or funerary text, mentioning a name that may be Mascellus.

EDCS-10601067.summary: This is a very fragmented inscription, likely a personal name, possibly Titus Au[---] Secundus.

EDCS-10601069.translation: [---]io and IVS[---] MALIVT[---] IOV[---] to his wife(?) [---] of Massa[---] as a IVIR.
EDCS-10601069.summary: This fragmentary inscription appears to be part of a dedication or funerary text, mentioning a wife and a position as a IVIR (a type of magistrate).

EDCS-10601070.translation: To the departed spirits. Secundinia [erected this] for her deceased husband, Gallionius Planctus.
EDCS-10601070.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Secundinia for her deceased husband, Gallionius Planctus.

EDCS-10601071.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely naming Gaius Sattonius.

EDCS-10601072.summary: This is a very brief inscription, possibly a funerary marker or dedication, mentioning 'Elox' and 'mother'.

EDCS-10601074.translation: To the departed spirits. Cletussto Ver[---] deceased and Eburia M[---] for [her/his] wife while alive [---].
EDCS-10601074.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Cletussto Ver[---] and Eburia M[---], possibly a married couple.

EDCS-10601075.text_edition: \n Deae Dianae Quintus Postumius Potens votum solvit\n
EDCS-10601075.translation: Quintus Postumius Potens fulfilled his vow to the goddess Diana.
EDCS-10601075.summary: This is a votive inscription where Quintus Postumius Potens dedicates something to the goddess Diana.

EDCS-10601076.translation: To the departed spirits. Riceno and Vinnia [---] erected [this] for their deceased [relative?], Arrius Gaippus.
EDCS-10601076.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Riceno and Vinnia for the deceased Arrius Gaippus.

EDCS-10601077.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Attucia Artilla and Acceptia Tasgilla, and her son (?), Sattonius Secundinus, for themselves [made this monument].
EDCS-10601077.summary: This is a funerary inscription likely for Attucia Artilla and Acceptia Tasgilla, set up by Sattonius Secundinus.

EDCS-10601078.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the name and age at death of Cabilonnus.

EDCS-10601079.translation: To Marciana Victorina, his departed wife. Her husband Tetius Secundus and their son Secundius Ursio, while alive, made this for her and for themselves.
EDCS-10601079.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Tetius Secundus and his son Secundius Ursio for Marciana Victorina.

EDCS-10601081.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Urbio Sat[...].
EDCS-10601081.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription mentioning the name Urbio Sat[...].

EDCS-10601083.summary: This is a dedication to the deity Artio, whose father was Biber.

EDCS-10601084.summary: This is likely a funerary inscription or a simple label identifying Tertius Tertinius Ursulus.

EDCS-10601085.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Iuno, mentioning her father Quintus.

EDCS-10601086.translation: To Mercury. Lucius Iunetius Geminus [dedicated this].
EDCS-10601086.summary: This is a dedication to the god Mercury by Lucius Iunetius Geminus.

EDCS-10601089.text_edition: \n Marti Smertulitano et Ancamnae Caius G Sec \n
EDCS-10601089.translation: To Smertulitanus Mars and Ancamna. Caius G Sec [dedicated this].
EDCS-10601089.summary: This is a dedication to the deities Mars Smertulitanus and Ancamna by Caius G Sec.

EDCS-10601091.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Primanius Ursulus, his excellent freedman.
EDCS-10601091.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Primanius Ursulus, the excellent freedman of an unnamed patron.

EDCS-10601093.text_edition: \n Deo Mercurio sacrum Sautus Novialchi filius aedes duas cum suis ornamentis et triburnalia votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10601093.translation: Sacred to the god Mercury. Sautus, son of Novialchus, gratefully and deservedly paid his vow, dedicating two shrines with their furnishings and rooms for the celebration of games.
EDCS-10601093.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the god Mercury by Sautus, son of Novialchus, who fulfilled a vow by dedicating shrines and furnishings, likely in the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-10601094.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Heirs [---] made (this).
EDCS-10601094.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Anisatius Titus and his wife Secundia Carata, erected by their heirs, probably from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-10601095.text_edition: \n Mercurio sacrum Indutius Veriugus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10601095.translation: Sacred to Mercury. Indutius Veriugus gratefully and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-10601095.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to the god Mercury by Indutius Veriugus, likely from a provincial area and dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-10601096.translation: Of Marcus Iovincatus Sumaronis and his wife Sollia Abdugissa.
EDCS-10601096.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely recording the names of a couple, Marcus Iovincatus Sumaronis and his wife Sollia Abdugissa, possibly part of a tomb or dedication, from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-10601097.translation: Sacred to the god Intarabus. Quintus Solimarius Bitus consecrated a shrine with its furnishings by order, gratefully and deservedly.
EDCS-10601097.summary: This inscription records the consecration of a shrine to the god Intarabus by Quintus Solimarius Bitus, acting on divine command, likely from Roman Britain and dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-10601099.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deo Mercurio Vassocaleti Mandalonius Gratus donum dedit\n
EDCS-10601099.translation: In honor of the divine house, Mandalonius Gratus gave a gift to the god Mercury Vassocaletus.
EDCS-10601099.summary: This inscription records a gift to the god Mercury Vassocaletus, made in honor of the imperial family, by Mandalonius Gratus, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-10601100.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae numinibus Auggustorum faraburem exaedificaverunt suo i<m=N>pendio iuniores vici hic consistentes loco sibi concesso et donato a vikanis Bedensibus dedicatum effectum I Idus Iulias Imperatore domino nostro Phili[ppo] Augusto et Titianio consulibus [tioii e]t Secundio Secu \n
EDCS-10601100.translation: In honor of the divine house and the divine spirits of the Emperors, the young men living in this neighborhood, at their own expense, built a building, on land granted and donated to them by the villagers of Bedens, dedicated and completed on the Ides of July, during the consulship of our lord the Emperor Philippus Augustus and Titianus, [by Tiostios and] Secundio Secundus.
EDCS-10601100.summary: This inscription records the construction of a building by the local youth in honor of the imperial family and divine emperors, funded by the villagers of Bedens, and dedicated on July 13th during the consulship of Philippus and Titianus (244 CE).

EDCS-10601101.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae et Numinibus Auggustorum Iovi Optimo Maximo Lucius Ammiatius Gamburio proscaenium cum tribunali et eo amplius |(denarios) L ex quorum usuris tutelam proscaenii et ludos omnibus annis pridie Kalendas Maias curatores vici procurare debebunt fidei mandavit dedicatum Saturnino et Gallo consulibus\n
EDCS-10601101.translation: In honor of the divine house and the divine spirits of the Emperors. Lucius Ammiatius Gamburio provided a stage with a platform and more, for 50 denarii, to Jupiter Optimus Maximus; from the income of which the curators of the neighborhood shall be responsible for the maintenance of the stage and games every year on the day before the Kalends of May. He entrusted this to the loyalty of the board; dedicated during the consulship of Saturninus and Gallus (221 CE).
EDCS-10601101.summary: This inscription records a dedication of funds by Lucius Ammiatius Gamburio to Jupiter Optimus Maximus for the maintenance of a stage and the funding of games in perpetuity, dedicated in 221 CE.

EDCS-10601104.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Suommoius.
EDCS-10601104.summary: This is a short funerary inscription for Suommoius, dedicated to the spirits of the departed, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-10601111.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deo Caprioni Lucius Teddiatius Primus\n
EDCS-10601111.translation: In honor of the divine house, Lucius Teddiatius Primus [dedicated this] to the god Caprio.
EDCS-10601111.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the god Caprio in honor of the imperial family by Lucius Teddiatius Primus, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-10601113.translation: To Amme[nius?] for [his?] son IV[---] and D[---], [he?] made it.
EDCS-10601113.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription, likely recording a dedication made by a parent for their son, with incomplete names and relationship details.

EDCS-10601114.text_edition: \n Messionius Vitalis fecit sibi vivus annorum LX\n
EDCS-10601114.translation: Messionius Vitalis made this for himself alive, aged 60.
EDCS-10601114.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Messionius Vitalis, who commissioned it during his lifetime and recorded his age at death.

EDCS-10601115.translation: To the god Apollo Inecius of Iassi.
EDCS-10601115.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription to the god Apollo Inecius, likely from the region of Iassos.

EDCS-10601118.text_edition: \n Caivae deae aedem omni sua impensa donavit Marcus Victorius Pollentinus et ob perpetuam tutelam eiusdem aedis dedit HS nummum C dedicatum III Nonas Octobres Glabrione et Torquato consulibus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10601118.translation: Marcus Victorius Pollentinus dedicated the temple to the goddess Caivae with all his own expense and for her perpetual protection he gave 100 sesterces; he paid his vow willingly and deservedly, dedicated on the 3rd day before the Nones of October in the consulship of Glabrio and Torquatus.
EDCS-10601118.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription by Marcus Victorius Pollentinus to the goddess Caivae, detailing the expenses for the temple construction and a monetary donation, dated to 90 AD.

EDCS-10601121.translation: To the spirits of the departed Aprosso[s?], former Augustalis, and his wife Saturnina, and [their children?], and [names illegible], for Aquilonis and Iatossa, deceased, Apros[s]ius Ursicius made this for his fathers, mothers, and himself while alive.
EDCS-10601121.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aprosso[s], an Augustalis, and his wife Saturnina, as well as other deceased individuals, commissioned by Apros[s]ius Ursicius for his ancestors and himself.

EDCS-10601124.translation: To the spirits of the departed Capit[on], son of Publi[u]s, a merchant, his heir arranged for this to be made.
EDCS-10601124.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Capit[on], son of Publi[u]s, a merchant, with the heir responsible for arranging the monument's construction.

EDCS-10601125.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning Lucius Securius [---]tus, a merchant, likely part of a larger monument or epitaph.

EDCS-10601127.translation: Caius Albinius Asper made this for Secundia Restituta, his wife, and [for himself?] while alive.
EDCS-10601127.summary: This is a funerary inscription commissioned by Caius Albinius Asper for his wife Secundia Restituta and possibly himself.

EDCS-10601128.translation: To the spirits of the departed Marcus Ammutius Ollognatus for himself and his deceased wife Atussia Anna, and for Ollognatio Secundus, their son, and his wife Devillia Amillo PI[---]
EDCS-10601128.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Ammutius Ollognatus, his wife Atussia Anna, their son Ollognatio Secundus, and his wife Devillia Amillo, indicating a family burial.

EDCS-10601130.translation: [for---] deceased and for Artima, daughter [---], and [---]dulto NIEM[---]
EDCS-10601130.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, possibly funerary, mentioning deceased individuals named Artima and others with incomplete names.

EDCS-10601131.translation: Ateforus made this for his deceased wife Severa and for himself while alive.
EDCS-10601131.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Ateforus for his wife Severa, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-10601132.translation: Securius Novellus arranged for this to be made for his father Securio Atepo, his brother Securius Novianus, and his mother Iulia.
EDCS-10601132.summary: A funerary monument commissioned by Securius Novellus for his deceased father, brother, and mother.

EDCS-10601133.summary: A fragmentary inscription that appears to record personal names, possibly funerary or commemorative.

EDCS-10601134.translation: To the departed spirits. Primionius, son of Lucius Cobrovvius Primio and Papinia Krilla, his wife, made this [---]
EDCS-10601134.summary: A dedication to the underworld gods (Dis Manibus) for Lucius Cobrovvius Primio and his wife Papinia Krilla, commissioned by their son Primionius.

EDCS-10601135.translation: To the departed spirits. He dedicated this title alive for Lucius Cossacionius Porcellus, deceased, and for Sacrila Sacrilea, his wife, and for himself and his family.
EDCS-10601135.summary: A funerary dedication made while alive by an individual for his deceased husband Lucius Cossacionius Porcellus and his wife Sacrila Sacrilea, and for their family.

EDCS-10601136.translation: Gimmionius Gariolus and Gimmonia Aestiva, children and heirs, arranged for this to be made for [name] deceased and for his wife Iunia Cariola.
EDCS-10601136.summary: A funerary monument commissioned by the children and heirs Gimmionius Gariolus and Gimmonia Aestiva for a deceased man and his wife Iunia Cariola.

EDCS-10601137.translation: To the departed spirits. The heir arranged for this to be made for Lettius Seranus and Annita, his wife.
EDCS-10601137.summary: A funerary dedication arranged by an heir for Lettius Seranus and his wife Annita.

EDCS-10601138.summary: A very brief inscription identifying Marcus Lucius as both a freedman and an heir.

EDCS-10601139.translation: [name] and Masclia Magna and Luca [---] Musicus Romogillus [---] next to PROR [---]
EDCS-10601139.summary: A fragmentary inscription that appears to list several names, possibly in a funerary or commemorative context.

EDCS-10601140.translation: To the departed spirits. Peculinius Motuacus Secco [---] [---]
EDCS-10601140.summary: A funerary dedication to the underworld gods for Peculinius Motuacus and others.

EDCS-10601142.translation: Titus Julius Eutychianus made this for his well-deserving wife, [A]urnia Secundina, his freedwoman, and for himself while alive.
EDCS-10601142.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by a husband for his wife and himself, likely dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-10601145.translation: To the departed spirits. Securius Lalissus and Capitonia Lala made this for their departed sons Sextus, Tertinus, and Amma, and for themselves while alive.
EDCS-10601145.summary: This funerary inscription records parents dedicating a monument for their deceased children and themselves, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-10601146.translation: To the departed spirits. Acceptius Varusius and Totia Lalla, parents, and Varusius Atto, their deceased son, and themselves made this while alive.
EDCS-10601146.summary: This is a funerary inscription from parents dedicating a tomb for their deceased son and themselves, probably from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-10601147.text_edition: \n coniugi Severinae et Varisto filio defunctis Primionius\n
EDCS-10601147.translation: For his wife Severina and his deceased son Varisto.
EDCS-10601147.summary: This is a fragment of a funerary inscription mentioning a wife and a deceased son, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-10601148.translation: Victor Vabilis and Ivenilia, parents, saw to the making of this for themselves while alive.
EDCS-10601148.summary: This funerary monument was prepared by parents for themselves while alive, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-10601149.translation: Soratia (?) Prudentia and herself, while alive, saw to the making of this for her deceased mother Matrona, her deceased uncle Vitalis, and her parents.
EDCS-10601149.summary: This funerary inscription records a woman dedicating a monument for her deceased mother, uncle, parents, and herself, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-10601157.summary: This is a fragment of a funerary inscription, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-10601158.translation: Potentinus made this for himself while alive.
EDCS-10601158.summary: This funerary inscription records an individual dedicating a monument for himself while alive, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-10601159.translation: [---] children and Secundinius and Ingenuia Decmina, and Secundinia Afra (?).
EDCS-10601159.summary: This is a fragment of a funerary inscription possibly listing family members, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-10601161.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deo Mercurio et Rosmertae Docci Aprossus et Acceptus IIIIIIviri Augustales votum solverunt libentes merito\n
EDCS-10601161.translation: In honor of the divine house, Docci Aprossus and Acceptus, IIII viri Augustales, paid their vow willingly and deservedly to the god Mercury and Rosmerta.
EDCS-10601161.summary: This inscription records a vow paid by four Augustales officials to Mercury and Rosmerta in honor of the imperial family, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-10601163.translation: In honor of the divine house, to the god Mercury and the goddess Rosmerta, Mercurialis, freedman of Augustus, assistant to the registrar, has gladly paid his deserved vow.
EDCS-10601163.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Mercury and Rosmerta by an imperial freedman.

EDCS-10601168.translation: To the departed spirits of Primulus, infant son of Sequentis, and of Primula.
EDCS-10601168.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for a deceased infant and his mother.

EDCS-10601169.translation: To the departed spirits. Publius Firmius Covirus, while alive, made this for himself and for Sittia Anna, his deceased wife.
EDCS-10601169.summary: This is a tombstone inscription made by a man for himself and his late wife.

EDCS-10601171.translation: To the departed spirits. Lucius Apronius Secco, while alive, made this for himself.
EDCS-10601171.summary: This is a tombstone inscription made by a man for himself.

EDCS-10601174.translation: To the departed spirits. His brothers, with the procurator Sira overseeing, took care to have this made for Maiorius Ianuarius. Maiorius Acceptus also made this for himself and for Censonia Prima, while alive.
EDCS-10601174.summary: This tombstone inscription records the building of a monument by brothers for their deceased brother and also by Maiorius Acceptus for himself and his wife.

EDCS-10601176.translation: To the departed spirits. Lucius Senilius Sacratus, deceased father. Lucius Sacratius Sacrianus, Sacratius, and Sacrius, sons, made this for themselves and their families, while alive.
EDCS-10601176.summary: This tombstone inscription records a monument made by sons for their deceased father and their families.

EDCS-10601180.translation: In honor of the divine house. Tetricianius Serotinus gave a statue of Mercury as a gift to his brothers.
EDCS-10601180.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription of a statue to Mercury by Tetricianius Serotinus for his brothers.

EDCS-10601184.translation: To the departed spirits. Fructuosus and Aurelius Fructuosus the younger, their son, took care to have this made while alive. To the departed spirits. Fructuosus and Aurelius Fructuosus the younger, their son, took care to have this made.
EDCS-10601184.summary: This tombstone inscription records a monument made by a father and son for themselves.

EDCS-10601185.summary: This is a fragmentary tombstone inscription, likely recording a name.

EDCS-10601186.translation: To the departed spirits. Poppius Secundinus made this for himself and his family.
EDCS-10601186.summary: This is a tombstone inscription made by a man for himself and his family.

EDCS-10601187.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Marcus Restionius Restitutus and Marcus Restitutius Aurorianus and Restitutia Auroriana made this for themselves while alive.
EDCS-10601187.summary: A funerary monument set up by Marcus Restionius Restitutus and his relatives for themselves during their lifetime.

EDCS-10601188.translation: To Iucundius, [about] BVCCIAII(?), [for] his wife D...
EDCS-10601188.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription, possibly dedicated to Iucundius and his wife.

EDCS-10601189.summary: A fragmentary inscription mentioning the deceased Lallius O...

EDCS-10601194.summary: A very fragmentary inscription with names that are difficult to reconstruct.

EDCS-10601195.summary: A fragmentary inscription mentioning two individuals named Vollio.

EDCS-10601196.translation: For Publius Sincoriius Dubitatus and Memoria Sacrilla, deceased parents, Dubitatus, Mensor, Moratus, and also for himself while alive.
EDCS-10601196.summary: A funerary monument dedicated to parents by their children, who also provided for themselves.

EDCS-10601197.translation: The colonists of Crutisium made this for the god Mercury from their own funds, through Dannus Giamillus.
EDCS-10601197.summary: A dedication to the god Mercury made by colonists from their own funds.

EDCS-10601198.text_edition: \n Carantiae coniugi Prisco Cani filio defunctis Lusia Iblia sibi et suis viva fecit\n
EDCS-10601198.translation: Lusia Iblia made this for her husband Priscus, son of Canius, and for herself and her family while alive.
EDCS-10601198.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by Lusia Iblia for her deceased husband and for herself and her family.

EDCS-10601199.translation: For Gaius Ripa, son of Gaius Ripani, grandson of Gaius Ripani, son of Artillus, [this was made] for himself and his family.
EDCS-10601199.summary: A funerary monument set up for Gaius Ripa and his family by himself while alive.

EDCS-10601203.translation: Here in peace rests Ursus, innocent, who lived for 3 years and 46 days.
EDCS-10601203.summary: A tombstone recording the short life of a child named Ursus.

EDCS-10601206.text_edition: \n Mercurio et Rosmertae Messor Cani libertus\n
EDCS-10601206.translation: To Mercury and Rosmerta, Messor, freedman of Canus.
EDCS-10601206.summary: This is a dedication to the gods Mercury and Rosmerta by Messor, a freedman.

EDCS-10601207.translation: The workshop of Aemilianus was begun on the Nones of March.
EDCS-10601207.summary: This inscription records the commencement of a workshop belonging to Aemilianus.

EDCS-10601208.translation: To Croelonia Sacrina, his deceased mother, her son Carantinius Vexillus [---] made this.
EDCS-10601208.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Carantinius Vexillus to his deceased mother, Croelonia Sacrina.

EDCS-10601210.translation: To the god Mercury Clement, Poppa willingly and deservedly fulfilled her vow.
EDCS-10601210.summary: This is a votive inscription to Mercury Clement by Poppa.

EDCS-10601211.text_edition: \n siaN Vectimarus vivos sic sibi et Privatiae Sincorillae coniugi et Edullio filio defunctis \n
EDCS-10601211.translation: Vectimarus, alive, erected this for himself and for his deceased wife Privatia Sincorilla and his deceased son Edullius.
EDCS-10601211.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Vectimarus for himself and his deceased wife and son.

EDCS-10601212.summary: This inscription likely records the weight of goods belonging to Publius Licinius Ruticus.

EDCS-10601213.translation: Germanius made [this] while alive for himself and for his wife Diucia.
EDCS-10601213.summary: This is a funerary monument commissioned by Germanius for himself and his wife Diucia.

EDCS-10601215.translation: To the departed gods. Acceptia Quigilla Talionium Lucilla had this made for her deceased mother.
EDCS-10601215.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Acceptia Quigilla Talionium Lucilla for her deceased mother.

EDCS-10601216.translation: To the departed gods. Marcus Catullius Martialis ordered this to be made in his will for himself and for his wife Drippia Martia. Martialius Restitutus [made it].
EDCS-10601216.summary: This is a funerary inscription commissioned in a will by Marcus Catullius Martialis for himself and his wife, executed by Martialius Restitutus.

EDCS-10601217.translation: Piraucobruna, alive, made [this] and set it up for the departed spirits of Atti, and for herself.
EDCS-10601217.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Piraucobruna for the deceased Atti and for herself.

EDCS-10601219.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Seneconius Seisserus made this for his deceased son Marino, and for his living wife Belatulla, and for himself while alive.
EDCS-10601219.summary: A funerary monument erected by Seneconius Seisserus for his son, wife, and himself.

EDCS-10601224.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus. Fidelis willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10601224.summary: A votive inscription dedicated to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, recording the fulfillment of a vow.

EDCS-10601225.translation: To the god Mercurius Iovantucarus, for the safety of Roman Empire and Emperor Severus, Julius Romanus the father, having been warned by a vision, willingly and gladly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10601225.summary: A votive inscription dedicated to Mercurius Iovantucarus by Julius Romanus for the safety of the Roman Empire and Emperor Severus.

EDCS-10601228.translation: Lucanius Lucius willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10601228.summary: A votive inscription by Lucanius Lucius recording the fulfillment of a vow.

EDCS-10601229.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Primanius Ingenuus, also known as Pottus, made this while alive for himself and for his deceased wife Sementinia Gabrilla, and for his other family members.
EDCS-10601229.summary: A funerary monument erected by Primanius Ingenuus for himself, his deceased wife, and family.

EDCS-10601230.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Utius Brasius made this for his wife Vesecunia Secundina, and for himself and his other family members while alive.
EDCS-10601230.summary: A funerary monument erected by Utius Brasius for his wife and family.

EDCS-10601232.translation: To the spirits of the departed. His father Lucceius took care to have this made for the deceased Arto.
EDCS-10601232.summary: A funerary monument commissioned by Lucceius for his deceased son Arto.

EDCS-10601233.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Attianus Memmiolus.
EDCS-10601233.summary: A funerary monument dedicated to Attianus Memmiolus.

EDCS-10601234.translation: With a mind sound and mindful of love(?). Fulvius Potentinus made this while alive for himself and for his deceased wife Lucania Ianuaria.
EDCS-10601234.summary: A funerary monument erected by Fulvius Potentinus for himself and his deceased wife.

EDCS-10601235.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Iurcinius DRINDO(?) and his wife Calen Agatillus took care to have this made.
EDCS-10601235.summary: A funerary monument commissioned by Iurcinius DRINDO(?) and his wife Calen Agatillus.

EDCS-10601236.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Popillianus made this for his most dutiful brother Lallius Atticinus, deceased, and for his mother Popaea, and his mother.
EDCS-10601236.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated to deceased family members by Popillianus.

EDCS-10601237.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Litugenius Secundinus, grandfather, alive, and for Nocturna, grandmother, deceased, and for Anavon, grandmother, deceased, and...
EDCS-10601237.summary: A funerary epitaph mentioning deceased and living grandparents, with the inscription incomplete.

EDCS-10601239.translation: Maternius Marinus for himself and for Censorinia Faustina, his deceased wife.
EDCS-10601239.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Maternius Marinus for himself and his deceased wife.
