EDCS-10601240.translation: [...] Melanasia, daughter of CTO(?), and Caud[...], and Aurusius, for his wife [...], Attius [...]
EDCS-10601240.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription mentioning several individuals, possibly a dedication to a wife.

EDCS-10601241.translation: To the spirits of the departed. The children made this for Marcus Memmius Commentus and for Primia Urbana.
EDCS-10601241.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated by children to their deceased parents.

EDCS-10601243.translation: [...]arae, Peculiaria, and Frontinia, and Quigilla, Peculiaris [...]
EDCS-10601243.summary: A fragmentary inscription listing several names, possibly related to a funerary monument or a group of individuals.

EDCS-10601244.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Penausius Laganus and Sidonius Iassus arranged for this monument to be made for their son [or daughter] from their own funds.
EDCS-10601244.summary: A funerary epitaph where parents funded the monument for their child.

EDCS-10601245.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Primitivia Pri[...], wife, and for herself, alive, made this for Sattonius Artisus, deceased.
EDCS-10601245.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a wife for her deceased husband and for herself.

EDCS-10601247.translation: Greetings, Sexti Iucundus; farewell, Sexti Iucundus.
EDCS-10601247.summary: A funerary epitaph offering a farewell greeting to Sexti Iucundus.

EDCS-10601248.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Vitalia [...] Amillius [...] Iustinius Iustus(?) and for himself, alive, made this.
EDCS-10601248.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Iustinius Iustus(?) for deceased individuals and himself.

EDCS-10601250.translation: To the spirits of the departed. [---]mia, wife of [---]on, son of [---] Mico[---], was set up by her son.
EDCS-10601250.summary: A funerary dedication for a woman, set up by her son.

EDCS-10601251.translation: To the spirits of the departed. [---]um was arranged to be made for his father [---]nio and [---]epta [---].
EDCS-10601251.summary: A funerary dedication, likely for a father, with one of his children arranging the monument.

EDCS-10601256.summary: A dedication to the god Apollo by an individual.

EDCS-10601257.translation: In honor of the imperial household, to Concordia, Marcus Petronius [---] for the city of Castor and Pollux.
EDCS-10601257.summary: An honorary inscription dedicated to Concordia and the imperial family, possibly on behalf of the city.

EDCS-10601258.translation: To the genius of Gaius Aurelius Maternus, prefect of the equites, quaestor of the civitas Mediatricum, Cathirigius Delphicus, his client, [set this up].
EDCS-10601258.summary: An inscription honoring the genius of a Roman official, dedicated by his client.

EDCS-10601260.translation: To Hercules, Taliounus, son of Oricla, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10601260.summary: A votive inscription to Hercules by Taliounus, son of Oricla.

EDCS-10601261.translation: To the most holy divine power of the goddess Icovellavna, Saturninus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10601261.summary: A votive inscription to the goddess Icovellavna by Saturninus.

EDCS-10601262.translation: [---] to Icovellavna, [---]mus Licini[---] fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-10601262.summary: A votive inscription to the goddess Icovellavna, with a partial name of the dedicant.

EDCS-10601268.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus, in honor of the divine household, the neighborhood of Honoris publicly set this up, and those inscribed below, under the supervision of Titus Iulius Adiutor, Marcus Paullus Martialis, Publius Donnax. Quintus Giamius Bellus and Communis, son of Giamius. Elvorix, son of Varicillus. Melus, son of Cintusmi. Marcus Macirius Atrectus donated the price. Terentinus and Peregrinus, sons of Illanvissa. Gaius Germanicus Corobus. Sextus Elvius Clemens.
EDCS-10601268.summary: A public dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and the imperial family by multiple individuals and groups from the vicus Honoris.

EDCS-10601269.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus, in honor of the divine household, Marcus Valerius Iuvenalis, freedman of Marcus Valerius Indus, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10601269.summary: A votive inscription to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and the imperial family by a freedman.

EDCS-10601271.translation: To the spirits of the Senones, Tris and his master, and Mercury, by order of Mercury.
EDCS-10601271.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the spirits of the Senones and Mercury, likely from a tomb.

EDCS-10601272.translation: Lucius Iulius Primulus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Mercury.
EDCS-10601272.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicating a monument to Mercury by Lucius Iulius Primulus.

EDCS-10601273.translation: Aureliana, mother of Divicianus, dedicated this to the god Mercury for his health, in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-10601273.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Mercury by Aureliana for the health of Divicianus.

EDCS-10601277.translation: The sacred god Mercury, by Amilius, the magister of the Bodatius quarter.
EDCS-10601277.summary: This is an inscription dedicating a monument to Mercury by Amilius, the local official of the Bodatius quarter.

EDCS-10601278.translation: Musicus, son of Lillutus, and his family, in fulfillment of a vow, to the god Mercury and Rosmerta.
EDCS-10601278.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicating a monument to Mercury and Rosmerta by Musicus and his family.

EDCS-10601280.translation: Iulius Paternus, the scribe, in fulfillment of a vow, to the goddess Mogontia.
EDCS-10601280.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicating a monument to the goddess Mogontia by Iulius Paternus, a scribe.

EDCS-10601284.summary: This is a dedication inscription by Marcus Vegesonius Marcellus.

EDCS-10601285.summary: This is a dedication inscription by Marcus Vegesonius Marcellus, with some characters lost.

EDCS-10601287.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely naming Dexter and his affiliation or parentage.

EDCS-10601290.translation: For the health of the Emperor Caesar Publius Helvius Pertinax Augustus, father of the country, chief priest, with tribunician power, twice consul, and of Flavia Titiana Augusta, Oceanus, a household slave, administrator of grain. [For the health of the Emperor] Caesar Augustus, father of the country, chief priest, with tribunician power, twice consul, and of Flavia Titiana Augusta.
EDCS-10601290.summary: This is a public dedication made by a slave named Oceanus for the health of Emperor Pertinax and Empress Flavia Titiana, likely placed on a public building.

EDCS-10601482.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by an heir for Catonius Catullinus and his wife.

EDCS-10601484.translation: [---] set up [this monument] at their own expense.
EDCS-10601484.summary: This fragmented inscription indicates that Courunius and Austr[---] paid for the monument themselves.

EDCS-10601485.translation: [---] son Dacillus Sen[---], his children and their children made [this].
EDCS-10601485.summary: This fragmented funerary inscription records that Dacillus Sen[---] and his descendants commissioned the monument.

EDCS-10601486.translation: Tertia, daughter of Scitus, wife of Marinus Ianuarius, son of Donnetus the Helvetian, set [this up] while alive.
EDCS-10601486.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated by Tertia, wife of Marinus Ianuarius, while she was still alive.

EDCS-10601489.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Martial, son of Sabinus.

EDCS-10601490.translation: In honor of the divine house, to Cassibodua [or Victory].
EDCS-10601490.summary: This inscription is a dedication in honor of the imperial family to the goddess Cassibodua (or Victory).

EDCS-10601491.translation: In honor of the divine house, to Mercury. Sextus Iulius [dedicated this].
EDCS-10601491.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the god Mercury by Sextus Iulius in honor of the imperial family.

EDCS-10601492.translation: In honor of the Divine House, to the god Apollo. Lucius Cassius Nobilis [...]
EDCS-10601492.summary: This inscription honors the god Apollo and is dedicated by Lucius Cassius Nobilis, likely in the imperial period.

EDCS-10601494.summary: This inscription consists of a name, Primanius Priscus, possibly marking a tomb or a dedication, dating from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10601495.translation: To the spirits of the departed: to Illius Martialis and Vitialis' wife, Vitalia [...]
EDCS-10601495.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Illius Martialis and his wife Vitalia, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10601496.translation: In honor of the Divine House: [...]SVLD [...]SVL [...] Repertus? Renatus? [...] willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10601496.summary: This inscription, likely honoring the imperial house, records a vow fulfilled by Repertus and Renatus, with the date inferable to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10601497.translation: To the spirits of the departed and to the memory of Mascellio Matutinus, his son, and to Matutinus, son of Marcianus, his father, and [...]vita
EDCS-10601497.summary: This funerary inscription honors Mascellio Matutinus and his father Matutinus, son of Marcianus, dating from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10601498.summary: This inscription fragment names Silia Carila as the daughter of someone, likely a funerary or dedicatory text from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10601499.translation: To the spirits of the departed; to Magiorix, son of Natalis
EDCS-10601499.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Magiorix, son of Natalis, dating from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10601504.translation: In honor of the Divine House, Marceleius Marianus set this up at his own expense to the unconquered god.
EDCS-10601504.summary: This inscription records that Marceleius Marianus dedicated a monument at his own expense to the unconquered god, in honor of the Divine House, likely during the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10601507.translation: To the god Sucellus and Nantosuelta, Bellosus, son of Massa, willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10601507.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Bellosus, son of Massa, to the gods Sucellus and Nantosuelta, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10601508.translation: In honor of the Divine House, Marcus Tignuarius willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10601508.summary: This inscription records that Marcus Tignuarius fulfilled a vow in honor of the Divine House, likely during the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10601509.translation: Decmana, his wife, willingly and deservedly fulfilled her vow.
EDCS-10601509.summary: This is a dedication to an unnamed deity, likely feminine, by a woman named Decmana who fulfilled her vow.

EDCS-10601510.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Cariatus, son of Gaita(?), and his wife Felis(?).
EDCS-10601510.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Cariatus and his wife Felis, honoring the departed.

EDCS-10601512.translation: Sanctus had this made for Saccomainus, son of Cantognatus, and for Saccetus, son of Saccomainus Bellator, son of Belatullus.
EDCS-10601512.summary: This is a funerary monument commissioned by Sanctus for several individuals, likely family members, with complex filiation.

EDCS-10601513.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Caius Lucillius Lepidinus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-10601513.translation: Gaius Lucillius Lepidinus willingly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Jupiter Best and Greatest.
EDCS-10601513.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Gaius Lucillius Lepidinus, who fulfilled his vow.

EDCS-10601514.text_edition: \n Deo Mercurio Lucius Vatinius Felix miliaria a vico Saravo leugis XII constitui iussit votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10601514.translation: Lucius Vatinius Felix ordered the erection of this milestone 12 leagues from the village of Saravus, to the god Mercury, and willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10601514.summary: This is a milestone inscription commissioned by Lucius Vatinius Felix, dedicated to Mercury, marking a distance of 12 leagues.

EDCS-10601515.translation: Lucius Sulpicius Ocelio willingly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Mercury Vos(egus?) and Hecate, during the consulship of Emperor Trajan, during his Dacian victory.
EDCS-10601515.summary: This is a dedication to Mercury and Hecate by Lucius Sulpicius Ocelio, mentioning Emperor Trajan and likely dating to the Dacian Wars.

EDCS-10601516.translation: To the god Mercury. Canetus Martialis.
EDCS-10601516.summary: This is a dedication to the god Mercury by Canetus Martialis.

EDCS-10601519.summary: This is a brief inscription identifying an individual named Belliccus, son of Surbur.

EDCS-10601520.translation: Marcus Monianius Magnus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Bugius.
EDCS-10601520.summary: This is a dedication to an individual named Bugius by Marcus Monianius Magnus, who fulfilled his vow.

EDCS-10601524.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Aventinus for Iulius Sacratus.
EDCS-10601524.summary: This is a tombstone inscription set up by Aventinus for Iulius Sacratus.

EDCS-10601525.translation: To Belatulla, wife of Maius Blandus Marianus, Belatulla erected [this].
EDCS-10601525.summary: This inscription is a funerary monument set up by Belatulla for her mother, also named Belatulla.

EDCS-10601526.translation: To the divine shades of Solidia Minuta.
EDCS-10601526.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Solidia Minuta.

EDCS-10601527.translation: To the divine shades. Iucunda, wife of Vinicius Fand[us], [erected this].
EDCS-10601527.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Iucunda for her husband, Vinicius Fandus.

EDCS-10601530.translation: To Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, son of Drusus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the third time, imperator for the third time, father of the fatherland, consul-designate. Dedicated by the villagers of Marosalla at public expense on the ninth day before the Kalends of October in the year when Gaius Passienus Crispus and Titus Statilius Taurus were consuls.
EDCS-10601530.summary: This is a public dedication to Emperor Claudius by the villagers of Marosalla, dating to 44 AD.

EDCS-10601532.translation: To the god Mercury. Siliana, daughter of Silvestris, willingly paid her vow as deserved.
EDCS-10601532.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Mercury, dedicated by Siliana.

EDCS-10601533.translation: To Mercury. Titus S. A. willingly paid his vow.
EDCS-10601533.summary: This is a votive inscription to Mercury, dedicated by Titus S. A.

EDCS-10601536.translation: To Carissimus. Capiri willingly paid [his] vow as deserved.
EDCS-10601536.summary: This is a votive inscription to Carissimus, dedicated by Capiri.

EDCS-10601537.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest. Casillus(?), son of Cassi, gave this gift.
EDCS-10601537.summary: This is a dedication of a gift to Jupiter, likely by Casillus.

EDCS-10601541.translation: To Mercury. Cupitus, son of Dercoies, willingly paid his vow as deserved.
EDCS-10601541.summary: This is a votive inscription to Mercury, dedicated by Cupitus.

EDCS-10601542.translation: To the divine shades of Calvus, son of Publius.
EDCS-10601542.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Calvus, son of Publius.

EDCS-10601543.translation: To the god Mercury, by Tritus, son of Sacrius.
EDCS-10601543.summary: This is a dedication to the god Mercury by Tritus.

EDCS-10601544.translation: To the spirits of the departed; Ammillo, son of Sedulus, (died).
EDCS-10601544.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Ammillo, son of Sedulus.

EDCS-10601547.translation: To the spirits of the departed; Cantai, daughter of Carmulus.
EDCS-10601547.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Cantai, daughter of Carmulus.

EDCS-10601548.translation: To the spirits of the departed; Carantodia, daughter of Amianus.
EDCS-10601548.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Carantodia, daughter of Amianus.

EDCS-10601549.translation: To the spirits of the departed; to Caratulla, daughter of Samon(is?).
EDCS-10601549.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Caratulla, daughter of Samon(is?).

EDCS-10601552.summary: This is a dedication to Cornelianus by Comisarus Mater(nus?).

EDCS-10601553.summary: This appears to be the beginning of a funerary inscription for Cossilus Censorinus.

EDCS-10601555.translation: In honor of B() B(); Decma and Ammil(la?).
EDCS-10601555.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Decma and Ammil(la?) to unspecified deities or persons.

EDCS-10601556.translation: To the spirits of the departed; Divixta, daughter of Soianus, wife of Severianus.
EDCS-10601556.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Divixta, daughter of Soianus and wife of Severianus.

EDCS-10601560.translation: To the spirits of the underworld; to Lavena, daughter of Marianus.
EDCS-10601560.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lavena, daughter of Marianus.

EDCS-10601562.translation: In memory of Lupus, son of Lupe (?).
EDCS-10601562.summary: This is a funerary inscription mentioning Lupus, possibly the son of Lupe, with the name of the son being uncertain.

EDCS-10601563.translation: To Manius, son of Marcus, Martinus (?).
EDCS-10601563.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or memorial to Manius, son of Marcus, with the name Martinus being uncertain.

EDCS-10601564.translation: To the departed spirits of Martinus.
EDCS-10601564.summary: A funerary dedication to the departed spirit of a person named Martinus.

EDCS-10601565.translation: To the departed spirits of Maurus, son of Adiutor.
EDCS-10601565.summary: A funerary dedication to Maurus, identified as the son of Adiutor.

EDCS-10601566.translation: To the departed spirits of Monimena, daughter of Carantius; her children placed (this).
EDCS-10601566.summary: A funerary dedication by children to their mother Monimena, daughter of Carantius.

EDCS-10601568.translation: To the departed spirits of Pardose (?), VER[---]EII (?).
EDCS-10601568.summary: A funerary dedication to a person named Pardose (?), with damaged or uncertain names following.

EDCS-10601569.translation: To the departed spirits of Primani; his wife Iunia Mea placed (this).
EDCS-10601569.summary: A funerary dedication by Iunia Mea to her husband Primani.

EDCS-10601571.translation: To the departed spirits of Sacrilla.
EDCS-10601571.summary: A funerary dedication to a person named Sacrilla.

EDCS-10601573.summary: A funerary inscription mentioning a couple, Sedatus and his wife Aine.

EDCS-10601575.translation: To the departed spirits; Severus placed (this) for his wife.
EDCS-10601575.summary: A funerary dedication by Severus, son of Sextus, to his wife.

EDCS-10601576.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Publius Severus, likely a tombstone or memorial marker.

EDCS-10601577.translation: In memory of Sacrius, son of Sicno.
EDCS-10601577.summary: This is a funerary inscription remembering Sacrius, son of Sicno, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10601578.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Monument for Siora Escitatus, [erected by] her husband.
EDCS-10601578.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Siora Escitatus, dedicated by her husband, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10601579.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Tasgilia, [erected by] Casurius, her son.
EDCS-10601579.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Tasgilia, dedicated by her son Casurius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10601580.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Vimpata.
EDCS-10601580.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Vimpata, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10601586.translation: To Hercules Saxanus, and their auxiliaries of the V cohorts who are under the centurion Lucius Pompeius Secundus of the XXI Legion Rapax. They willingly and deservedly fulfilled their vow.
EDCS-10601586.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Hercules Saxanus by soldiers of the XXI Legion Rapax and their auxiliaries, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10601587.translation: To Hercules Saxanus, and to Emperor Vespasian Augustus, and to Emperor Titus, and to Caesar Domitian. Marcus Vibius Martialis, centurion of the X Gemina Legion, and the fellow soldiers of the same legion who are under his command, willingly and deservedly fulfilled their vow.
EDCS-10601587.summary: This is a votive inscription to Hercules Saxanus and the Flavian emperors, dedicated by a centurion and soldiers of the X Gemina Legion, likely from the Flavian period (AD 69-96).

EDCS-10601588.translation: Sacred to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Hercules Saxanus. Publius Talpidius Clemens, centurion of the VIII Augusta Legion, with the soldiers of the same legion, willingly, gladly, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10601588.summary: This is a votive inscription to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Hercules Saxanus, dedicated by a centurion and soldiers of the VIII Augusta Legion, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10601589.translation: To Mercury, in honor of the divine house. Atilius Carus willingly, gladly, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10601589.summary: This is a votive inscription to Mercury, dedicated by Atilius Carus in honor of the imperial family, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10601590.translation: To Cambo Suniducus, a gladiator, first rank, victor.
EDCS-10601590.summary: This inscription honors Cambo Suniducus, a gladiator, celebrating his rank and victories, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10601591.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Cesue, son of Avitus.
EDCS-10601591.summary: A funerary epitaph for Cesue, son of Avitus.

EDCS-10601598.translation: To Tiberius Caesar Augustus, son of Augustus, for the eternal welfare of the divine house.
EDCS-10601598.summary: A dedication possibly related to imperial cult, mentioning Tiberius, son of Augustus.

EDCS-10601602.summary: A funerary epitaph for Claudia Tertia.

EDCS-10601603.translation: The remains of Iulia Melli, and her mother Naïs, mixed together.
EDCS-10601603.summary: A funerary inscription recording the commingling of remains for Iulia Melli and her mother Naïs.

EDCS-10601604.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Paterna, daughter of Viducus.
EDCS-10601604.summary: A funerary epitaph for Paterna, daughter of Viducus.

EDCS-10601605.summary: A fragmented funerary inscription recording the maker of a monument, possibly for a woman named -ria.

EDCS-10601609.summary: A fragmented inscription possibly recording the erection of a monument by Cassius for someone named Sacra.

EDCS-10601610.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Of Crixus.

EDCS-10601615.translation: The innocent soul of Lucilla. Carussa [dedicated this?].
EDCS-10601615.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucilla, possibly dedicated by Carussa.

EDCS-10601625.translation: To Apollo and Sirona. Biturix, son of Iulius, gave [this].
EDCS-10601625.summary: A dedication of a gift by Biturix, son of Iulius, to the gods Apollo and Sirona.

EDCS-10601627.translation: To Sanuacus, son of Cantebosis, and to Iunius, son of Fri[---]ii[---]inoi.
EDCS-10601627.summary: This dedication is made to two individuals, Sanuacus and Iunius, whose parentage is partially preserved.

EDCS-10601628.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. [This grave is for] Iucundus (?).
EDCS-10601628.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the departed, likely for an individual named Iucundus.

EDCS-10601632.summary: This inscription records the names Maogounus and Invictionus, possibly a personal name and a cognomen, or two names.

EDCS-10601633.translation: Catullinus, son of Catullius, [erected this] for his son.
EDCS-10601633.summary: This epitaph states that Catullinus dedicated a monument for his son.

EDCS-10601634.translation: Maccus, son of Attilius (?), called Graecus.
EDCS-10601634.summary: This inscription identifies an individual named Maccus, possibly the son of Attilius, and gives him the cognomen Graecus.

EDCS-10601635.translation: To the god Mercury, Publius [---] fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-10601635.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Mercury, with Publius fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-10601636.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Carosa, daughter of Melindus.

EDCS-10601638.translation: Victorinus Potentinus, son of Genoesugenus, lived 21 years for his wife Perssicila.
EDCS-10601638.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Victorinus Potentinus, who died at 21, dedicated by his wife Perssicila.

EDCS-10601641.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Seia Iunia Acer [erected this for her] husband.
EDCS-10601641.summary: This funerary inscription by Seia Iunia Acer is dedicated to her husband.

EDCS-10601642.translation: To the god Hercules, Livianus Be[---] and Severus [---] fulfilled their vow willingly and deservedly, the place granted by decree of the pagus.
EDCS-10601642.summary: This is a votive inscription to Hercules, where Livianus and Severus fulfilled a vow, with land granted by the pagus.

EDCS-10601645.translation: To Jupiter, Best and Greatest, the residents of the Solimari district had this made, with Meddgnatus, son of Ategnia, and Serenus, freedman of Silvanus, taking responsibility.
EDCS-10601645.summary: This is a votive inscription by the vicani Solimarienses, dedicated to Jupiter, commissioned by Meddgnatus and Serenus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10601648.translation: Albucius, in fulfillment of a vow, willingly and deservedly gave this gift to the god Mercury and Rosmerta.
EDCS-10601648.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Mercury and Rosmerta by Albucius, who fulfilled a vow, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10601649.translation: Citusmus, son of Samotalus, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Mercury and Rosmerta.
EDCS-10601649.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Mercury and Rosmerta by Citusmus, who fulfilled a vow, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10601650.translation: Tiola willingly and deservedly fulfilled her vow.
EDCS-10601650.summary: This is a votive inscription by Tiola, who fulfilled a vow, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10601656.summary: This is a personal inscription, likely a funerary one, recording the name of Docenus, son of Prition.

EDCS-10601659.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the Manes by Iassia.

EDCS-10601662.summary: This is a personal inscription, likely funerary, honoring Marullus, son of Saturninus.

EDCS-10601663.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely funerary, recording parts of a name and filiation.

EDCS-10601664.translation: Regulus, son of Rebricus, to the departed spirits.
EDCS-10601664.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the Manes by Regulus, son of Rebricus.

EDCS-10601665.translation: To all the departed spirits, for remembrance, by Sabatia and Severa.
EDCS-10601665.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to all the gods of the underworld by Sabatia and Severa, likely to commemorate loved ones.

EDCS-10601668.translation: In honor of the divine house, Padula dedicated this to the goddesses Iuno, for the health of Sextus Rufus Agricola, Regalis, Petturonis, and Grannica, and willingly fulfilled her vow.
EDCS-10601668.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated by Padula to the Iunoes for the health of several individuals, likely during the imperial period.

EDCS-10601669.translation: Sacred to Mercury and Rosmerta. Regalis and Augustus, brothers and heirs of Februrinus, willingly fulfilled their vow.
EDCS-10601669.summary: This is a votive inscription by two brothers, Regalis and Augustus, dedicating a monument to Mercury and Rosmerta.

EDCS-10601670.translation: To Apollo, Scottius, son of Cotitus, willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10601670.summary: A votive inscription by Scottius, son of Cotitus, to the god Apollo.

EDCS-10601671.translation: A monument for Reginna, daughter of Vimpa.
EDCS-10601671.summary: This inscription marks a monument erected for Reginna, daughter of Vimpa.

EDCS-10601673.summary: This fragment appears to be part of a dedication to the deity Camulorix.

EDCS-10601674.summary: This fragment likely identifies a person, Sabinus, son of Satti, possibly as a dedicant or the subject of an inscription.

EDCS-10601675.translation: Sextus Iulius Senovyrus, son of Dubnotalus, and Iulia Litumara, daughter of Litaviccus, arranged for this to be made.
EDCS-10601675.summary: This inscription records that Sextus Iulius Senovyrus and Iulia Litumara commissioned the creation of a monument, likely a tomb or dedication.

EDCS-10601676.translation: To the departed spirits: Sacirobena and Marinus.
EDCS-10601676.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Sacirobena and Marinus.

EDCS-10601677.translation: To the god Neptune, Toutissia Vestina willingly fulfilled her vow.
EDCS-10601677.summary: A votive inscription by Toutissia Vestina to the god Neptune.

EDCS-10601678.translation: Agathobius donated this to his fellow slave Anaillus.
EDCS-10601678.summary: This inscription records a donation made by Agathobius to his fellow slave, Anaillus.

EDCS-10601679.translation: To Hercules? Talissa, daughter of Cosvonnia.
EDCS-10601679.summary: This is a dedication, likely to Hercules, by an individual named Talissa.

EDCS-10601681.summary: This inscription is a simple name and filiation, possibly on a tombstone or ownership marker.

EDCS-10601682.summary: This inscription records that Senileius was the maker of the object it is inscribed on.

EDCS-10601683.translation: To the departed spirits. For Decminus, son of [---].
EDCS-10601683.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the memory of Decminus.

EDCS-10601684.summary: This inscription records the filiation of an unknown individual, possibly on a funerary or dedicatory monument.

EDCS-10601686.translation: To the god Mercurius Recmus. Riguirus, son of [---], willingly placed this vow. Paternus, son of Boancus, fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-10601686.summary: This is a religious dedication to Mercurius Recmus, with two individuals fulfilling vows.

EDCS-10601688.translation: To the departed spirits. Tiberius Claudius Auguralis.
EDCS-10601688.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Tiberius Claudius Auguralis.

EDCS-10601691.translation: For Poppaea Sabina, daughter of Iullus. Gaius Julius Iullus, heir by will.
EDCS-10601691.summary: This inscription records a bequest or memorial for Poppaea Sabina, with Gaius Julius Iullus acting as heir.

EDCS-10601696.translation: To the god Mercurius and Rosmerta. Carantus, son of Sacrus, fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly for the health of his son Urbicius.
EDCS-10601696.summary: This is a religious dedication to Mercurius and Rosmerta, made by Carantus for his son's well-being.

EDCS-10601699.translation: To the unconquered god. Germanus fulfilled (his vow).
EDCS-10601699.summary: This is a religious dedication to an unconquered god, made by Germanus.

EDCS-10601700.summary: This is a dedication to a master, likely from a freedman or slave, as suggested by the name Animosus and the term 'domino'.

EDCS-10601701.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely intended as a memorial for someone named Artula.

EDCS-10700334.translation: Libonius Mettus and Cracuna, brothers, have given this gift to the Divinity of Augustus and the Genius of the prefects.
EDCS-10700334.summary: This is a dedication by two brothers, Libonius Mettus and Cracuna, to the Divinity of Augustus and the Genius of the prefects.

EDCS-10700335.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus hic fecit claro viguit qui nomine semper doctor Romani nobilis eloquii Lucius Terentius Iulianus qui et Concordius vir perfectissimus magister studiorum grammaticus Latinus\n
EDCS-10700335.translation: To the departed spirits: Here lies Lucius Terentius Iulianus, who was also called Concordius, a most distinguished man, master of studies, a teacher of Roman eloquence, who always flourished with wisdom and was known by his famous name.
EDCS-10700335.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Terentius Iulianus, a renowned teacher of rhetoric and grammar, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-10700337.translation: Obstina had this made during her lifetime for her husband [---]crottioni [---] and for herself.
EDCS-10700337.summary: This funerary monument was commissioned during her lifetime by Obstina for her husband and herself, with part of the husband's name and description lost.

EDCS-10700338.text_edition: \n Genio ||(centurionum) praepositorum Macalius Avitus Vitalius Respectus cives Suebi Nicrensens his qui ordines sequentur dono dederunt merito\n
EDCS-10700338.translation: Macalius Avitus Vitalius Respectus, citizens of Nicrens in Suebia, have given this gift to the Genii of the preceding centurions who will follow in order, as is fitting.
EDCS-10700338.summary: This is a dedication by three soldiers from Suebia to the Genii of their centurions, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10700339.translation: He made this living for his deceased son Cultorius and for himself and his family.
EDCS-10700339.summary: This is a funerary dedication made during the lifetime of the dedicator for their deceased son and for themselves and their family.

EDCS-10700341.translation: To the Genius of Gaius Iulius Serenus.
EDCS-10700341.summary: This is a dedication to the Genius of Gaius Iulius Serenus, possibly from a subordinate or devotee.

EDCS-10700343.summary: This is a simple dedication or gift from Primitius to Prissia.

EDCS-10700344.translation: Severus made it. May you be happy.
EDCS-10700344.summary: This is a brief inscription by Severus, possibly marking a completed work or object, with a wish for good fortune.

EDCS-10700346.translation: Fedola rests here in peace, who lived 75 years, dying four days before the Kalends of March; her son and daughter placed this monument.
EDCS-10700346.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Fedola, erected by her children, likely from the later Roman Empire given the phrasing and common Christian elements.

EDCS-10700347.translation: Victura rests here in peace, who lived 14 years and 40 days. Leonia her mother placed this monument.
EDCS-10700347.summary: A funerary epitaph for the young Victura, set up by her mother Leonia, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10700348.translation: Maximianus lies here in peace, who lived 65 years, 4 months, and 20 days. His sons Memoriosus and Prudens made this monument.
EDCS-10700348.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Maximianus, indicating his age at death and identifying his sons, Memoriosus and Prudens, as the erectors.

EDCS-10700352.summary: This is a simple inscription that likely names an individual, Sincorius Censorinus, possibly on a tomb or a dedication.

EDCS-10700353.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed, Ammius Atucius.
EDCS-10700353.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the 'Dis Manibus' (Spirits of the Departed), identifying the individual as Ammius Atucius, likely on a tomb.

EDCS-10700354.text_edition: \n Deo Intarabo sua inpensa Germanius us dono dedit\n
EDCS-10700354.translation: Germanius dedicated this gift to the god Intarabus at his own expense.
EDCS-10700354.summary: This is a votive inscription where Germanius dedicates a gift to the god Intarabus at his own expense, suggesting a personal religious act.

EDCS-10700355.translation: He made this, while alive, for [his wife?] O[?] and Mattonia, his deceased wife.
EDCS-10700355.summary: This funerary inscription records that a living husband erected a monument for his deceased wife, Mattonia, possibly also mentioning another individual.

EDCS-10700356.text_edition: \n Votis X domini nostri Constantini Augusti votis X domini nostri Licini Augusti Servandus\n
EDCS-10700356.translation: At the tenth anniversary vows for our lord Constantine Augustus, and the tenth anniversary vows for our lord Licinius Augustus, Servandus [did this].
EDCS-10700356.summary: This inscription records Servandus fulfilling decennial vows to the emperors Constantine Augustus and Licinius Augustus, likely related to military or imperial service.

EDCS-10700359.text_edition: \n Apollini Tiberius Claudius Cinii libertus Reburrus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10700359.translation: To Apollo, Tiberius Claudius Reburrus, freedman of Cinii, paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-10700359.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Apollo by Tiberius Claudius Reburrus, a freedman, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-10700360.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed, [dedicated to?] Restitutus(?) ...
EDCS-10700360.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription beginning with 'Dis Manibus' (To the Spirits of the Departed), indicating a tombstone for someone named Restitutus.

EDCS-10700362.summary: This inscription indicates ownership of a location by a person named Privatus Biracus.

EDCS-10700364.summary: This inscription appears to record the name of an individual, Tessius Martalus.

EDCS-10700365.translation: Victorius, son of Arttonius, son of Artto.
EDCS-10700365.summary: This inscription provides a patronymic name structure, indicating Victorius, son of Arttonius, son of Artto.

EDCS-10700366.summary: This inscription records a name with a patronymic, Manlius, son of Matuacus.

EDCS-10700368.summary: This inscription provides a patronymic name, Seisserius, son of Ollius.

EDCS-10700370.translation: Mascellio, son of Collius, from Decentia.
EDCS-10700370.summary: This inscription records the name Mascellio, his patronymic Collius, and a place of origin, Decentia.

EDCS-10700372.translation: Son of Titus, grandson of Titius.
EDCS-10700372.summary: This inscription indicates a filiation, recording the son of Titus and grandson of Titius.

EDCS-10700377.summary: This inscription records two names, likely an individual named Senomaius Iatlius.

EDCS-10700378.summary: This inscription records the name Quintus Caredonius and a numerical designation, possibly indicating a series or rank.

EDCS-10700388.summary: This inscription provides a name with a patronymic, Cintusmus, son of Primitivus.

EDCS-10700392.translation: To Moce, son of Mocetus, of the family of Axillus.
EDCS-10700392.summary: This inscription is a dedication or funerary marker for Moce, identifying his parentage and family affiliation.

EDCS-10801360.text_edition: \n OOIIII Severian Gentilius memoriae amici faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-10801360.translation: Severian Gentilius arranged for this to be made for the memory of his friend.
EDCS-10801360.summary: This is a funerary dedication arranged by Severian Gentilius for his deceased friend, likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-10801398.translation: To the Divine Manes. For Manilianus, son of Sedatus, husband of Mansuetus, mother (of the deceased).
EDCS-10801398.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Manilianus, likely set up by his mother, Mansuetus, and possibly his wife, indicating a family memorial.

EDCS-10900238.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Servandiae Servandae filiae defunctae Iulius Servandus IIIIIIvir Augustalis et Victoriae Silviae coniugi eiius et sibi vivi fecerunt\n
EDCS-10900238.translation: To the Divine Manes. For Servandia, daughter of Servandus, now deceased. Julius Servandus, a member of the IIII viri Augustales, and Victoriae Silvia, his wife, and for himself, made this while alive.
EDCS-10900238.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated by Julius Servandus, a magistrate, for his deceased daughter, his wife, and himself, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10900244.text_edition: \n Deo Apollini Sextus Similius Severus ELOGS votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10900244.translation: To the god Apollo, Sextus Similius Severus gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10900244.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Apollo by Sextus Similius Severus, indicating the fulfillment of a religious promise.

EDCS-10900247.translation: In honor of the divine house. For the goddess Pritona [or] Iunona, for the safety of the inhabitants of Contomaglensium, Tertinius Modestus [made this].
EDCS-10900247.summary: This inscription is a dedication to a goddess (Pritona or Iunona), possibly related to imperial cult and for the welfare of the inhabitants of Contomaglensium, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10900249.text_edition: \n Ibliomariae Gabrella defunctis et Viriliae Sacrae vivae Marcus Ibliomar<i>us Restitutus fecit\n
EDCS-10900249.translation: For Ibliomaria Gabrella, deceased, and for Virilia Sacra, alive. Marcus Ibliomarius Restitutus made this.
EDCS-10900249.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Marcus Ibliomarius Restitutus for his deceased wife (or relative) Ibliomaria Gabrella and for his living wife Virilia Sacra, indicating a memorial planned for the future.

EDCS-10900250.translation: To the Divine Manes. For Arbullius Agurio. [---]
EDCS-10900250.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription dedicated to the Divine Manes for Arbullius Agurio.

EDCS-10900251.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Attillio Paterno Censilla uxor faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-10900251.translation: To the Divine Manes. Censilla, wife of Attillius Paternus, arranged for this to be made.
EDCS-10900251.summary: This is a funerary inscription arranged by Censilla for her husband Attillius Paternus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000207.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Cinnenae defunctae Tertius Tertinus coniugi\n
EDCS-11000207.translation: To the Divine Manes. For Cinnena, deceased. Tertius Tertinus, her husband.
EDCS-11000207.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Tertius Tertinus for his deceased wife Cinnena.

EDCS-11000208.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Iaretio Losunio patri defuncto \n
EDCS-11000208.translation: To the departed spirits of Iaretio Losunio, my father, who has passed away.
EDCS-11000208.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to the father of the deceased, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000210.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo votum solverunt libentes merito Matutinus et Victor fratres\n
EDCS-11000210.translation: Matutinus and Victor, brothers, willingly and deservedly paid their vow to Jupiter Best and Greatest.
EDCS-11000210.summary: This is a votive inscription where two brothers fulfilled a vow to Jupiter, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11201732.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae dis Cassibus Marcus A G votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11201732.translation: In honor of the divine house, Marcus A G willingly and deservedly paid his vow to the gods of the household.
EDCS-11201732.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to household gods in honor of the imperial family, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11201733.translation: To the gods of the household, Marcus Couirius.
EDCS-11201733.summary: This is a dedication to household gods by Marcus Couirius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11201737.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deo Intarabo Bittius Benignius Acceptus restituit\n
EDCS-11201737.translation: In honor of the divine house, Bittius Benignius Acceptus restored this to the god Intarabus.
EDCS-11201737.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription where Bittius Benignius Acceptus restored a monument to the god Intarabus in honor of the imperial family, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11201739.text_edition: \n TAVIHEP In honorem domus divinae Marti et Ancamnae et Genio pagi Vilciatis Caius Serotinius Iustus ex voto posuit Avitus\n
EDCS-11201739.translation: In honor of the divine house, Caius Serotinius Iustus, with Avitus, placed this offering by vow to Mars, Ancamna, and the Genius of the district of Vilciatis.
EDCS-11201739.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Mars, Ancamna, and the Genius of the Vilciatis district by Caius Serotinius Iustus and Avitus, in honor of the imperial family, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11201740.text_edition: \n ------ pagan]orum pagi Teucoriatis Teucoriatius Securus illorum paganorum libertus et Secundius Primulus antistes donum dederunt\n
EDCS-11201740.translation: [...of the] pagans of the district of Teucoriatis, Teucoriatius Securus, freedman of those pagans, and Secundius Primulus, priest, gave this gift.
EDCS-11201740.summary: This inscription records a gift given by a freedman and a priest to the pagans of the Teucoriatis district, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11201741.text_edition: \n Marti Iovantucaro sacro sic Primuus pro Restitutio Primo filio votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11201741.translation: Primuus willingly and deservedly paid his vow to Mars Iovantucarus, sacred to him, for the restoration of his son Primo.
EDCS-11201741.summary: This is a votive inscription where Primuus paid a vow to Mars Iovantucarus for the health of his son Primo, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11201742.text_edition: \n Marti Iovantucaro Sextus Restitutius Romanus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11201742.translation: Sextus Restitutius Romanus willingly and deservedly paid his vow to Mars Iovantucarus.
EDCS-11201742.summary: This is a votive inscription where Sextus Restitutius Romanus paid a vow to Mars Iovantucarus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11201743.text_edition: \n Marti Iovantucaro pro salute Mercurialis filius Secundius Secundinus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11201743.translation: Secundius Secundinus, son of Mercurialis, willingly and deservedly paid his vow to Mars Iovantucarus for the health of Mercurialis.
EDCS-11201743.summary: This is a votive inscription where Secundius Secundinus paid a vow to Mars Iovantucarus for the health of his father Mercurialis, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11201744.text_edition: \n Deo Iovantucaro pro Mercuriale filio votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11201744.translation: Optatius Verus, son of Devas, erected this for Mars and Ancamna, fulfilling his vow gladly and deservedly.
EDCS-11201744.summary: This is a dedication to Mars and Ancamna by Optatius Verus.

EDCS-11201746.text_edition: \n Leno Marti et Ancamnae Optatius Verus Devas ex voto posuit\n
EDCS-11201746.translation: Optatius Verus, son of Devas, erected this for Mars and Ancamna, fulfilling his vow gladly and deservedly.
EDCS-11201746.summary: This is a dedication to Mars and Ancamna by Optatius Verus.

EDCS-11201747.text_edition: \n Deo Invicto Mithrae Martius Martialis pater in suo posuit\n
EDCS-11201747.translation: Martius Martialis, as father, dedicated this to the Unconquered God Mithras on his own property.
EDCS-11201747.summary: This is a dedication to the god Mithras by Martius Martialis, who identifies himself as a father.

EDCS-11201748.text_edition: \n Deo Invicto Soli Martius Martialis pater in suo posuit\n
EDCS-11201748.translation: Martius Martialis, as father, dedicated this to the Unconquered Sun God on his own property.
EDCS-11201748.summary: This is a dedication to the Sun God by Martius Martialis, who identifies himself as a father.

EDCS-11201749.text_edition: \n Numinibus exhedram sic cum coloniae curam agente bilio Secundo Aquino Lucio At Covirio Secundo Cummio Vitale Matuinio Mansueto Aprilio Ibliomaro dedicatum \n
EDCS-11201749.translation: This exhedra was dedicated to the numina (divine powers) by Bilio Secundus Aquino, Lucius At Covirius Secundus, Cummia Vitale, Matuinius Mansuetus, and Aprilis Ibliomarus, while the colony was administered by the aedile, Bilio Secundus Aquino.
EDCS-11201749.summary: This dedication records the construction of an exhedra to various divine powers, sponsored by several individuals during the aedileship of Bilio Secundus Aquino.

EDCS-11201752.translation: Arbusius C. dedicated this to the goddess Ritona Pritona.
EDCS-11201752.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Ritona Pritona by Arbusius C.

EDCS-11201754.text_edition: \n Deo Vertumno sive Pisinto Caius Fruendus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11201754.translation: Gaius Fruendus gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the god Vertumnus, also known as Pisintus.
EDCS-11201754.summary: This is a votive dedication to the god Vertumnus (or Pisintus) by Gaius Fruendus.

EDCS-11201755.translation: Sextus Attionius Victorinus and Braetia Germana, parents, erected this in fulfillment of a vow, dedicated on the day before the Ides of June, under the consulship of Arrianus and Papo.
EDCS-11201755.summary: This dedication records a votive offering by parents Sextus Attionius Victorinus and Braetia Germana, with a specific dedication date and consuls.

EDCS-11201756.text_edition: \n Dis Cassibus Cossus Frontonis filius sortilegus ex visu votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11201756.translation: Cossus, son of Frontonis, a diviner, fulfilled his vow gladly and deservedly in accordance with a vision.
EDCS-11201756.summary: This is a votive dedication to the Chthonic Gods by Cossus, son of Frontonis, who identifies himself as a diviner and claims to have acted upon a vision.

EDCS-11201758.text_edition: \n S ocellus Cocio votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11201758.translation: Ocellus Coci fulfilled his vow gladly and deservedly.
EDCS-11201758.summary: This is a votive dedication by Ocellus Coci.

EDCS-11201763.translation: Gaius Julius and Julius Fab[---] gave [this] to the province.
EDCS-11201763.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the province by Gaius Julius and Julius Fab[---], likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11201766.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Apronius Chrysanthus and Chreste, parents, [dedicated this] to Apronia Auspicata.
EDCS-11201766.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by parents to their daughter Apronia Auspicata, dating to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-11201767.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Speratius [---] Socralis (?) dedicated [this] to Julia Aesiva, his wife, and to Tigidia, his dearest daughter.
EDCS-11201767.summary: This funerary epitaph is dedicated by Speratius to his wife and daughter, likely dating to the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-11201769.translation: Primulius Alpinus dedicated this to his most devoted father and patron, Primulus of Iassos, while alive.
EDCS-11201769.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Primulius Alpinus to his father and patron, Primulus, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11201770.translation: While alive, Gaius Puccasius Valens, Marcus Puccasius Felix, and Lucius Tertius Speratus made [this] for themselves and their families, to the spirits of the underworld.
EDCS-11201770.summary: This is a funerary monument built by three men for themselves and their families, dating to the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-11201771.translation: Secundinus Africanus [is here], to the spirits of the underworld.
EDCS-11201771.summary: This is a brief funerary epitaph for Secundinus Africanus, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-11201774.translation: Here lies in peace Amata, a faithful virgin, who lived 13 years, and [---] months and 5 days. Her brother placed the monument.
EDCS-11201774.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life and death of Amata, a virgin who died at age 13, with the monument erected by her brother, likely from the 3rd-4th century CE.

EDCS-11201775.translation: On the eighth day before the Ides of May, on a Sunday, the girl Aspecta, fifteen years of age, departed this life, and her elder brother, Parrontius, departed this life on the third day before the Ides of May, having lived 20 years and 20 days.
EDCS-11201775.summary: This inscription records the deaths of two siblings, Aspecta and Parrontius, with specific dates and ages, likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-11201776.translation: Calvio rests here in peace, who lived 6 years, and 7 months and 13 days. Vincaimus made [this] for his pupil.
EDCS-11201776.summary: This funerary epitaph records the short life of Calvio, a pupil, with the monument erected by Vincaimus, likely from the 3rd-4th century CE.

EDCS-11201777.translation: Here rests in peace Elpidia, who lived more or less 40 years. Her husband, Carus, placed the monument.
EDCS-11201777.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life of Elpidia, who died around the age of 40, with the monument erected by her husband, likely from the 3rd-4th century CE.

EDCS-11201778.translation: To Macedonia, dearest wife, who lived 14 years. Pelagius and Irene, parents, erected [this]. Eustasius rests here in peace, a citizen of Surus, who lived 40 years. Ced[--]bius and Iliodorus erected [this] to their parent.
EDCS-11201778.summary: This inscription is a funerary monument commemorating two individuals, Macedonia and Eustasius, with their ages and dedicators provided, dating likely to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11201781.translation: Here lies Macedonia, who lived [--] year and [--] months. Lea erected this monument to her sweetest daughter.
EDCS-11201781.summary: This is a funerary inscription from the Roman Imperial period, honoring a deceased girl named Macedonia, erected by her mother Lea.

EDCS-11201782.translation: [--] rests here. Maura, his wife, erected this monument in peace.
EDCS-11201782.summary: This is a funerary inscription from the Roman Imperial period, recording the erection of a monument by a wife named Maura for her deceased husband.

EDCS-11201784.translation: Suricula, daughter, lies in peace, who lived six years. Father and mother erected this monument.
EDCS-11201784.summary: This is a funerary inscription from the Roman Imperial period, commemorating a six-year-old girl named Suricula, erected by her parents.

EDCS-11201790.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Claudia Atticilia made this for her husband Marcus Iulius Martialis, son of Marcius.
EDCS-11201790.summary: This is a funerary inscription from the Roman Imperial period, dedicating a monument to Marcus Iulius Martialis by his wife Claudia Atticilia.

EDCS-11201791.translation: In honor of the Divine House. Marcus Plautius Restitutus, in fulfillment of a vow, to the god Veraudunus and Inciona, for his mother Alpinia Lucana.
EDCS-11201791.summary: This inscription from the Roman Imperial period records a votive offering by Marcus Plautius Restitutus to the gods Veraudunus and Inciona, on behalf of his mother.

EDCS-11201792.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Marcus Secundius Secundinus erected this monument during his lifetime for his wife Gallia Varicilla and for himself.
EDCS-11201792.summary: This funerary inscription from the Roman Imperial period records Marcus Secundius Secundinus dedicating a monument for himself and his wife Gallia Varicilla.

EDCS-11201793.translation: To the Divine Spirits. For Aprilis Firmus, deceased.
EDCS-11201793.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription from the Roman Imperial period, intended to honor Aprilis Firmus.

EDCS-11201796.translation: Lemaftus erected this for his deceased wife Mammiccia during his lifetime.
EDCS-11201796.summary: This funerary inscription from the Roman Imperial period records Lemaftus dedicating a monument for his deceased wife Mammiccia.

EDCS-11201799.translation: To the Divine Spirits. For Ancreianius Mansuetus, for his son Mansuetinus, and for himself.
EDCS-11201799.summary: This funerary inscription from the Roman Imperial period is dedicated to Ancreianius Mansuetus, his son Mansuetinus, and the dedicator himself.

EDCS-11201802.summary: This inscription appears to be a funerary epitaph for Insticius Romanus, likely a Roman citizen.

EDCS-11201803.translation: To Boudinae and Alaunae, Gaius Sextilius Sollemnis.
EDCS-11201803.summary: This is a dedication to the deities Boudinae and Alaunae by Gaius Sextilius Sollemnis.

EDCS-11201804.translation: To the god Voroius, to Boudinae and Alaunae, Gaius Sextilius Sollemnis.
EDCS-11201804.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the god Voroius and the deities Boudinae and Alaunae by Gaius Sextilius Sollemnis.

EDCS-11201945.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Caio Claudio Secundino signifero veterano legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis librarii et collegium tubicinum militum Bingensium EPC\n
EDCS-11201945.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Gaius Claudius Secundinus, standard-bearer, veteran of the twenty-second legion Primigenia, pious and faithful, scribe, and the association of trumpeters of the soldiers of Bingen, in the province of Gaul, dedicated this.
EDCS-11201945.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Gaius Claudius Secundinus, a veteran and scribe from the twenty-second legion, by his military association.

EDCS-11202021.translation: To the honor of Titus Tertinius, decurion and *duumvir*, Macrinus [dedicated this].
EDCS-11202021.summary: This inscription honors Titus Tertinius, who held the offices of decurion and *duumvir*, likely in a Roman colony.

EDCS-11202035.translation: [dedicated to] Priscus, priest of Rome and Augustus, *magister quaestor* of the civitas of the Treveri, and prefect of the cohort of the Aresacians.
EDCS-11202035.summary: This is a dedication to Priscus, who held significant religious and civic offices in the civitas of the Treveri, including priest and prefect.

EDCS-11202040.translation: of Titus Publicius Tertius, forest warden.
EDCS-11202040.summary: This inscription identifies Titus Publicius Tertius as a forest warden.

EDCS-11202041.translation: [dedicated to] Mages and [to] his wife, Mages, while still alive.
EDCS-11202041.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication, possibly funerary, to Mages and his wife.

EDCS-11202042.translation: The heirs erected [this] at their own expense to TIPP Augustus, son of Sottus, and to Vasso, wife of Maunnat, daughter of Maunnatus.
EDCS-11202042.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication by heirs to Tipp Augustus and his wife Vasso.

EDCS-11202043.translation: [dedicated] to and to Julia Primilla, his wife, [he] erected [this] at his own expense.
EDCS-11202043.summary: This funerary epitaph records a husband erecting a monument at his own expense to his wife, Julia Primilla.

EDCS-11202080.text_edition: \n et deae Avetae Tiberius Venustius Vitalis Caius Leusius Giamissa Marcus Tongonius Iul Aivinius Lossa Vainius Varus Annius Iarus Brittonius Hilarus dono dederunt\n
EDCS-11202080.translation: Tiberius Venustius Vitalis, Caius Leusius Giamissa, Marcus Tongonius, Iulius Aivinius, Lossa Vainius Varus, Annius Iarus, and Brittonius Hilarus gave this as a gift to the goddess Aveta.
EDCS-11202080.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Aveta by a group of individuals, likely a collegium or a local community.

EDCS-11202083.text_edition: \n Matronis Marcus Valerius Crescens eques legionis VI victricis cornicularius Publi Abulli Luculli \n
EDCS-11202083.translation: To the Matronae, Marcus Valerius Crescens, a clerk of the Sixth Legion Victrix, for Publius Abullius Lucullus.
EDCS-11202083.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Matronae by a soldier serving in the Sixth Legion Victrix, apparently on behalf of another individual.

EDCS-11202084.text_edition: \n Deo Mercurio Lucanius Divixius ex iussu\n
EDCS-11202084.translation: To the god Mercury, Lucanius Divixius, by order.
EDCS-11202084.summary: This is a dedication to Mercury by Lucanius Divixius, who claims to be acting under divine command.

EDCS-11202085.translation: Festus gladly paid his vow, as deserved.
EDCS-11202085.summary: This is a votive inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow by an individual named Festus.

EDCS-11202087.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Numinibus Augustorum VIASAOGNAT libenti animo\n
EDCS-11202087.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, and to the Divine Powers of the Emperors, VIASAOGNAT(?) with a willing heart.
EDCS-11202087.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter and the Imperial cult, with an unclear dedication formula.

EDCS-11202088.text_edition: \n Numinibus Augustorum et Iunonibus Lucius Martius Gasculus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11202088.translation: To the Divine Powers of the Emperors and to the Junones, Lucius Martius Gasculus gladly paid his vow, as deserved.
EDCS-11202088.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the Imperial cult and the Junones by Lucius Martius Gasculus.

EDCS-11202089.translation: Leno to Mars and Victory. Quintus Asicius Centaurus paid his vow, gladly, as deserved.
EDCS-11202089.summary: This is a votive inscription by Quintus Asicius Centaurus dedicated to Mars and Victory.

EDCS-11202090.translation: To the goddess Minerva, [3]tus Ga[3] Suessio [3]arius paid [his] vow, gladly, as deserved.
EDCS-11202090.summary: This is a partial votive inscription dedicated to the goddess Minerva, with the dedicator's name largely lost.

EDCS-11202091.text_edition: \n Deo Invicto Mithrae Nicasius votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11202091.translation: To the unconquered god Mithras, Nicasius paid his vow, gladly, as deserved.
EDCS-11202091.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the god Mithras by Nicasius.

EDCS-11202093.text_edition: \n Vorioni deo sacrum voto suscepto Vettius Demioncus (?)raddari filius votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11202093.translation: Sacred to the god Vorionius. Vettius Demioncus, son of Raddari(?), fulfilled his vow, gladly, as deserved.
EDCS-11202093.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the god Vorionius by Vettius Demioncus, possibly of local or foreign origin.

EDCS-11202094.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Marcus Cousius Senecianus sibi vivus et Herenianiae Orfitae coniugi defunctae fecit\n
EDCS-11202094.translation: To the departed spirits. Marcus Cousius Senecianus made this for himself while alive and for his departed wife Herennia Orfita.
EDCS-11202094.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Marcus Cousius Senecianus for himself and his wife, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-11202095.translation: To the departed spirits of Iustus and...
EDCS-11202095.summary: A fragmentary funerary epitaph mentioning the departed spirits, possibly early imperial.

EDCS-11202096.translation: [To the departed spirits.] For Maternia Decmilla, deceased. Lucius Publicius Severus, the secretary, made this for himself and for Mag[n]ita, his wife, while alive.
EDCS-11202096.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Lucius Publicius Severus for his wife Maternia Decmilla and himself, mentioning his status as a secretary, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century.

EDCS-11202097.translation: ...nausus made this for himself while alive.
EDCS-11202097.summary: A fragmentary funerary epitaph indicating that someone named Nausus set it up for himself, possibly from the imperial period.

EDCS-11202102.text_edition: \n Coniugi pientissimae Aurorae in pace fideli Aquilinus\n
EDCS-11202102.translation: Aquilinus [set this up] for his most devoted wife Aurora, faithful in peace.
EDCS-11202102.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated by Aquilinus to his wife Aurora, indicating a Christian context from late antiquity.

EDCS-11202103.translation: Here rests in peace the venerable man Ludubertus, from a noble family, who lived about 65 years, whose deposit is on the 16th day before the Kalends of January, and he handed over all his possessions to Saint Peter and made himself a cleric.
EDCS-11202103.summary: A late antique or early medieval epitaph for Ludubertus, detailing his noble lineage, lifespan, date of death (December 17th), and his clerical status, indicating a Christian context.

EDCS-11202104.text_edition: \n Hic quiescet Pancaria quae vixit annos XX Florus coniux et patris pro caritate titulum posuerunt\n
EDCS-11202104.translation: Pancaria, who lived 20 years, rests here. Florus, her husband, and her father, set up this monument out of love.
EDCS-11202104.summary: A funerary epitaph for Pancaria, who died at age 20, set up by her husband Florus and father, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century.

EDCS-11202105.translation: Pascasius, who lived 2 years and 6 months, rests here. His parents set up this monument for him.
EDCS-11202105.summary: A funerary epitaph for Pascasius, who died at the age of 2 years and 6 months, set up by his parents, likely from late antiquity.

EDCS-11202107.translation: Vitalis, faithful in peace, rests here, who lived 3 years minus 38 days. For his nourishment, they set up this monument.
EDCS-11202107.summary: A funerary epitaph for Vitalis, who died at approximately 2 years and 7 months of age, set up by his caretakers ('nutritores'), likely from late antiquity.

EDCS-11202108.translation: Ursicina rests here in peace, who lived 5 years and 11 months and 3 days. Elpidius and Ursula, [his/her] first-born daughters, set this up.
EDCS-11202108.summary: A funerary epitaph for Ursicina, who died at age 5 years, 11 months, and 3 days, set up by her daughters Elpidius and Ursula, likely from late antiquity.

EDCS-11202111.translation: Here rests the venerable youth Numodoal, who lived for more or less 16 years, died in peace in the month of February, on the 8th day; his father and mother placed this tombstone for him in peace.
EDCS-11202111.summary: A tombstone for a young man named Numodoal, set up by his parents, dating to February.

EDCS-11202112.translation: Here rests in peace Spu[---]a, who lived one year and [---] months and seven days; her parents, Concordius the father and Ur[---] the mother, placed this tombstone for their most sweet daughter.
EDCS-11202112.summary: A tombstone for a child named Spu[---]a, set up by her parents, dating to a period of about one year and some months.

EDCS-11202121.translation: Here lies Amantia, who lived 3 years, 8 months, 1 day; Vetranio and Lea placed the tombstone in peace.
EDCS-11202121.summary: A tombstone for Amantia, who lived a very short life, set up by Vetranio and Lea.

EDCS-11202123.translation: Here lies Valerius, who lived 35 years; Silentia his wife placed the tombstone, laid to rest on the fifth day before the Ides of June.
EDCS-11202123.summary: A tombstone for Valerius, set up by his wife Silentia, dated to the fifth day before the Ides of June.

EDCS-11202125.translation: [---]a can grieve [---] genus [---] is buried here Eutropia [---] limbs, sudden death [---] laws [---] Hon[---]
EDCS-11202125.summary: A fragmentary inscription possibly recording the burial of Eutropia, mentioning grief and sudden death.

EDCS-11202126.translation: [---]aesuru [---] 2 years [---] his sister (?) [---] who lived 35 days [---] Hirpila the parents [---] placed the tombstone.
EDCS-11202126.summary: A fragmentary tombstone for a child who lived 35 days, possibly set up by a sister and parents.

EDCS-11202132.translation: [---]ola rests here in peace [---] VOIUS her husband [---]
EDCS-11202132.summary: A fragmentary inscription mentioning a person named [---]ola resting in peace, with her husband VOIUS.

EDCS-11202142.translation: To the Genius of Vosugonum, Sabinus, the public slave.
EDCS-11202142.summary: An inscription dedicating something to the Genius of Vosugonum by Sabinus, a public slave.

EDCS-11202146.translation: To the departed spirits, Attillius Sen[---]
EDCS-11202146.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription dedicated to the Manes by Attillius Sen[---].

EDCS-11202148.translation: [---]avelius arranged for it to be made.
EDCS-11202148.summary: A fragmentary inscription indicating that [---]avelius was responsible for the construction or erection of something.

EDCS-11202152.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Genio Apollinessium Mesol Mascellio et Euticius Marcianus donum dederunt\n
EDCS-11202152.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, and to the Genius of the Apollinessians, Mesol and Mascellio and Euticius Marcianus gave this gift.
EDCS-11202152.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter and the Genius of the Apollinessians by Mesol, Mascellio, and Euticius Marcianus.

EDCS-11202154.translation: Solinus, son of Saturninus, dedicated this statue(?) to the god Mercury in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-11202154.summary: This is a votive dedication to the god Mercury by Solinus Saturnini, likely on a statue base.

EDCS-11202156.translation: Decmanus and Dentilia to their mother Eutychia; Decmanus to his wife.
EDCS-11202156.summary: This is a funerary monument for Eutychia, set up by her son Decmanus and possibly his wife Dentilia, and also a separate dedication from Decmanus to his wife.

EDCS-11800705.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Iassius Silvinus and Julius Iassius, his father. And from Drapus, son of Germanus, the grandson.
EDCS-11800705.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Iassius Silvinus and his father Julius Iassius, set up by Drapus, grandson of Germanus.

EDCS-11800706.translation: Masclus and Petrullus, sons, had this made for Suarica, their living wife and mother.
EDCS-11800706.summary: This is a funerary monument for Suarica, commissioned by her sons Masclus and Petrullus.

EDCS-11800708.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Amabilis, son of [3]assius, and [3]vianus SVI[1]INN [---].
EDCS-11800708.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription for Amabilis and possibly another individual, dedicated to the departed spirits.

EDCS-11801051.text_edition: \n Sublime de se sparsit per saecula famam fida cui coniux Allecta tis ne ref ut quia morte silent aeterno carmine vivant\n
EDCS-11801051.translation: Allecta, his faithful wife, scattered his fame wide through the ages, so that he might live forever in song, even though death silences.
EDCS-11801051.summary: This is a poetic epitaph celebrating the enduring fame of a deceased individual, attributed to his wife Allecta.

EDCS-11901939.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Caio Domitio Cai filio\n
EDCS-11901939.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Gaius Domitius, son of Gaius.
EDCS-11901939.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gaius Domitius, son of Gaius.

EDCS-11901968.text_edition: \n Deo Intarabo Ategniomarus Respecti votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11901968.translation: Ategniomarus Respectus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the god Intarabus.
EDCS-11901968.summary: This is a votive inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow by Ategniomarus Respectus to the god Intarabus.

EDCS-11901971.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Aprilis Ledonae coniugi eius fili VI\n
EDCS-11901971.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Aprilis, and for Ledona, his wife, and their six sons.
EDCS-11901971.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aprilis, his wife Ledona, and their six sons.

EDCS-11901972.translation: To Mainusius Mascellioni and his wife Matutinia Malla.
EDCS-11901972.summary: This is a funerary dedication by an individual to their deceased parents, Mainusius Mascellioni and Matutinia Malla.

EDCS-11901973.translation: Resta, his wife, made this for the deceased Pexius Avitus and for herself while alive.
EDCS-11901973.summary: This is a funerary epitaph made by Resta for her deceased husband Pexius Avitus and for herself, indicating it was prepared during her lifetime.

EDCS-11901974.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Sattoni Exomni Primius Prisso nepoti fecit\n
EDCS-11901974.translation: To the departed spirits, Primius Prisso made this for his grandson, Sattioni Exomni.
EDCS-11901974.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Primius Prisso for his deceased grandson, Sattioni Exomni.

EDCS-11901975.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Secundius Attianus et Censorinia Matrausus coniugi et) filio defunctis\n
EDCS-11901975.translation: To the departed spirits, Secundius Attianus and Censorinia Matrausus for their wife and son who have died.
EDCS-11901975.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Secundius Attianus for his deceased wife and son, Censorinia Matrausus.

EDCS-11901976.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Tacitio Derissori filio iuveni defuncto et Saturniniae Saturninae coniiugi sic defun[ctae ------\n
EDCS-11901976.translation: To the departed spirits, for his son Tacitius Derissor, a young man who died, and for his wife Saturninia Saturnina, who died thus...
EDCS-11901976.summary: This is a funerary dedication by an unnamed individual for their deceased son, Tacitius Derissor, and deceased wife, Saturninia Saturnina.

EDCS-11901981.text_edition: \n Melio Ocosuono et Ocosuonio Gnato filio eius Mato uxor viva fecit\n
EDCS-11901981.translation: Mato, the wife, made this while alive for Melio Ocosuono and his son Gnato Ocosuonio.
EDCS-11901981.summary: This is a funerary epitaph made by Mato for her deceased husband Melio Ocosuono and son Gnato Ocosuonio.

EDCS-11901983.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, father of the fatherland, 22 Roman miles from Bagacum of the Nervii.
EDCS-11901983.summary: This inscription records a road milestone dedicated to Emperor Antoninus Pius, indicating a distance of 22 Roman miles from Bagacum.

EDCS-11901984.text_edition: \n honestam missionem dedimus Claudius Livianus praefectus praetorio subscripsit XIIII Kalendas Februarias Gallo et Bradua consulibus Auli Ampi Epaphroditi Quinti Apidi Thalli Publi Atini Trophimi Quinti Pompei Homeri Marci Iuni Eutychi Publi Cauli Vitalis Cai Iuli Aprilis\n
EDCS-11901984.translation: We granted an honorable discharge, signed by Claudius Livianus, praetorian prefect, on the 14th day before the Kalends of February, during the consulship of Gallus and Bradua, for Aulus Ampius Epaphroditus, Quintus Apidius Thallus, Publius Atinius Trophimus, Quintus Pompeius Homerus, Marcus Junius Eutychus, Publius Caelius Vitalis, Gaius Julius Aprilis.
EDCS-11901984.summary: This inscription records the granting of honorable discharges to several individuals, signed by Claudius Livianus, the praetorian prefect, during the consulship of Gallus and Bradua.

EDCS-11901987.translation: For Lucius Antaeus Parcus, son of Lucius Lucius Antaeus, [for his] 'diaglaucaeum'. For Lucius Antaeus Geminianus, [his] 'ambrosium' for eye ailments.
EDCS-11901987.summary: This inscription lists medicinal preparations, likely eye salves or treatments, intended for members of the Antaeus family.

EDCS-11901988.translation: Of Gaius Valerius Matti... eye ointment.
EDCS-11901988.summary: This inscription appears to be a label or record of an eye ointment belonging to Gaius Valerius Matti.

EDCS-11901989.translation: Fatalis's diacholes, to bitterness. Fatalis's Dionysius, to the lacunae. [3]anu[3] [3 cro]code[s].
EDCS-11901989.summary: This inscription appears to be fragmentary and possibly lists names or items related to difficulties or remedies, with lacunae indicating missing text.

EDCS-11901993.translation: Vitalis. Vitalis. Vitalis. C. T. C. [Caius] T. C. Marcus Gavius. Tertius Severus. [Ter]tius Severus. [Ter]tius Severus. Lucius Severius. T.C.L. G.P.
EDCS-11901993.summary: This inscription is a list of names, likely of individuals involved in a transaction or association, with some names repeated and abbreviations present.

EDCS-12000726.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Anillus.
EDCS-12000726.summary: A dedication to the departed spirits (Dis Manibus) for a person named Anillus, likely a tomb inscription.

EDCS-12000728.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Druca.
EDCS-12000728.summary: A dedication to the departed spirits (Dis Manibus) for a person named Druca, likely a tomb inscription.

EDCS-12000729.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Pisc[...].
EDCS-12000729.summary: A dedication to the departed spirits (Dis Manibus) for a person whose name begins with 'Pisc', likely a tomb inscription with a lacuna.

EDCS-12000730.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Titiola daughter of Secundus.
EDCS-12000730.summary: A dedication to the departed spirits (Dis Manibus) for Titiola, daughter of Secundus, likely a tomb inscription.

EDCS-12000733.translation: Sacred to Oglaius (?), Augustus. Ateuritus the shoemaker, having fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-12000733.summary: A dedication to Augustus by Ateuritus, a shoemaker, who willingly fulfilled his vow, likely an offering or shrine inscription.

EDCS-12000736.summary: This inscription consists of two personal names, Appinosa and Epasi, with no further context provided.

EDCS-12000742.translation: Heli[nas] rests here in peace. She lived 30 years. She died in September, on the 6th day.
EDCS-12000742.summary: A tombstone inscription recording the death of Helinas, who lived 30 years and died on September 6th.

EDCS-12000749.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deae Dianae Numini Sanctissimo Anulinus Polibius sic nummularius sacrae monetae Augusti nostri ex voto posuit votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-12000749.translation: In honor of the divine house, to the goddess Diana, to her Most Holy Numina, Anulinus Polibius, the money-changer of the sacred mint of our Augustus, placed this in fulfillment of a vow, having fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-12000749.summary: An inscription honoring the imperial family and the goddess Diana, dedicated by Anulinus Polibius, a money-changer, who fulfilled a vow related to the imperial mint.

EDCS-12000751.text_edition: \n Numinibus Augustorum deo Intarabo et Genio collegii fabrorum dolabrariorum quibus splendidissimus ordo templum sicut consaeptum est au curam agente Magissio Maina tum praefecto eorum decuria I Borinius Meritus Latinius Veco Covirius Saturn Iulius Sevianus Arvescius Nitius Mercatorius I QuadIII Ioincionius Securius I Mainutius Ner Quintius III Somanius Lucinus Ioincionius Cossus Ilvatius Primanus Mansuetius Primus Dagissius AIIinus Excingonius Secundus Covirius Tertius Secundius Secundinus Mainutius Silvinus Secundius Primus I A II issius AIIOTLG Messorius Primus Iulius saN Blussinius nnus Victorius Rusticus Iulius Lallus Secundius Secundinus VIVOIIV Vialti Iiallus Drappus Maciatus usticus vaHciaN(us) ammiN SOIV SAV IC decuria II LalIII I CI CI BeIbu II II OII RomacIr Secundius Ibli Secundius Ses Lugissius \n
EDCS-12000751.translation: To the divine Emperors and the god Intarabus and the Genius of the guild of carpenters with axes, for whom the most distinguished council has enclosed the temple, with the supervision of Magistius Maina, then their prefect, from decuria I: Borinius Meritus, Latinius Veco, Covirius Saturn, Iulius Sevianus, Arvescius Nitius, Mercatorius I, QuadIII, Ioincionius Securius I, Mainutius Ner, Quintius III, Somanius Lucinus, Ioincionius Cossus, Ilvatius Primanus, Mansuetius Primus, Dagissius AIIinus, Excingonius Secundus, Covirius Tertius, Secundius Secundinus, Mainutius Silvinus, Secundius Primus, I, AIIissius, Messorius Primus, Iulius, Blussinius, Victorius Rusticus, Iulius Lallus, Secundius Secundinus, VIVOIIV Vialti Iiallus, Drappus Maciatus, usticus vaHciaN(us), ammiN SOIV SAV IC. From decuria II: LalIII I CI CI BeIbu II II OII RomacIr, Secundius Ibli, Secundius Ses, Lugissius.
EDCS-12000751.summary: This is a dedication to imperial deities, a local god, and the Genius of the guild of carpenters, listing numerous members of the guild who contributed to the enclosure of a temple.

EDCS-12000754.translation: In honor of the Divine House. In the street of Senia, with Cossius Ursulus in charge. 'Touch me and beware of a fine if anyone loses the boundary stone; he will pay 12.5 denarii.'
EDCS-12000754.summary: This is a boundary stone inscription indicating a penalty for damaging or moving it, likely set up during the imperial period.

EDCS-12000757.summary: This fragment likely refers to a brewer named Capurillus, possibly from an epitaph or a building inscription, dating to the Roman Imperial period.
