EDCS-12000759.translation: to Genialis, son of [---], Maiianius Iunian/[---] VMODATDOVI/[---]
EDCS-12000759.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, possibly an epitaph or a dedication, mentioning a person named Genialis and another named Maiianius Iunian/[---], from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12000760.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Primia Firma, to her most beloved wife, deceased, Sextus placed this monument, and for himself, while alive, he arranged for it to be made.
EDCS-12000760.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Sextus for his deceased wife, Primia Firma, and also for himself, indicating it was commissioned during his lifetime.

EDCS-12000761.translation: Marcus Sextilius, son of Marcus, of the Pomentina tribe, is buried here.
EDCS-12000761.summary: This is a simple epitaph identifying the deceased as Marcus Sextilius, son of Marcus, from the Pomentina tribe, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12000775.translation: Arcadius, who lived for 11 years and 4 months, rests here in peace; his father and mother placed this monument for him.
EDCS-12000775.summary: This is a Christian epitaph recording the death of a child, Arcadius, who lived 11 years and 4 months, with the monument placed by his parents.

EDCS-12000777.text_edition: \n Hic iacet Lycontia quae vixit annos LXX Retecius titulum posuit\n
EDCS-12000777.translation: Lycontia, who lived 70 years, lies here. Retecius placed the monument.
EDCS-12000777.summary: This is an epitaph recording the death of Lycontia at the age of 70, with the monument placed by Retecius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12000779.translation: Perses, the dearest husband, who lived 45 years, rests here in peace; he placed the monument.
EDCS-12000779.summary: This is an epitaph for Perses, described as a dearest husband who lived 45 years, with the monument placed by himself, suggesting it was a pre-arranged burial structure.

EDCS-12000780.translation: [---]minus, [---]anus, twenty years old(?), Sedulus placed the monument [---]
EDCS-12000780.summary: This is a fragmentary epitaph, likely recording the age of the deceased as twenty years old, with Sedulus identified as the one who placed the monument, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12000784.summary: A funerary inscription for Quesusianus, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-12000785.translation: Holy good name, pious name, holy name. I bind you to holy Diana, Rodanum whom Anula Regula bore, mistress of the house, that I may have such great fame. I bind Bonarium to the house. [---]ti[---]tai[---]otun
EDCS-12000785.summary: A magical inscription invoking the goddess Diana and possibly a local deity (Rodanum) to bind someone named Bonarium and for the author to gain fame, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12000786.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription naming Nestoria, likely indicating she was born to someone.

EDCS-12000787.translation: I invoke you, Yibal Foqoirm, in your cult place, Diana and Mars, that you may vindicate me. Bind Eusebius in chains and vindicate me. Eusebius, the deposited one.
EDCS-12000787.summary: A magical curse inscription invoking Diana and Mars to bind and vindicate the speaker against someone named Eusebius.

EDCS-12000789.translation: If you [heard] the god, who heard you, the fraudulent action which (she) wrought against me, Hostilla, born in Racatia...
EDCS-12000789.summary: A fragment of a legal or magical text, possibly a curse, concerning a fraudulent act by Hostilla.

EDCS-12000792.summary: A funerary inscription recording the deposited name of Prissia.

EDCS-12000795.summary: A list of names, possibly family members or a record of inheritance, featuring variations of the name 'Ursus'.

EDCS-12000797.summary: A fragmentary inscription that appears to record a personal name, possibly a nickname or gentilicium.

EDCS-12000804.translation: For Mercury. Marcus Cassius Venustus willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-12000804.summary: A dedication to the god Mercury by Marcus Cassius Venustus, who fulfilled a vow.

EDCS-12000809.translation: To the Divine Shades. Lucius Securius Melausus and Venustiae Dedissae [fulfilled their vow].
EDCS-12000809.summary: A funerary dedication to the Divine Shades by Lucius Securius Melausus and Venustiae Dedissae.

EDCS-12000810.translation: To the departed spirits. Dexterius Plantintinus had this made for himself while alive, and for his deceased wife Mottia Victorina, and also for his son Vicentius.
EDCS-12000810.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Dexterius Plantintinus for himself and his family.

EDCS-12000811.translation: To the departed spirits. Daguo Dagsillus Ebthocatus(?) made this for himself while alive.
EDCS-12000811.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Daguo Dagsillus Ebthocatus(?) for himself.

EDCS-12200010.summary: This inscription records a restoration, possibly of a public work, by an individual named Marius, with a date that is uncertain.

EDCS-12200011.translation: To the departed spirits. Apollinaris, freedman of Quintus Livius Castor, Augustalis and member of the college of the six magistrates.
EDCS-12200011.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Apollinaris, a freedman of a prominent citizen, likely from the 1st or 2nd century AD.

EDCS-12200012.translation: To the departed spirits. For Sextus Publicius Decmanus, freedman of the colony of the Mediomatrici.
EDCS-12200012.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sextus Publicius Decmanus, a freedman of the colony of the Mediomatrici, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-12200013.translation: For Iulius Cervessarius [---], from Mediomatricum, lived <50>(?) years [---]. His wife placed this for him while alive.
EDCS-12200013.summary: This funerary inscription records the life and death of Iulius Cervessarius, set up by his wife.

EDCS-12200014.translation: The sons took care to place this for Casatus Caratus the potter.
EDCS-12200014.summary: This inscription records the sons commissioning a monument for their father, Casatus Caratus, who was a potter.

EDCS-12200015.translation: To the departed spirits. For Acisillia Fabr[i]cilla.
EDCS-12200015.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Acisillia Fabr[i]cilla.

EDCS-12200016.translation: To the departed spirits. For Aeliola.
EDCS-12200016.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aeliola.

EDCS-12200017.translation: To the departed spirits. For Agisilla.
EDCS-12200017.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Agisilla.

EDCS-12200018.translation: To the shades of the departed. Attia...
EDCS-12200018.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Attia, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12200020.translation: To the shades of the departed. Cantedo, son of Sextulus.
EDCS-12200020.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Cantedo, son of Sextulus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12200022.translation: To the shades of the departed. Cartulla.
EDCS-12200022.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Cartulla, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12200023.translation: To the shades of the departed. Castus.
EDCS-12200023.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Castus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12200026.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication to Cintusmus by a sibling, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12200027.translation: To the shades of the departed. Deccosus.
EDCS-12200027.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Deccosus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12200029.translation: To the shades of the departed. Emerita. Divicius, son of Iancus, dedicated from his own means.
EDCS-12200029.summary: This is a funerary inscription showing Divicius dedicating a monument from his own funds for Emerita, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12200030.translation: ... Diucius dedicated from his own funds.
EDCS-12200030.summary: This funerary inscription records Diucius dedicating a monument from his own funds, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12200031.translation: To the shades of the departed. For Heutychia, his former foster-child, Philetianus, in remembrance.
EDCS-12200031.summary: This is a funerary inscription where Philetianus commemorates his foster-child Heutychia, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12200032.translation: For Firmus. Vera, his mother, for his memory.
EDCS-12200032.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Vera for her son Firmus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12200033.translation: To the departed spirits. The heirs of Focatus took care to erect this.
EDCS-12200033.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by the heirs of Focatus.

EDCS-12200034.translation: To the departed spirits. For Decimus Julius Primanus.
EDCS-12200034.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Decimus Julius Primanus.

EDCS-12200035.translation: To the departed spirits. For Julius Vassillus. Maritumus and Gentilis, his sons.
EDCS-12200035.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by the sons Maritumus and Gentilis for their father Julius Vassillus.

EDCS-12200037.translation: To the departed spirits. For Julia.
EDCS-12200037.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Julia.

EDCS-12200038.translation: To the departed spirits. For Julia Matto. Martius [erected this].
EDCS-12200038.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Martius for Julia Matto.

EDCS-12200039.translation: To the departed spirits. Severius Carillus set this up for Liccatulia.
EDCS-12200039.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Severius Carillus for Liccatulia.

EDCS-12200040.summary: This is a funerary inscription potentially dedicated to Liv...ina by her husband Attillus.

EDCS-12200041.translation: To the departed spirits. For Lucina.
EDCS-12200041.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Lucina.

EDCS-12200042.translation: To the departed spirits. For Maia.
EDCS-12200042.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Maia.

EDCS-12200043.summary: This is a funerary inscription identifying Maia as the daughter of Jocus.

EDCS-12200044.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Mainno [---].
EDCS-12200044.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed, with the name of the deceased partially preserved.

EDCS-12200046.summary: This inscription appears to be a funerary dedication to Marina, a freedwoman.

EDCS-12200047.translation: [---]ax Movesi placed this monument for his son Martialis.
EDCS-12200047.summary: This funerary epitaph records that Movesi placed a monument for his son Martialis.

EDCS-12200049.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Marcus Melodius Avitus.
EDCS-12200049.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed, naming Marcus Melodius Avitus.

EDCS-12200050.translation: [---] to Mercurialis, who lived 1 year, 5 months, and 22 days. Leda, his nurse, and Chrysopaes, his fellow foster-brother, placed this monument in memory.
EDCS-12200050.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of a child named Mercurialis and is dedicated by his nurse and fellow foster-brother.

EDCS-12200051.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Atledo(?).
EDCS-12200051.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed, with the name Atledo preserved with a query.

EDCS-12200052.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Ovniccus.
EDCS-12200052.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to the spirits of the departed, naming Ovniccus.

EDCS-12200053.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Pacata, daughter of Pacatus.
EDCS-12200053.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Pacata, the daughter of Pacatus.

EDCS-12200054.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Pasvius Priscus.
EDCS-12200054.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed, naming Pasvius Priscus.

EDCS-12200055.translation: [To the spirits] of the departed. [---]ius Tittausus, son of [---], placed this monument.
EDCS-12200055.summary: This is a funerary inscription, likely for Pompeius Tittausus, placed by himself or a family member.

EDCS-12200056.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Poppusa.
EDCS-12200056.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Poppusa.

EDCS-12200057.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Quintus.
EDCS-12200057.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Quintus.

EDCS-12200058.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Rustica.
EDCS-12200058.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Rustica.

EDCS-12200059.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Sabineius Sextus; his wife set this up.
EDCS-12200059.summary: This is a funerary dedication set up by a wife for her husband, Sabineius Sextus.

EDCS-12200060.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Saevius Ingenuus.
EDCS-12200060.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Saevius Ingenuus.

EDCS-12200061.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Salvia Catulla.
EDCS-12200061.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Salvia Catulla.

EDCS-12200063.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Servianus, son of Servanus.
EDCS-12200063.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Servianus, son of Servanus.

EDCS-12200064.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Vibius Severus.
EDCS-12200064.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Vibius Severus.

EDCS-12200065.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Titullina, freedwoman of Iunius Priscus.
EDCS-12200065.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Titullina, a freedwoman of Iunius Priscus.

EDCS-12200066.summary: This is a funerary dedication fragment where a mother dedicates the monument to Touto (with a name uncertain due to damage).

EDCS-12200067.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Vitalis, son of Tiberinus.
EDCS-12200067.summary: A funerary dedication to Vitalis, son of Tiberinus.

EDCS-12200095.translation: Here rests in peace Aralainus, who lived about sixty years, for whom his dear wife and sons erected this tombstone.
EDCS-12200095.summary: A funerary epitaph for Aralainus, erected by his wife and sons, who lived about sixty years.

EDCS-12200097.translation: Here lies Paulus, who lived for 3 years and 45 days.
EDCS-12200097.summary: A funerary epitaph for Paulus, recording his short lifespan of 3 years and 45 days.

EDCS-12200110.translation: [To] Innatus, to Sett[---] / [---] Solituma[e] / [to] Censorina, wife / [and] Caratilla, daughter / [---]a Carassoun[a(?)]
EDCS-12200110.summary: A fragmentary funerary dedication likely honoring multiple family members including Censorina and Caratilla.

EDCS-12200114.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Vibia A[---]II[---].
EDCS-12200114.summary: A fragmentary funerary dedication to Vibia.

EDCS-12200117.translation: To Senecianus SE[---] / [---] and Cesti[---] / Nevoni[---]
EDCS-12200117.summary: A fragmentary inscription possibly dedicating a monument to Senecianus and others.

EDCS-12200118.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Iulos, son of Iunius.
EDCS-12200118.summary: A funerary dedication to Iulos, son of Iunius.

EDCS-12200119.translation: To Siora, daughter of Cotnus, and to Cabrilla, daughter
EDCS-12200119.summary: A funerary dedication to Siora, daughter of Cotnus, and possibly to Cabrilla, daughter.

EDCS-12200123.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Priscianus, son of Victorinus.
EDCS-12200123.summary: A funerary dedication to Priscianus, son of Victorinus.

EDCS-12200127.translation: To the spirits of the departed, [P]aternus.

EDCS-12400147.text_edition: \n Tiberius Claudius Drusi filius Caesar Augustus Germanicus pontifex maximus tribunicia potestate V imperator XI consul III designatus IIII Vorganium milia passuum VIIII\n
EDCS-12400147.translation: To Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, son of Drusus, Pontifex Maximus, with tribunician power for the fifth time, Imperator for the eleventh time, Consul for the third time, designated Consul for the fourth time, 9 miles from Vorganium.
EDCS-12400147.summary: This milestone records a distance of 9 miles from Vorganium, dedicated to Emperor Claudius, likely during his reign (41-54 AD).

EDCS-12400242.translation: To our lord, the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maximian, the Senior, Pious, Fortunate, Unconquered Augustus.
EDCS-12400242.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the co-emperor Maximian, likely part of a monument or inscription marking a distance, dating to his reign (286-305 AD).

EDCS-12400244.text_edition: \n Imperatore Caesare Lucio Septimio Severo Pio Pertinace Augusto Arabico Adiabenico Parthico maximo patre patriae consule III et Imperatore Caesare Marco Aurelio Antonino Pio Augusto Felice et [Geta nobilissimo] [Caesare] curante Lucio P Postumo legato Auggustorum pro praetore ab Augusta Suessionum leugae VII\n
EDCS-12400244.translation: Under Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus, Arabicus, Adiabenicus, Parthicus Maximus, father of the fatherland, Consul for the third time, and Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Augustus Felix, and [Geta nobilissimus Caesar], under the administration of Lucius P. Postumius, Legate of the Augusti, 7 leagues from Augusta Suessionum.
EDCS-12400244.summary: This milestone indicates a distance of 7 leagues from Augusta Suessionum, during the consulship of Septimius Severus and Caracalla, with Geta also mentioned, dating to 202 AD.

EDCS-12400245.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Augustus Britannicus Maximus, with tribunician power for the 14th time, Imperator for the second time, Consul for the fourth time, father of the fatherland, proconsul, 7 leagues from Augusta Suessionum.
EDCS-12400245.summary: This milestone records a distance of 7 leagues from Augusta Suessionum, dedicated to Emperor Caracalla, likely during his reign (198-217 AD).

EDCS-12400247.translation: To our lord Galerius Valerius Maximianus, the most noble Caesar, from the civitas Ambianorum, 1 league from Samarobriva.
EDCS-12400247.summary: This inscription marks a distance of 1 league from Samarobriva, dedicated to the Caesar Galerius Maximian, likely during his tetrarchic rule (293-305 AD).

EDCS-12400248.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Piavonius Victorinus, the Pious, Fortunate, Unconquered Augustus, Pontifex Maximus, with tribunician power, Consul, father of the fatherland, proconsul, from the civitas Remorum, 4 leagues.
EDCS-12400248.summary: This milestone records a distance of 4 leagues, dedicated to the usurper Emperor Victorinus, likely during his reign (269-271 AD).

EDCS-12400257.translation: To Emperor Caesar Nerva Augustus, Pontifex Maximus, [with tribunician] power, [father of the fatherland], Consul for the third time, from the civitas Med(iomatricorum).
EDCS-12400257.summary: This inscription, likely from a milestone, honors Emperor Nerva, mentioning his consulship for the third time and his relation to the civitas of the Med(iomatrici), dating to his reign (96-98 AD).

EDCS-12400268.text_edition: \n Domino nostro Flavio Claudio Constantino nobilissimo Caesari leugas XV\n
EDCS-12400268.translation: To our lord Flavius Claudius Constantinus, the most noble Caesar, 15 leagues.
EDCS-12400268.summary: This inscription, likely a milestone, records a distance of 15 leagues and is dedicated to the Caesar Constantine (likely Constantine I), dating to his reign as Caesar (c. 306-307 AD or later).

EDCS-12400270.text_edition: \n Tiberius Claudius Drusi filius Caesar Augustus Germanicus pontifex maximus tribunicia potestate III imperator III pater patriae consul III designatus IIII Andemantunno milia passuum XXII\n
EDCS-12400270.translation: To Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, son of Drusus, Pontifex Maximus, with tribunician power for the third time, Imperator for the third time, father of the fatherland, Consul for the third time, designated Consul for the fourth time, 22 miles from Andemantunnum.
EDCS-12400270.summary: This milestone records a distance of 22 miles from Andemantunnum, dedicated to Emperor Claudius, likely during his reign (41-54 AD).

EDCS-12400271.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Traiano Hadriano Augusto pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate V consuli III patri patriae Andematunno milia passuum XIII\n
EDCS-12400271.translation: To Emperor Caesar Traianus Hadrianus Augustus, Pontifex Maximus, with tribunician power for the fifth time, Consul for the third time, father of the fatherland, 13 miles from Andematunnum.
EDCS-12400271.summary: This milestone indicates a distance of 13 miles from Andematunnum, dedicated to Emperor Hadrian, dating to his fifth tribunician power grant (c. 121-122 AD).

EDCS-12400272.text_edition: \n Tiberius Claudius Drusi filius Caesar Augustus Germanicus pontifex maximus tribunicia potestate III imperator III pater patriae consul III designatus IIII Andemantunno milia passuum XII\n
EDCS-12400272.translation: To Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, son of Drusus, high priest, with the tribunician power for the 3rd time, imperator for the 3rd time, father of the country, consul for the 3rd time, consul-designate for the 4th time, 12 miles from Andemantunnum.
EDCS-12400272.summary: This milestone records Emperor Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus and the distance from a Gallic settlement, likely dating to his reign (41-54 AD).

EDCS-12400274.text_edition: \n Domino nostro Flavio Crispo Invicto nobilissimo Caesare civitate Leucorum leugae VIII\n
EDCS-12400274.translation: To our lord Flavius Crispus, unconquered, most noble Caesar, 8 leagues from the city of the Leuci.
EDCS-12400274.summary: This milestone or boundary marker is dedicated to Caesar Flavius Crispus and indicates a distance from the civitas of the Leuci, likely dating to the early 4th century AD.

EDCS-12400275.text_edition: \n Domino nostro Flavio Claudio Constantino nobil<i=L>ssimo Caesar<i=F> civitate Leucorum leugae VIII \n
EDCS-12400275.translation: To our lord Flavius Claudius Constantinus, most noble Caesar, 8 leagues from the city of the Leuci.
EDCS-12400275.summary: This milestone or boundary marker is dedicated to Emperor Constantine the Great and indicates a distance from the civitas of the Leuci, likely dating to the early 4th century AD.

EDCS-12400277.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari divi Traiani Parthici filio divi Nervae nepoti Traiano Had[riano ------\n
EDCS-12400277.translation: To Emperor Caesar Trajan Hadrianus, son of the deified Trajan Parthicus, grandson of the deified Nerva...
EDCS-12400277.summary: This inscription, though fragmentary, is a dedication to Emperor Hadrian, likely on a public monument, dating to his reign (117-138 AD).

EDCS-12400278.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Marco Cassianio Latinio Postumo Pio Felici Invicto Augusto pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate X consuli IIII patri patriae a civitate Mediomatricorum leugae XIII\n
EDCS-12400278.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Cassianius Latinus Postumus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, high priest, with tribunician power for the 10th time, consul for the 4th time, father of the country, 13 leagues from the civitas of the Mediomatrici.
EDCS-12400278.summary: This milestone honors the 'Gallic Emperor' Postumus, detailing his titles and the distance from the territory of the Mediomatrici, dating to his reign (260-269 AD).

EDCS-12400279.summary: This fragmentary inscription is a dedication to the emperor Galerius Maximinus, likely on a public monument, dating to the Tetrarchic period (late 3rd to early 4th century AD).

EDCS-12400284.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, Arabicus, Adiabenicus, Parthicus Maximus, Britannicus Maximus, high priest, with tribunician power for the 15th time, imperator for the 2nd time, consul for the 3rd time, father of the country, 9 leagues from Augusta Treverorum.
EDCS-12400284.summary: This milestone honors Emperor Caracalla, listing his extensive titles and the distance from Trier (Augusta Treverorum), dating to his reign (198-217 AD).

EDCS-12400285.translation: To Emperor Caesar Flavius Valerius Constantinus, Pius Felix Invictus, most noble Caesar, son of the deified Constantius, of the blessed Augustus.
EDCS-12400285.summary: This dedicatory inscription honors Caesar Constantine the Great, proclaiming his lineage and virtues, likely dating to the period he was junior emperor (c. 307-324 AD).

EDCS-12400289.text_edition: \n Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus pontifex maximus tribunicia potestate IIII imperator VIII consul designatus IIII pater patriae ab Augusta milia passum LIIII\n
EDCS-12400289.translation: Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, high priest, with tribunician power for the 4th time, imperator for the 8th time, consul-designate for the 4th time, father of the country, 54 miles from Augusta.
EDCS-12400289.summary: This milestone records Emperor Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus and the distance from Augusta (likely Augusta Treverorum), dating to his reign (41-54 AD).

EDCS-12400291.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Piavronius Victorinus, Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, high priest, with tribunician power, consul, proconsul, 20 leagues from Augusta Treverorum.
EDCS-12400291.summary: This milestone honors the 'Gallic Emperor' Victorinus, detailing his titles and the distance from Trier (Augusta Treverorum), dating to his reign (269-271 AD).

EDCS-12400293.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Trajan Hadrian Augustus, son of the deified Trajan the Parthian, grandson of the deified Nerva, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 5th time, consul for the 3rd time, father of the fatherland, from the colony Augusta Treverorum, 22 miles.
EDCS-12400293.summary: This is a milestone or boundary marker set up by the colony Augusta Treverorum, recording a distance of 22 miles to the emperor Trajan Hadrian Augustus.

EDCS-12400294.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 2nd time, consul for the 2nd time, father of the fatherland, from the colony Augusta Treverorum, 22 Roman miles.
EDCS-12400294.summary: This is a milestone or boundary marker set up by the colony Augusta Treverorum, recording a distance of 22 miles to the emperor Antoninus Pius.

EDCS-13302670.translation: If you give, give // If you are willing.
EDCS-13302670.summary: This is a very short, possibly votive inscription, with a conditional offer or plea.

EDCS-13303248.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating the tomb or memorial to the departed spirit of a person named Bacca.

EDCS-13303249.translation: To the departed spirits, in memory of Iberna, who lived 24 years.
EDCS-13303249.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating Iberna, who died at the age of 24.

EDCS-13303251.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Rusoniae Nonnae Maianus Primi cassidarius coniugi et sibi vivus posuit\n
EDCS-13303251.translation: To the departed spirits, in memory of Rusonia Nonna. Maianus Primi, a gladiator, set this up for his wife and himself while he was alive.
EDCS-13303251.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Maianus Primi, a gladiator, for his wife Rusonia Nonna and himself.

EDCS-13303252.translation: To the departed spirits and in memory of Avita, daughter of Miscuron.
EDCS-13303252.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating the tomb or memorial to Avita, daughter of Miscuron.

EDCS-13303253.text_edition: \n Tiberio Claudio Caesari Augusto Germanico pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate VIII consuli IIII imperatori XVI patri patriae censori civitas Sulbanectium publice\n
EDCS-13303253.translation: To Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 8th time, consul for the 4th time, imperator for the 16th time, father of the fatherland, censor, by the community of Sulbanectium, publicly.
EDCS-13303253.summary: This inscription records a public dedication by the community of Sulbanectium to the emperor Claudius.

EDCS-13303254.translation: Sacred to Mercury Augustus. Gaius Julius Healissus has paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-13303254.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Mercury Augustus by Gaius Julius Healissus.

EDCS-13303257.translation: To the departed spirits of Abacius, son of Gavernis. // To the departed spirits of Dedicca, daughter of Caracillus. // To the departed spirits of Suhetius, son of Cruponis.
EDCS-13303257.summary: This inscription contains three separate funerary dedications to Abacius, Dedicca, and Suhetius.

EDCS-13303258.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Expectatus, son of Silibicca. To the spirits of the underworld, for Propincquus, son of Silibicca.
EDCS-13303258.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates two individuals, Expectatus and Propincquus, both sons of Silibicca, likely within the same tomb or monument.

EDCS-13303259.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Pollienius Domestica. To the spirits of the underworld.
EDCS-13303259.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Pollienius Domestica, likely a woman, with a repetition of the dedication to the spirits of the underworld.

EDCS-13303262.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, likely recording that Sextus made or dedicated a monument.

EDCS-13303266.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Cariano Belliani filio et Felici Cariani filio Bellianus Boudilli et Augusta Crobi filia patres ponendum curaverunt\n
EDCS-13303266.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Carianus, son of Bellianus, and for Felix, son of Cariani. Bellianus, son of Boudillus, and Augusta, daughter of Crobus, parents, took care to place this.
EDCS-13303266.summary: This funerary inscription records the parents, Bellianus and Augusta, dedicating a monument to their sons Carianus and Felix.

EDCS-13303267.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Publius Frontinus Venulinus.
EDCS-13303267.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated to Publius Frontinus Venulinus.

EDCS-13303268.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Lucius Eustachius.
EDCS-13303268.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated to Lucius Eustachius.

EDCS-13303269.summary: This is a highly fragmentary inscription, possibly indicating the father of Publius Atrectus.

EDCS-13303271.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Catullia Paulina.
EDCS-13303271.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated to Catullia Paulina.

EDCS-13303272.translation: In honor of the divine house, to the god Mercury. Publius Hicilius P(---)eralis fulfilled his vow, deservedly, to Par(---)cilius Pluncus.
EDCS-13303272.summary: This inscription records Publius Hicilius P(---)eralis dedicating a monument to Mercury, fulfilling a vow for Par(---)cilius Pluncus, in honor of the imperial family.

EDCS-13303280.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Herculi Saxsetano vexsillarii! legionis XIIII geminae Martiae victricis qui sub curas sic Cai Appi Capitonis |(centurionis) legionis eiusdem votum solverunt libentes laeti merito\n
EDCS-13303280.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and to Hercules Saxsetanus, the standard-bearers of the Fourteenth Legion Gemina Martia Victrix, who under the command of the centurion Gaius Appius Capito of the same legion, fulfilled their vow willingly, gladly, and deservedly.
EDCS-13303280.summary: This inscription records the standard-bearers of the Fourteenth Legion Gemina Martia Victrix, under the command of Centurion Gaius Appius Capito, fulfilling a vow to Jupiter and Hercules.

EDCS-13303282.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Regina and her daughter Attiola.
EDCS-13303282.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the spirits of the underworld for Regina and her daughter Attiola.

EDCS-13303283.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Consillianus.
EDCS-13303283.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the spirits of the underworld for Consillianus.

EDCS-13303286.translation: To Mercury. Catullinus, son of Meritus, freely and deservedly fulfills his vow.
EDCS-13303286.summary: This is a votive inscription to Mercury, dedicated by Catullinus, son of Meritus.

EDCS-13303390.translation: With Anaillus, 3 days; with Tertius, 1 day; 3 days for rain; 6 days for preparing a rain-battered mortar; 1 day for tiles in the field of Rassura; 1 day for Paterclus.
EDCS-13303390.summary: This inscription appears to record the number of days allocated for various tasks or activities, possibly related to construction or labor, with specific mentions of people and materials.

EDCS-13303395.translation: Of Quintus Germanus Securus, remedies for old scars // Of Quintus Germanus Securus, a plaster for roughness.
EDCS-13303395.summary: This inscription lists medicinal preparations or remedies for scars and skin roughness, attributed to Quintus Germanus Securus.

EDCS-13303396.translation: Of Ingenuus Aurelius Tiberius, a statuette for brightness // Of Lucius Longinius Albus, son of Lucius.
EDCS-13303396.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a statuette for brightness by Ingenuus Aurelius Tiberius, followed by the name of Lucius Longinius Albus.

EDCS-13303397.translation: Of Lucius Titus Martialis, a powder for eye inflammation // Of Lucius Titus Martialis, a myrrh-scented eye-wash // Martialis, son of Titus.
EDCS-13303397.summary: This inscription lists eye medications, including one for inflammation and another scented with myrrh, attributed to Lucius Titus Martialis.

EDCS-13303399.translation: Of Caius Censor Verus, a remedy for scars // Of Caius Censor Verus, a good-smelling preparation for a condition // Of Caius Censor Verus, a crocodile-based remedy for an everted eyelid // Of Caius Censor Verus, a 'palladium' preparation for roughness.
EDCS-13303399.summary: This inscription details a series of medicinal preparations or remedies for various ailments, such as scars, skin conditions, and eye problems, all attributed to Caius Censor Verus.

EDCS-13303409.translation: To the divine will of Augustus // Gemellus, an 'antistes' (leader/priest).
EDCS-13303409.summary: This inscription is dedicated to the divine will of Augustus and mentions Gemellus, likely a religious official.

EDCS-13303412.summary: This is a personal inscription expressing remembrance from one sister to another.

EDCS-13303420.summary: This is a tombstone inscription likely commemorating a pious individual, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13600209.translation: From the pottery workshop of Paternus, belonging to the two Junii, Mellissus and Melissa.
EDCS-13600209.summary: This inscription identifies a pottery workshop and its owners, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13900145.text_edition: \n Castor Pollus sic Aelena sic Iobis sic Lyda sic Agamemnon Quodvoltdeus sic Folox so medix Andegasi pone Florus Eleni Criscentia sic Andegasus Theodulus Calemerus Secundus Paregorius Paregorius Felix Felex sic Eusebius Eusebius\n
EDCS-13900145.translation: Castor, Pollux, thus Elena, thus Iobis, thus Lyda, thus Agamemnon, Quodvoltdeus, thus Felix, so physician Andegasus, placed here Florus, Eleni, Criscentia, thus Andegasus, Theodulus, Calemerus, Secundus, Paregorius, Paregorius, Felix, Felex, thus Eusebius, Eusebius.
EDCS-13900145.summary: This inscription appears to be a list of names, possibly slaves or freedmen, associated with a household or estate, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-14800054.translation: To the spirits of the underworld; of Benuccha, daughter of Messicus.
EDCS-14800054.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the departed spirits for Benuccha, daughter of Messicus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-14800055.translation: Hermes made this for his most dutiful wife, Ulpia Hygeia.
EDCS-14800055.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Hermes for his wife Ulpia Hygeia, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-14800062.translation: Probini's gems for roughnesses // Probini's celestial carvings // Probini's jewels for roughnesses // Victorini's palladium for darkness.
EDCS-14800062.summary: This inscription lists types of decorative or protective objects, possibly related to jewelry or amulets, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-14800063.translation: From the medicinal preparations of Tiberius Claudius Mercator for clarity // [From the medicinal preparations] of Tiberius Ol[---] Mero
EDCS-14800063.summary: This inscription seems to refer to medicinal preparations or remedies from individuals named Tiberius Claudius Mercator and Tiberius Ol[---] Mero, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15300300.translation: To our lord, the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maximian Senior, Pious, Fortunate, Augustus.
EDCS-15300300.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Maximian, dating to his reign as Augustus (c. 286-305 AD).

EDCS-15500019.summary: This is a boundary marker or land ownership inscription for Lucius C(...), dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16000491.translation: Caius Terentius Creticus's basilicon // Caius Terentius Creticus's chloron for burns // Caius Terentius Creticus's rhon (?) // Caius Terentius Creticus's POSCOMIVIV
EDCS-16000491.summary: This inscription lists several items or substances, possibly related to cosmetics or medicine, associated with Caius Terentius Creticus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16200647.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely part of a tombstone, that lists names or epithets.

EDCS-16200995.text_edition: \n Leno Marti et Xulsigiis Lucius Virius Diseto votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-16200995.translation: Lucius Virius Diseto willingly and deservedly paid his vow to Lenus Mars and Xulsigius.
EDCS-16200995.summary: This is a dedication of a votive offering to the deities Lenus Mars and Xulsigius by Lucius Virius Diseto.

EDCS-16300561.summary: This is a very short inscription, possibly a funerary text or a simple marker, containing two names.

EDCS-16400026.translation: Whatever R/*acanus and his advocate have, they have.
EDCS-16400026.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, possibly a legal notice or a witty epigram related to ownership or claims.

EDCS-16400376.translation: Let's drink. Pulcher and Auriga. Hercules and Antheus.
EDCS-16400376.summary: This inscription appears to be a convivial or possibly a funerary epigram, mentioning individuals and mythological figures.

EDCS-16400595.translation: African products, excellent quality, 19 pounds and a half-pound, plus three half-pounds. Total: 17 pounds and 19 unciae.
EDCS-16400595.summary: This inscription records a sale or delivery of goods, specifying weights and perhaps the seller or recipient, dated by the IIIS XVIIII notation.

EDCS-16500081.summary: This inscription marks the workshop belonging to someone named Afronis.

EDCS-16500082.summary: This inscription identifies the workshop of Aiccardus.

EDCS-16500085.summary: This inscription indicates the workshop belonging to Lairino.

EDCS-16500088.summary: This inscription denotes the workshop of Uuba.

EDCS-16600301.translation: Of Marcus Iovincatus Sumaronis and his wife Sollia.
EDCS-16600301.summary: This inscription likely records the names of a couple, possibly on a funerary monument or property marker.

EDCS-16700180.summary: This inscription indicates the origin of a product or artifact from the workshop of Arda(c)ius.

EDCS-16700181.summary: This inscription indicates the origin of a product or artifact from the workshop of Secundus.

EDCS-16700314.translation: To the departed spirits of Maclonus and his mother Cintuma.
EDCS-16700314.summary: This is a dedication to the spirits of the deceased, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-16800438.summary: This inscription attributes the work to Uxopillus, possibly an artisan or craftsman.

EDCS-17200002.translation: Marcus Valerius Sedulus's penicillium for all kinds of eye inflammation, from egg. // Marcus Valerius Sedulus's diasmurnes after an attack of inflammation, from egg. // Marcus Valerius Sedulus's euodes for roughness and old scars. // Marcus Valerius Sedulus's diamisus crocodes for old roughness.
EDCS-17200002.summary: This text lists several medicinal preparations by Marcus Valerius Sedulus for various eye conditions and skin ailments, likely from a medical text or advertisement.

EDCS-18300822.translation: Gentianus's dialepidos for roughness. // Gentianus's leniment for attacks of inflammation. // Gentianus's herbacium for clarity. // Gentianus's diamisus for old scars.
EDCS-18300822.summary: This inscription lists several medicinal preparations attributed to Gentianus for various ailments, likely from a medical text or advertisement.

EDCS-18500164.translation: Secundus Antonius's crocodes for roughness. // Antony's crocodes dialepidos, physician.
EDCS-18500164.summary: This inscription refers to medicinal preparations, possibly eye salves, by Secundus Antonius and a physician named Antonius, likely from a medical text or advertisement.

EDCS-20500300.text_edition: \n Sincorio Crispi filio Carapantho faciendum curavit Gamago Craucilli filius scribsit sic Gaverius lapicida\n
EDCS-20500300.translation: Gamago, son of Craucillus, saw to its construction for his son Sincorius Crispus, Carapanthus. The stonecutter wrote as follows: Gaverius.
EDCS-20500300.summary: This funerary inscription records the deceased Sincorius Crispus, son of Carapanthus, for whom his father Gamago commissioned the monument, with the stonecutter Gaverius identified.

EDCS-20500304.translation: Lucius Surius and Quintus [served as] standard-bearers.
EDCS-20500304.summary: This inscription records Lucius Surius and Quintus as having served as standard-bearers, likely in a military context.

EDCS-20500309.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription with names, likely part of a funerary monument.

EDCS-20500319.translation: To the spirits of the departed. The heir had this placed for Marino, son of Pacatus, and for his wife Materna.
EDCS-20500319.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a heir for their relatives, Marino and Materna.

EDCS-23400559.translation: To the goddess Nehalennia, Sextus Severinius Severus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-23400559.summary: This votive inscription records Sextus Severinius Severus fulfilling a vow to the goddess Nehalennia.

EDCS-23400560.translation: To the goddess Nehalennia, Quintus Julius Frontinus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-23400560.summary: This votive inscription records Quintus Julius Frontinus fulfilling a vow to the goddess Nehalennia.

EDCS-23400561.translation: To the goddess Nehalennia, Agilius Secundus, a beneficiarius consularis, for himself and his family, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-23400561.summary: This votive inscription records Agilius Secundus, a beneficiarius consularis, fulfilling a vow to the goddess Nehalennia for his family.

EDCS-23400562.text_edition: \n Deae Nehalenniae Varausius Ahucconis votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-23400562.translation: To the goddess Nehalennia, Varausius Ahucconis willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-23400562.summary: This votive inscription records Varausius Ahucconis fulfilling a vow to the goddess Nehalennia.

EDCS-23400563.text_edition: \n Deae Nehalenniae Caius Aurelius Verus negotiator Britannicianus ex voto libens merito\n
EDCS-23400563.translation: To the goddess Nehalennia, Gaius Aurelius Verus, a merchant from Britannia, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-23400563.summary: This votive inscription records Gaius Aurelius Verus, a merchant from Britannia, fulfilling a vow to the goddess Nehalennia.

EDCS-23400564.translation: To the goddess Nehalennia, Vacrenus... by order...
EDCS-23400564.summary: This fragmentary votive inscription records a vow made to the goddess Nehalennia, possibly under order.

EDCS-23400566.text_edition: \n Deae Nehalenniae Quartius Reditus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-23400566.translation: To the goddess Nehalennia, Quartius Reditus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-23400566.summary: This votive inscription records Quartius Reditus fulfilling a vow to the goddess Nehalennia.

EDCS-23400567.translation: To the goddess Nehalennia, Volusius Dius and Serotinus willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-23400567.summary: This votive inscription records Volusius Dius and Serotinus fulfilling a vow to the goddess Nehalennia.

EDCS-23400569.translation: To the goddess Nehalennia, Tagamas, son of Tagadius, paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-23400569.summary: This is a votive dedication to the goddess Nehalennia, made by Tagamas, son of Tagadius.

EDCS-23400573.translation: To the goddess Nehalennia, Lucius Optatus paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-23400573.summary: This is a votive dedication to the goddess Nehalennia, made by Lucius Optatus.

EDCS-23400574.summary: This is a fragmentary dedication to the goddess Nehalennia, mentioning someone named Nico.

EDCS-23400575.translation: To the goddess Nehalennia, Gaius Sentius Certus and Gaius Sentius Primitivus, by order of the same goddess, [erected this].
EDCS-23400575.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Nehalennia made by Gaius Sentius Certus and Gaius Sentius Primitivus under divine instruction.

EDCS-23400576.translation: To the goddess Nehalennia, Marcus Cupitius Victor, acting as an assistant, fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly, in accordance with his undertaking.
EDCS-23400576.summary: This is a votive dedication to the goddess Nehalennia by Marcus Cupitius Victor, who acted as an assistant.

EDCS-23400581.translation: To Nehalennia, Sentius Atticus and Tertinius Quartinus fulfilled their vows willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-23400581.summary: This is a votive dedication to Nehalennia made by Sentius Atticus and Tertinius Quartinus.

EDCS-23400586.translation: To the goddess Nehalennia, Gaius Iulius Ianuarius, a merchant from Agrippinensis dealing in salt, willingly [erected this].
EDCS-23400586.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Nehalennia by Gaius Iulius Ianuarius, a salt merchant from Agrippinensis.

EDCS-23400589.text_edition: \n Deae Nehalenniae Marcus Ottinius Frequens sevir Augustalis coloniae Claudiae Augustae Agrippinensium votum solvit libens merito Fusciano II et Silano II consulibus\n
EDCS-23400589.translation: To the goddess Nehalennia, Marcus Ottinius Frequens, a *sevir Augustalis* of the colony of Claudia Augusta Agrippinensium, fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly, in the consulship of Fuscianus II and Silanus II.
EDCS-23400589.summary: This is a votive dedication to the goddess Nehalennia by Marcus Ottinius Frequens, a high-ranking civic priest in Cologne, dated to the consulship of Fuscianus II and Silanus II.

EDCS-23400594.text_edition: \n Deae Nehaleniae Marcus Iustinius Albus libens merito\n
EDCS-23400594.translation: To the goddess Nehalennia, Marcus Iustinius Albus willingly and deservedly [erected this].
EDCS-23400594.summary: This is a votive dedication to the goddess Nehalennia made by Marcus Iustinius Albus.

EDCS-23400595.translation: To the goddess Nehalennia, Mercatorius Amabilis placed [this] out of his vow, willingly, gladly, and deservedly.
EDCS-23400595.summary: This is a votive dedication to the goddess Nehalennia made by Mercatorius Amabilis.

EDCS-23400596.text_edition: \n Deae Nechalenniae sic Lucius Patruitius Saturninus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-23400596.translation: To the goddess Nehalennia, Lucius Patruitius Saturninus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-23400596.summary: This is an ex-voto inscription by Lucius Patruitius Saturninus to the goddess Nehalennia.

EDCS-23400597.translation: To the goddess Nehalennia, Acceptius Bassus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-23400597.summary: This is an ex-voto inscription, likely fragmentary, by Acceptius Bassus to the goddess Nehalennia.

EDCS-23400598.translation: To the goddess Nehalennia, Lucius Tertinius Victor willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-23400598.summary: This is an ex-voto inscription by Lucius Tertinius Victor to the goddess Nehalennia.

EDCS-23400599.text_edition: \n Deae Nehalenniae Publius Arisenius Marius libertus Publi Ariseni Vhi negotiatoris Britanniciani ob merces bene conservatas votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-23400599.translation: To the goddess Nehalennia, Publius Arisenius Marius, freedman of Publius Arisenius Vhi, a merchant from Britain, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow for goods well preserved.
EDCS-23400599.summary: This is an ex-voto inscription by Publius Arisenius Marius, a freedman and merchant, to the goddess Nehalennia for the preservation of his goods.

EDCS-23400600.translation: To the goddess Nehalennia, Exsibillus, [son] of Albinus, for himself and his family, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-23400600.summary: This is an ex-voto inscription by Exsibillus for himself and his family to the goddess Nehalennia.

EDCS-23400601.translation: To the goddess Nehalennia, Quintus Castricius Senecianus, by her command, willingly and deservedly [fulfilled his vow].
EDCS-23400601.summary: This is an ex-voto inscription by Quintus Castricius Senecianus to the goddess Nehalennia, acting under divine inspiration.

EDCS-23400602.translation: To the goddess Nehalennia, the negotiator Septiminius Casali[---] willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-23400602.summary: This is a fragmentary ex-voto inscription by the merchant Septiminius Casali[---] to the goddess Nehalennia.

EDCS-23400603.translation: To the goddess Nehalennia, Tertinius Virilis and Marius Agilis willingly and deservedly fulfilled their vows.
EDCS-23400603.summary: This is a joint ex-voto inscription by Tertinius Virilis and Marius Agilis to the goddess Nehalennia.

EDCS-23400604.translation: To the goddess Nehalennia, Marcus Antonius Felicio willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-23400604.summary: This is an ex-voto inscription by Marcus Antonius Felicio to the goddess Nehalennia.

EDCS-23400605.translation: To the goddess Nehalennia, Vettius Secundus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-23400605.summary: This is an ex-voto inscription by Vettius Secundus to the goddess Nehalennia.

EDCS-23400606.translation: To the goddess Nehalennia, Lucius Candidianus Victor willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-23400606.summary: This is a votive dedication to the goddess Nehalennia by Lucius Candidianus Victor.

EDCS-23400607.translation: To the goddess Nehalennia, Quadra[ti]us Ianuarius willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-23400607.summary: This is a votive dedication to the goddess Nehalennia by Quadra[ti]us Ianuarius.

EDCS-23400614.translation: To the goddess Nehalennia, Sumaronius Vitalis, sesquip[licarius] (a rank in the cavalry) of the ala Noricorum, and Aulus Verinius Secundus willingly and deservedly paid their vow.
EDCS-23400614.summary: This is a joint votive dedication to the goddess Nehalennia by Sumaronius Vitalis and Aulus Verinius Secundus, soldiers of the ala Noricorum.

EDCS-23400616.translation: To the goddess Nehalennia, Sabinus Superis willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-23400616.summary: This is a votive dedication to the goddess Nehalennia by Sabinus Superis.

EDCS-23400619.translation: To Nehalennia, Bosiconius Quartus, captain of the ship of Florus Severus, willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-23400619.summary: This is a votive dedication to the goddess Nehalennia by Bosiconius Quartus, a ship captain.

EDCS-23400625.translation: Freio Palusonis set up this altar to the goddess Nehalennia at his own expense, willingly and deservedly paying his vow.
EDCS-23400625.summary: This is a votive dedication to the goddess Nehalennia by Freio Palusonis, who erected an altar at his own expense.

EDCS-23400626.text_edition: \n Deae Nehaleniae Gimio Ganuentae consistens votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-23400626.translation: To the goddess Nehalennia, Gimio Ganuentae, residing here, willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-23400626.summary: This is a votive dedication to the goddess Nehalennia by Gimio Ganuentae.

EDCS-23400628.translation: To the goddess Nehalennia, [---] Tertinius Primitivus [---].
EDCS-23400628.summary: This is a fragmentary votive dedication to the goddess Nehalennia by Tertinius Primitivus.

EDCS-23400630.translation: To the goddess Nehalennia, Claudius Mar[--].
EDCS-23400630.summary: This is a fragmentary votive dedication to the goddess Nehalennia by Claudius Mar[--].

EDCS-23400631.translation: To the goddess Nehalennia, Caius Crescen[tius --].
EDCS-23400631.summary: This is a fragmentary votive dedication to the goddess Nehalennia by Caius Crescen[tius --].

EDCS-23400632.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Nehalen(n)ia by an individual whose name is partially preserved.

EDCS-23400638.translation: In honor of the Divine House. Memnon fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-23400638.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Memnon in honor of the Imperial house.

EDCS-23400652.translation: To the goddess Nehalen(n)ia, Andanhianius Severus willingly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-23400652.summary: This is a votive inscription to the goddess Nehalen(n)ia by Andanhianius Severus.

EDCS-23400653.translation: Gaius Vitalinius Genialis fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly; he fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-23400653.summary: This inscription records Gaius Vitalinius Genialis fulfilling his vow twice.

EDCS-23400654.translation: Libilus(?), for himself and his dependents, fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-23400654.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Libilus for himself and his family.

EDCS-23400656.translation: [...]lius Fe/[3]nius willingly and deservedly [fulfilled his vow].
EDCS-23400656.summary: This inscription records the partial name of an individual who willingly fulfilled a vow.

EDCS-23400658.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deae Nehalenniae Iucundinius Verinus N\n
EDCS-23400658.translation: In honor of the Divine House, Iucundinius Verinus [dedicated something] to the goddess Nehalen(n)ia.
EDCS-23400658.summary: This is an inscription honoring the imperial family and dedicated to the goddess Nehalen(n)ia by Iucundinius Verinus.

EDCS-23400668.translation: [...]arinus, for himself and his dependents, willingly [fulfilled his vow].
EDCS-23400668.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by an individual whose name is partially preserved.

EDCS-23400670.translation: Victor fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-23400670.summary: This is a votive inscription by Victor.

EDCS-24200276.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deo Iovi Optimo Maximo Nivalis pro salute sua et suorum posuit\n
EDCS-24200276.translation: In honor of the Divine House, Nivalis placed [this] for his own health and that of his dependents, to the god Jupiter Optimus Maximus.
EDCS-24200276.summary: This inscription records Nivalis dedicating something to Jupiter Optimus Maximus in honor of the imperial family and for his own well-being.

EDCS-24200281.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Secundinius Aventinus and Secundinius Securus, the living, made this for their deceased parents and for themselves, so that they might have (it), for their sons Secundinus, Securius, and Lucius Saccio Modestus, and for his son Modestius Macedo.
EDCS-24200281.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Lucius Secundinius Aventinus and Secundinius Securus for their deceased parents and for themselves, while still alive, and for their sons.

EDCS-24200282.translation: To Mars Cnabetius. Gaius Elvonius Caddimarus gladly paid his vow.
EDCS-24200282.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Mars Cnabetius, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE, indicating a soldier dedicating a sword.

EDCS-24200283.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Sacrio Apinosso defuncto et Catiae Carantodiae coniugi viva posuit\n
EDCS-24200283.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Catia Carantodia, still alive, placed this for Sacrius Apinossus, her deceased husband.
EDCS-24200283.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Catia Carantodia for her deceased husband, Sacrius Apinossus.

EDCS-24500422.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Santae, his wife.
EDCS-24500422.summary: This is a funerary epitaph, likely from the 2nd century CE, dedicated to Santae, the wife of Sennius.

EDCS-24500424.translation: Donissia, while alive, placed this for her deceased son Martius.
EDCS-24500424.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Donissia for her deceased son Martius.

EDCS-25200003.translation: Titus's crocodile for roughness and sycosis. Titus's crocodile for roughness and sycosis. Titus's basil for clarity, perfumed with opobalsamum. Titus's basil for clarity, perfumed with opobalsamum.
EDCS-25200003.summary: This is a list of cosmetic or medicinal preparations, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE, attributed to Titus.

EDCS-25200004.translation: Eutyches's plaster for roughness and scars.
EDCS-25200004.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription listing a medicinal preparation, likely for skin conditions, from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-25200005.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Cornelius Maturus.
EDCS-25200005.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE, dedicated to Cornelius Maturus.

EDCS-25200007.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Sexto Vervicio Modestino et Verviciae Modestinae parentes fecerunt\n
EDCS-25200007.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Parents made this for Sextus Vervicius Modestinus and Vervicia Modestina.
EDCS-25200007.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by parents for their children, Sextus Vervicius Modestinus and Vervicia Modestina.

EDCS-25300533.text_edition: \n Deo Invicto Mithrae Tullio Spuri votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-25300533.translation: To the Unconquered God Mithras. Tullius Spuri willingly paid his vow.
EDCS-25300533.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Mithras, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE, indicating Tullius Spuri fulfilled a vow.

EDCS-25601386.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deo Mercurio Securius Severus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-25601386.translation: In honor of the divine house, Securius Severus gladly fulfilled his vow to the god Mercury.
EDCS-25601386.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to the god Mercury made by Securius Severus.

EDCS-25601387.text_edition: \n Deo Mercurio peregrinorum Iulius Iulianus ex voto posuit\n
EDCS-25601387.translation: Julius Julianus set this up in fulfillment of a vow to the god Mercury for the travelers.
EDCS-25601387.summary: This is a votive dedication to Mercury by Julius Julianus, possibly for a group of travelers.

EDCS-25700582.translation: Leodenus, may he live, to the god.
EDCS-25700582.summary: A short inscription, possibly a personal dedication or prayer to a deity.

EDCS-28900007.translation: Cara, to Carantus, may he live.
EDCS-28900007.summary: A dedication or inscription from Cara to Carantus, wishing him life.

EDCS-28900009.translation: Calia sends greetings. Berte, with greetings from the workshop of Mounus(?).
EDCS-28900009.summary: This inscription appears to be a greeting or message related to a workshop, possibly from Calia and mentioning Berte and Mounus.

EDCS-28900015.summary: This inscription names 'Litugeni' and 'Litugenus', possibly referring to people or a place.

EDCS-28900016.summary: This inscription appears to name 'Diamisus', possibly a person or deity.

EDCS-28900017.translation: Atticus made the kanabis for the people of Bonn.
EDCS-28900017.summary: This inscription records the construction of a 'kanabis' (a type of building or structure) by Atticus for the inhabitants of Bonn.

EDCS-28900020.text_edition: \n Apollini et Mercurio Flavius Hiemalis votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-28900020.translation: To Apollo and Mercury, Flavius Hiemalis gladly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-28900020.summary: This inscription is a votive dedication to the gods Apollo and Mercury by Flavius Hiemalis.

EDCS-28900021.text_edition: \n Mercuriom Gratus M puteum cum suis ornamentis[3] Aceratius Primus Grati libertus Catenara cum Pupia libertae II votum solverunt libentes merito\n
EDCS-28900021.translation: Gratus, freedman of M. Aperacius, and his freedwoman Catenara, with Pupia, his freedwoman, gladly and deservedly fulfilled their vow for Mercury concerning a well with all its adornments.
EDCS-28900021.summary: This inscription records a joint votive offering to Mercury by freedmen and freedwomen for the construction of a well.

EDCS-28900022.text_edition: \n Mercurio sacrum Publius Octavius Vitalis votum susceptum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-28900022.translation: Sacred to Mercury. Publius Octavius Vitalis willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-28900022.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Mercury by Publius Octavius Vitalis, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-28900023.translation: To Victory, Attia made (this dedication) for herself, favorably.
EDCS-28900023.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Victoria by Attia, likely a personal votive offering from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-28900024.summary: This is a simple maker's mark or dedication by Facundus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-29600084.translation: Who would doubt that the heavens cannot deny him his excellent merits, and that a servant may hope to be blessed for a long time? Through the chance of death, the Lord has restored his cherished protégé, and mingled him, taken from earth, with the stars. Indeed, his faith and previous reward are recognized. He lived not in death, and you will be able to recognize no fate. He lived 29 years.
EDCS-29600084.summary: This is a funerary epigram for a young man who died at 29, likely from the Late Roman period, emphasizing his merits and heavenly reward.

EDCS-29600085.translation: Here lies Fedemia, who lived 16 years. Her brother Amonius placed this tombstone in peace.
EDCS-29600085.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Fedemia, who died at 16, with the monument erected by her brother, likely from the Late Roman period.

EDCS-29600086.translation: Here lies Flavius [---] from the household [---]. Alardus, soldier, died the 10th day before the Kalends of November.
EDCS-29600086.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription for Flavius, identified as 'from the household,' with a soldier's name and death date, likely from the Late Roman period.

EDCS-29600087.translation: [---] to the Lord. [---] in the name of Christ, who lived [---] years. [---] who, departing life, deserved an eternal [---] life. This crown was erected [---] he is associated in honor [---] the Kalends of May.
EDCS-29600087.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription, likely Christian, mentioning passage to the Lord, Christ, an eternal life, and a date, probably from the Late Roman period.

EDCS-29600089.translation: Here rests in peace Lycontius, the presbyter. His brothers Quiriacus and Leosa placed this monument. He rested on the day before the Kalends of November, on a Wednesday.
EDCS-29600089.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lycontius, a presbyter, erected by his brothers, with a specific date of rest, likely from the Late Roman period.

EDCS-29600090.translation: Here lies in peace Numidius, who lived 7 years. Valerius and Optata, his parents, placed this monument.
EDCS-29600090.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Numidius, who died at 7 years old, with the monument placed by his parents, likely from the Late Roman period.

EDCS-29600091.translation: Here lies Urbica, who lived 1 year and five months. Petamius placed this monument.
EDCS-29600091.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Urbica, who died at the age of 1 year and 5 months, with the monument placed by Petamius, likely from the Late Roman period.

EDCS-29600092.text_edition: \n Hic iacet Ursicinus qui vixit annos L menses IX dies VI fratres dulcissimi Ursinus et Ursus in pace titulum posuerunt\n
EDCS-29600092.translation: Here lies Ursicinus who lived 50 years, 9 months, and 6 days. His dearest brothers Ursinus and Ursus placed the monument.
EDCS-29600092.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Ursicinus, set up by his brothers.

EDCS-29600093.translation: Valentia rests here in peace, who lived 4 years, 9 months, and 5 days. Her father placed the monument.
EDCS-29600093.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Valentia, set up by her father.

EDCS-29600094.translation: Here lies Vector who lived 11 months. His mother Leosa placed the monument in peace.
EDCS-29600094.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Vector, set up by his mother.

EDCS-29600095.translation: Here rests Vitalis who lived 70 years. His son Volusianus placed the monument.
EDCS-29600095.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Vitalis, set up by his son.

EDCS-29600202.translation: Caretae, deceased (?), who lived [3] years, his little son VEIIEC[3] LABACRET[3] CE[1]ITTE[3] [6] [3]EI[3].
EDCS-29600202.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription, likely for a child named Caretae, with damaged lines.

EDCS-30100181.text_edition: \n Hic iacet Ursvixit annum et dies dulcissimae f<e=I>c<e=I>runts Aelia quae vix[it ------ \n
EDCS-30100181.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription for Aelia, with missing age information.

EDCS-30100182.translation: Here lies Ursicinus Anatolicus in Christ, who lived 29 years. who lived 29 years.
EDCS-30100182.summary: This is a bilingual funerary inscription for Ursicinus Anatolicus, indicating his Christian faith and lifespan.

EDCS-30100183.translation: Here lies Azizos Agrippa the Syrian, from the village of Kaprozabadaia, of the territory of Apamea.
EDCS-30100183.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Azizos Agrippa, identifying his origin and ethnicity.

EDCS-30100184.translation: Here lies in peace Concordia, who lived approximately 65 years. Her dearest sons Concordius and Concordialis placed the monument. He lived approximately 47 years.
EDCS-30100184.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Concordia, set up by her sons, also including details about the lifespan of another individual.

EDCS-30100185.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely naming Marcellianus.

EDCS-30100186.translation: Artemius, may you live in Christ.
EDCS-30100186.summary: This inscription is a Christian epitaph wishing life in Christ to Artemius.

EDCS-30100189.translation: Verna, may you live in Christ.
EDCS-30100189.summary: This is a Christian epitaph wishing life in Christ to Verna.

EDCS-30100199.translation: May you live... may you live.
EDCS-30100199.summary: This fragmentary inscription contains repeated wishes for life.

EDCS-30100200.translation: May you live in God... May you live in God, Maxima, may you live in God forever, Marti, may you live in God forever.
EDCS-30100200.summary: This inscription is a series of Christian wishes for eternal life in God, addressed to multiple individuals including Maxima and Marti.

EDCS-30100205.translation: Lucius Eustoli, may you live in Christ.
EDCS-30100205.summary: This is a Christian epitaph wishing life in Christ to Lucius Eustoli.

EDCS-30100206.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription that begins with the name Theodosius.

EDCS-30100213.translation: Here rests Castorius, who lived for more or less 60 years.
EDCS-30100213.summary: This is a Christian epitaph recording the death and age of Castorius.

EDCS-30100433.translation: Here lies Amanda, an infant, who lived for one year, six months, and nine days.
EDCS-30100433.summary: This is a Roman epitaph for an infant named Amanda, detailing her lifespan.

EDCS-30100436.translation: How well divine power unites in harmony those who are in concord, the members of the priesthood, whom this place adorns for two. Eucharius speaks, and Valerius together, rejoicing to place a seat for the living members; Cyrillus places this altar for these holy brothers, the holy architect adorns the lodging of the body.
EDCS-30100436.summary: This is a complex epitaph or dedication, likely for two priests named Eucharius and Valerius, by someone named Cyrillus, possibly commemorating the building or dedication of a religious space.

EDCS-30100437.translation: Leosus, who rested here in peace, lived for one year and VI months.
EDCS-30100437.summary: This inscription records the death of Leosus, likely a Christian burial marker.

EDCS-30100438.translation: Meraudis, who rested here in peace, lived for one year and XI months. Her dearest father set up this monument.
EDCS-30100438.summary: This inscription records the death of Meraudis and is a funerary monument erected by her father.

EDCS-30100444.translation: Beata, who lived XL years, set up this monument in peace.
EDCS-30100444.summary: This inscription records the death of Beata, who lived 40 years, and likely served as a funerary marker.

EDCS-30100445.translation: Tertius, 18 years old, set up [this monument].
EDCS-30100445.summary: This inscription records the death of Tertius, aged 18, and was likely a funerary monument.

EDCS-30100451.translation: Adeudatus, who lived for one year and seven months, rests here. Eustasius and Calopae set up this monument in peace.
EDCS-30100451.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Adeudatus, set up by Eustasius and Calopae.

EDCS-30100452.translation: Catia, who lived for XXXVIII years, one month, and XV days, rests here in peace. Rusticius set up this monument for his dearest wife.
EDCS-30100452.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Catia, erected by her husband Rusticius.

EDCS-30100454.translation: Here rests in peace Ger[---], who lived for one year and VIII months. Father Covoldus and mother Calopes(?) set up this monument.
EDCS-30100454.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Ger[---] and was erected by his parents.

EDCS-30100455.translation: Drula made [this] for her most beloved wife Mamerina, and for their daughter Sensuta, who lived LX years, resting well.
EDCS-30100455.summary: This funerary inscription records Drula's dedication to her wife Mamerina and daughter Sensuta.

EDCS-30100457.translation: [---] from a well-deserved [status] in charity to Primiano Eu[---].
EDCS-30100457.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely records a charitable donation or dedication.

EDCS-30100459.translation: Here rest in peace the elder Valentius, who lived approximately IIII years, and the younger Stefanus, [who lived...].
EDCS-30100459.summary: This inscription records the death of two individuals, Valentius and Stefanus, likely in infancy.

EDCS-30100460.translation: To Valeria, my most sweet daughter, who rests here in peace, who lived [3] years [and] [3] days.
EDCS-30100460.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young daughter named Valeria, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-30100465.translation: Victurinus placed this monument for one who lived 30 years.
EDCS-30100465.summary: A funerary epitaph indicating the deceased lived to be about 30 years old, with the monument erected by the husband Victurinus.

EDCS-30100468.translation: I am not able to restore this text fully, but it appears to be a funerary inscription lamenting a death and the passage of time, possibly mentioning Leodomundus as the dedicator.
EDCS-30100468.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription that laments a death and mentions a relative named Leodomundus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-30100478.translation: Here rests in peace Antonia, an infant who lived 2 years and 1 month; her mother [...] placed the monument.
EDCS-30100478.summary: A funerary epitaph for an infant named Antonia, who died at the age of 2 years and 1 month, erected by her mother.

EDCS-30100999.summary: A very short inscription repeating the name Nocturnus, possibly a marker or a personal reminder.

EDCS-30101006.summary: An inscription possibly commemorating Roman emperors Constantine I, Crispus, and Constantine II.

EDCS-30101010.summary: A short inscription possibly dedicating something to Titus by Catullinus.

EDCS-30101011.translation: To the departed spirits of Lucius Maternus Bellator.
EDCS-30101011.summary: A funerary dedication to the departed spirit of Lucius Maternus Bellator.

EDCS-30101012.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Marci Ianini Buccati et Catulliniae Divixtae coniugis filius\n
EDCS-30101012.translation: To the departed spirits of Marcus Ianinius Buccatus and his wife Catullinia Divixta, from their son.
EDCS-30101012.summary: A funerary dedication to Marcus Ianinius Buccatus and his wife Catullinia Divixta, erected by their son.

EDCS-30101013.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Marco Micioni Mattosso et coniugi Carantiae Decmani filiae\n
EDCS-30101013.translation: To the departed spirits of Marcus Micionius Mattosus and his wife Carantia, daughter of Decmanus.
EDCS-30101013.summary: A funerary dedication to Marcus Micionius Mattosus and his wife Carantia, daughter of Decmanus.

EDCS-30101014.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Tituro militi legionis VI\n
EDCS-30101014.translation: To the Divine Shades. To Titurus, a soldier of the Sixth Legion.
EDCS-30101014.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Titurus, a soldier of the Sixth Legion, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-30200799.translation: Here lies Eusebia, being in peace, a priestess(?) from the village of Addana, having lived a short life of 15 years, in the consulship of Honorius the 8th and Constantius the 1st, on the 12th day of Panemus, on a Sunday(?), in peace.
EDCS-30200799.summary: This is a Greek funerary epitaph from a later Roman or early Byzantine period, commemorating Eusebia, who died young and is identified with a specific village and consular dating.

EDCS-30200800.translation: Here lies Cassianus, son of Abedsimius, from the village of Addana, having lived a short life of 22 years.
EDCS-30200800.summary: This is a Greek funerary epitaph, likely from the late Roman or early Byzantine period, for Cassianus from the village of Addana who died young.

EDCS-30301494.translation: He who, walking, calmed the bitter waves of the sea, who grants life, who was able to loosen the fetters of death, will make my brother return to the world above after the darkness, after the sad lights of the sun, and will make Ericus rise again after the ashes, because I believe, O Christ the Redeemer, spare your faithful Ericus, who after his body left many tears behind him.
EDCS-30301494.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription for Ericus, emphasizing his resurrection and the compassion of Christ, likely from the late Roman or early Byzantine period.

EDCS-30301498.translation: Here lies Annius Cato, who lived 31 years and 4 months. His mother Annia placed this monument.
EDCS-30301498.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Annius Cato, recording his age and mentioning his mother as the dedicator, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-30301499.translation: Here lies Cornelia, who lived 22 years. Her mother Salvia and father Severus placed this monument.
EDCS-30301499.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Cornelia, recording her age and mentioning both her parents as the dedicator, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-30301500.translation: Here lies Aelia Herrenia, who lived more or less 21 years. Her mother Paula makes this monument.
EDCS-30301500.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aelia Herrenia, recording her approximate age and mentioning her mother as the dedicator, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-30301501.translation: Iulia for herself and for her husband, in peace.
EDCS-30301501.summary: This is a funerary epitaph intended for Iulia and her husband, indicating a late Roman or early Christian context with the phrase 'in pace'.

EDCS-30301502.translation: Licinius, who lived 24 years, rests here in peace.
EDCS-30301502.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Licinius, recording his age and indicating a Christian context with 'in pace', likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-30301503.translation: Here lies Magníola, who lived 11 years. Her mother Maura placed this monument.
EDCS-30301503.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Magníola, recording her young age and mentioning her mother as the dedicator, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-30301504.summary: This is a funerary inscription with a wish for the deceased, Servatus, to be in peace, likely from the early imperial period.

EDCS-30301505.translation: Little Claudia, who lived 14 years and 20 days, in peace. Athenimius raised this monument.
EDCS-30301505.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young girl named Claudia, recording her age at death and mentioning the person who erected the monument, Athenimius, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-31600184.translation: To Nicomachus, son of Domitius Tullus.
EDCS-31600184.summary: This is a funerary dedication likely for Nicomachus, identifying his father as Domitius Tullus, probably from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-31700033.summary: This inscription records the donation of a sandpit by a person named Iovinus, possibly of the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-31800072.translation: Quintus Valerius Sextus's perfumed oil for dark spots // Gaius Vitalis Amandio's green cosmetic for...
EDCS-31800072.summary: This inscription lists medicinal or cosmetic preparations, specifying their intended use, likely from a Roman period pharmacy or perfumery.

EDCS-31800074.translation: Lucius Antonius Epictetus's preparation for ear conditions // Lucius Antonius Epictetus's preparation for scars // Lucius Antonius Epictetus's preparation for brightness // Lucius Antonius Epictetus's preparation for clarity.
EDCS-31800074.summary: This inscription lists several pharmaceutical or cosmetic preparations made by Lucius Antonius Epictetus, indicating their medicinal or cosmetic purposes, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-32300926.translation: Sextus Po(.) Calenus's preparation for old scars // Sextus Po(.) Calenus's perfumed oil, anointed, for scars // Sextus Po(.) Calenus's preparation for old scars // Sextus Po(.) Calenus's preparation for soothing inflamed eyes.
EDCS-32300926.summary: This inscription lists several pharmaceutical or cosmetic preparations attributed to Sextus Po(.) Calenus, detailing their use for various ailments, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-32300931.summary: This is a brief inscription indicating that someone named Rusticus(?) was the maker of the object on which it is inscribed, possibly from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-32300934.summary: This inscription appears to list two personal names, Baudulfus and Haricura, perhaps as owners or makers of an object, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-32300959.summary: This inscription simply records the name Marcus Probius Burrus, likely identifying the owner or commissioner of an object or monument from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-32300960.summary: This inscription lists four personal names, likely belonging to individuals associated with a tomb or a religious group.

EDCS-32300962.summary: This is a titulary inscription for Emperor Constantine I, identifying him with his imperial titles.

EDCS-32300963.summary: This is a titulary inscription for Caesar Crispus, son of Constantine I.

EDCS-32300965.summary: This is a personal inscription, a wish for a long life for Lucilianus, possibly on a tomb.
